# Bootstrap 6 Tables

> Documentation and examples for opt-in styling of tables (given their prevalent use in JavaScript plugins) with Bootstrap.

<tr>
      <th scope="col">#</th>
      <th scope="col">First</th>
      <th scope="col">Last</th>
      <th scope="col">Handle</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">1</th>
      <td>Mark</td>
      <td>Otto</td>
      <td>@mdo</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">2</th>
      <td>Jacob</td>
      <td>Thornton</td>
      <td>@fat</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">3</th>
      <td colspan="2">Larry the Bird</td>
      <td>@twitter</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>`

## Overview

Due to the widespread use of `<table>` elements across third-party widgets like calendars and date pickers, CoreUI for Bootstrap's tables are **opt-in**. Add the base class `.table` to any `<table>`, then extend with our optional modifier classes or custom styles. All table styles are not inherited in Bootstrap, meaning any nested tables can be styled independent from the parent.

Using the most basic table markup, here's how `.table`-based tables look in CoreUI.

## Theme variants

Use contextual classes to color tables, table rows or individual cells.

```html
<table class="table-primary">...</table>
<table class="table-secondary">...</table>
<table class="table-success">...</table>
<table class="table-danger">...</table>
<table class="table-warning">...</table>
<table class="table-info">...</table>
```

```html
<tr class="table-primary">...</tr>
<tr class="table-secondary">...</tr>
<tr class="table-success">...</tr>
<tr class="table-danger">...</tr>
<tr class="table-warning">...</tr>
<tr class="table-info">...</tr>
```

```html
<tr>
  <td class="table-primary">...</td>
  <td class="table-secondary">...</td>
  <td class="table-success">...</td>
  <td class="table-danger">...</td>
  <td class="table-warning">...</td>
  <td class="table-info">...</td>
</tr>
```

> ##### Conveying meaning to assistive technologies
> 
> Relying on color to convey meaning creates a visual cue that assistive technologies, like screen readers, cannot perceive. It's essential that any information represented by color is either apparent from the content itself (e.g., the visible text) or supplemented by alternative methods, such as extra text using the `.visually-hidden` class.

### Hoverable rows

These hoverable rows can also be combined with the striped rows variant:

```html
<table class="table">

  </thead>

      ...

      <td>@twitter</td>
    </tr>

```

```html

  <thead>

  </thead>

    </tr>
    <tr>
      ...
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">3</th>

      <td>@twitter</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## How do the variants and accented tables work?

For the accented tables ([striped rows](#striped-rows), [striped columns](#striped-columns), [hoverable rows](#hoverable-rows), and [active tables](#active-tables)), we used some techniques to make these effects work for all our [table variants](#variants):

- We start by setting the background of a table cell with the `--cui-table-bg` custom property. All table variants then set that custom property to colorize the table cells. This way, we don't get into trouble if semi-transparent colors are used as table backgrounds.
- Then we add a gradient on the table cells with `background-image: linear-gradient(var(--cui-table-accent-bg), var(--cui-table-accent-bg));` to layer on top of any specified `background-color`. Since `--cui-table-accent-bg` is transparent by default, we have an invisible transparent linear gradient by default.
- When either `.table-striped`, `.table-hover` or `.table-active` classes are added, the `--cui-table-accent-bg` is set to a semitransparent color to colorize the background.
- For each table variant, we generate a `--cui-table-accent-bg` color with the highest contrast depending on that color. For example, the accent color for `.table-primary` is darker while `.table-inverse` has a lighter accent color.
- Text and border colors are generated the same way, and their colors are inherited by default.

Behind the scenes it looks like this:

```scss
// The variant sets the theme tokens and lets the base .table rules read them,
// the way the button variants do. Nothing is computed at build time, so a theme
// colour added by hand gets a table variant without compiling Sass.
@mixin table-variant($state) {
  .table-#{$state} {
    @include theme-tokens($state);

    --cui-table-color: var(--cui-theme-fg-emphasis);
    --cui-table-bg: var(--cui-theme-bg-subtle);
    --cui-table-border-color: var(--cui-theme-border);

    color: var(--cui-table-color);
    border-color: var(--cui-table-border-color);
  }
}
```

## Table borders

### Bordered tables

Add `.table-bordered` for borders on all sides of the table and cells.

[Border color utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/border-color/) can be added to change colors:

### Tables without borders

Add `.table-borderless` for a table without borders.

## Card-like tables

Need a bordered, rounded table without nesting it in a [card](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/card/)? Wrap the table and clip the corners.

### With utilities

Compose [border](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/border/), [border radius](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/border-radius/), and [overflow](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/overflow/) utilities. Drop the table's bottom margin with `.mb-0`.

```html
<div class="border rounded overflow-hidden">n  <table class="table table-striped mb-0">n    ...n  </table>n</div>
```

### With `.table-card`

Use `.table-card` for the card look in one class. It draws the default border and corner radius of a [card](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/card/), and a `.theme-*` class on it or on an ancestor colours the frame the way it colours a card. It clips the cells, drops the table's bottom margin, and removes the borders that would stack on the frame: the last row's bottom border and the outer borders of a `.table-bordered` table. A caption at the bottom keeps the line above it.

```html
<div class="table-card">n  <table class="table table-hover">n    ...n  </table>n</div>
```

Put it on the [responsive wrapper](#responsive-tables) itself when the table can be wider than its container:

```html
<div class="table-responsive table-card">n  <table class="table table-striped">n    ...n  </table>n</div>
```

> ##### Clipping
> 
> `.table-card` clips everything at its rounded edge: a dropdown menu opened from a cell, the focus ring of a control in an edge cell, and columns wider than the frame. Append menus outside the table with the dropdown's [`container` option](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/dropdown/#options), and add `.table-responsive` to the wrapper when the table can be wider than it.

## Small tables

Add `.table-sm` to make any `.table` more compact by cutting all cell `padding` in half.

## Table group dividers

Add a thicker border, darker between table groups—`<thead>`, `<tbody>`, and `<tfoot>`—with `.table-group-divider`. Customize the color by changing the `border-top-color` (which we don't currently provide a utility class for at this time).

```html
<table class="table">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">#</th>
      <th scope="col">First</th>
      <th scope="col">Last</th>
      <th scope="col">Handle</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody class="table-group-divider">
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">1</th>
      <td>Mark</td>
      <td>Otto</td>
      <td>@mdo</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">2</th>
      <td>Jacob</td>
      <td>Thornton</td>
      <td>@fat</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">3</th>
      <td colspan="2">Larry the Bird</td>
      <td>@twitter</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## Vertical alignment

Table cells of `<thead>` are always vertical aligned to the bottom. Table cells in `<tbody>` inherit their alignment from `<table>` and are aligned to the top by default. Use the [vertical align](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/vertical-align/) classes to re-align where needed.

```html
<div class="table-responsive">
  <table class="table align-middle">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        ...
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        ...
      </tr>
      <tr class="align-bottom">
        ...
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>...</td>
        <td>...</td>
        <td class="align-top">This cell is aligned to the top.</td>
        <td>...</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

## Nesting

Border styles, active styles, and table variants are not inherited by nested tables.

```html
<table class="table table-striped">
  <thead>
    ...
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ...
    <tr>
      <td colspan="4">
        <table class="table mb-0">
          ...
        </table>
      </td>
    </tr>
    ...
  </tbody>
</table>
```

## How nesting works

To prevent _any_ styles from leaking to nested tables, we use the child combinator (`>`) selector in our CSS. Since we need to target all the `td`s and `th`s in the `thead`, `tbody`, and `tfoot`, our selector would look pretty long without it. As such, we use the rather odd looking `.table > :not(caption) > * > *` selector to target all `td`s and `th`s of the `.table`, but none of any potential nested tables.

Note that if you add `<tr>`s as direct children of a table, those `<tr>` will be wrapped in a `<tbody>` by default, thus making our selectors work as intended.

## Anatomy

### Table head

Similar to tables and dark tables, use the modifier classes `.table-secondary` or `.table-inverse` to make `<thead>`s appear light or dark gray.

```html
<table class="table">
  <thead class="table-secondary">
    ...
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ...
  </tbody>
</table>
```

```html
<table class="table">
  <thead class="table-inverse">

  </thead>
  <tbody>
    ...
  </tbody>
</table>
```

```html
  <tbody>

  </tbody>

```

### Captions

A `<caption>` functions like a heading for a table. It helps users with screen readers to find a table and understand what it's about and decide if they want to read it.

```html
<table class="table table-sm">

```

You can also put the `<caption>` on the top of the table with `.caption-top`.

```html
<table class="table caption-top">
```

## Responsive tables

Responsive tables allow tables to be scrolled horizontally with ease. Make any table responsive across all viewports by wrapping a `.table` with `.table-responsive`. Or, pick a maximum breakpoint with which to have a responsive table up to by using `.table-responsive{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}`.

Every `.table-responsive*` is also a [query container](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/container-queries/), which is what [stacked tables](#stacked-tables) below query to decide when to break rows into blocks.

> ##### Vertical clipping/truncation
> 
> Responsive tables make use of `overflow-y: hidden`, which clips off any content that goes beyond the bottom or top edges of the table. In particular, this can clip off dropdown menus and other third-party widgets.

### Always responsive

Across every breakpoint, use `.table-responsive` for horizontally scrolling tables.

```html
<div class="table-responsive">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>
```

### Breakpoint specific

Use `.table-responsive{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}` as needed to create responsive tables up to a particular breakpoint. From that breakpoint and up, the table will behave normally and not scroll horizontally.

**These tables may appear broken until their responsive styles apply at specific viewport widths.**

{getData('breakpoints').filter((b) => b.abbr).map((b) => (
  
))}

```html
<div class="table-responsive-sm">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>

<div class="table-responsive-md">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>

<div class="table-responsive-lg">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>

<div class="table-responsive-xl">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>

<div class="table-responsive-2xl">
  <table class="table">
    ...
  </table>
</div>
```

## Stacked tables

A table that scrolls sideways is still a table; on a narrow screen it is often easier to read one record at a time. Add `.table-stacked{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}` next to `.table` to turn each row into a block below that breakpoint — the header is hidden from sight (it stays in the accessibility tree) and every cell carries its own label.

Two things are required: a `.table-responsive*` ancestor, because that is the query container the class measures, and a `data-cell` attribute on every `<td>` after the first, which supplies the label the hidden header would have given. The first cell is treated as the record's title and needs no label.

```html
<div class="table-responsive">
  <table class="table table-stacked-md">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col">Name</th>
        <th scope="col">Role</th>
        <th scope="col">Email</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>Mark Otto</td>
        <td data-cell="Role">Maintainer</td>
        <td data-cell="Email">mark@example.com</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

> Because the breakpoint is read from the `.table-responsive*` wrapper rather than the window, a stacked table inside a narrow column stacks there while the same markup in the main content area stays a table.

## Customizing

### CSS variables

```scss
$table-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-table-cell-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-table-cell-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-table-cell-vertical-align: top,
    --cui-table-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-table-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-table-accent-bg: transparent,
    --cui-table-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-table-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-table-group-separator-color: currentcolor,
    --cui-table-striped-color: var(--cui-table-color),
    --cui-table-striped-bg-factor: 5%,
    --cui-table-striped-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-table-color) var(--cui-table-striped-bg-factor), transparent),
    --cui-table-active-color: var(--cui-table-color),
    --cui-table-active-bg-factor: 10%,
    --cui-table-active-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-table-color) var(--cui-table-active-bg-factor), transparent),
    --cui-table-hover-color: var(--cui-table-color),
    --cui-table-hover-bg-factor: 7.5%,
    --cui-table-hover-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-table-color) var(--cui-table-hover-bg-factor), transparent),
  ),
  $table-tokens
);
```

Every value the table draws with is on the table element, so a one-off table is a style attribute away:

```html
<table class="table" style="--cui-table-cell-padding-y: 1rem; --cui-table-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base);">
  ...
</table>
```

The striped, active and hover backgrounds are mixed from `--cui-table-color`, so a variant that changes the text color carries them along. To make the zebra stripes stronger or fainter without touching the color, change the factor:

```html
<table class="table table-striped" style="--cui-table-striped-bg-factor: 12%;">
  ...
</table>
```

### Sass variables

These two pick which rows and which columns are striped. They are written into a
`:nth-of-type()` and a `:nth-child()` selector, and a selector cannot read a
custom property, so unlike the rest of the table's customization these stay Sass
and have no CSS variable counterpart.

```scss
$table-striped-order:         odd !default;
$table-striped-columns-order: even !default;
```

### Sass loops

```scss
// Which theme colours get a .table-* variant. The values come from the theme
// tokens now, so this is a list of names rather than a map of shifted colours.
$table-variants: map.keys($theme-colors) !default;
```

# Bootstrap 6 Figures

> Documentation and examples for displaying related images and text with the figure component in Bootstrap.

Anytime you need to display a piece of content—like an image with an optional caption, consider using a `<figure>`. For images without a caption, see [Images](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/content/images/).

## Basic example

Use the included `.figure`, `.figure-img` and `.figure-caption` classes to provide some baseline styles for the HTML5 `<figure>` and `<figcaption>` elements. `.figure` is an inline flex column, so it shrinks to the width of the image, the caption lines up with it, and `--cui-figure-gap` spaces the two apart. Images in figures have no explicit size, so be sure to add the `.img-fluid` class to your `<img />` to make it responsive.

```html
<figure class="figure">
  <svg class="docs-placeholder-img figure-img img-fluid rounded" width="400" height="300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title></title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em"></text></svg>
  <figcaption class="figure-caption">A caption for the above image.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## Aligning the caption

Aligning the figure's caption is easy with our [text utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/text-alignment/). Because the figure is only as wide as its image, the caption aligns against the image rather than the page.

```html
<figure class="figure">
  <svg class="docs-placeholder-img figure-img img-fluid rounded" width="400" height="300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title></title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em"></text></svg>
  <figcaption class="figure-caption text-end">A caption for the above image.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Each part declares what it reads: `.figure` the gap between image and caption, `.figure-caption` its own size and colour. That is why a caption works the same inside a `.figure` or on its own:

```scss
$figure-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-figure-gap: var(--cui-spacer-3),
  ),
  $figure-tokens
);

$figure-caption-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-figure-caption-font-size: var(--cui-small-font-size),
    --cui-figure-caption-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
  ),
  $figure-caption-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Forms

> Examples and usage guidelines for form control styles, layout options, and custom components for creating a wide variety of forms.

## Overview

CoreUI for Bootstrap's form controls expand on [our Rebooted form styles](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/content/reboot/#forms) with classes. Use these classes to opt into their customized displays for a more consistent rendering across browsers and devices.

Be sure to use an appropriate `type` attribute on all inputs (e.g., `email` for email address or `number` for numerical information) to take advantage of newer input controls like email verification, number selection, and more.

Here's a quick example to demonstrate CoreUI for Bootstrap's form styles. Keep reading for documentation on required classes, form layout, and more.

```html
<form>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <label for="exampleInputEmail1" class="form-label">Email address</label>
    <input type="email" class="form-control" id="exampleInputEmail1" aria-describedby="emailHelp">
    <div id="emailHelp" class="form-text">We'll never share your email with anyone else.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <label for="exampleInputPassword1" class="form-label">Password</label>
    <input type="password" class="form-control" id="exampleInputPassword1">
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4 form-field">
    <input type="checkbox" class="check" id="exampleCheck1">
    <label for="exampleCheck1">Check me out</label>
  </div>
  <button type="submit" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Submit</button>
</form>
```

## Form text

Block-level or inline-level form text can be created using `.form-text`.

> ##### Associating form text with form controls
> 
> Form text should be explicitly associated with the form control it relates to using the `aria-describedby` attribute. This will ensure that assistive technologies—such as screen readers—will announce this form text when the user focuses or enters the control.

Form text below inputs can be styled with `.form-text`. If a block-level element will be used, a top margin is added for easy spacing from the inputs above.

```html
<label for="inputPassword5" class="form-label">Password</label>
<input type="password" id="inputPassword5" class="form-control" aria-describedby="passwordHelpBlock">
<div id="passwordHelpBlock" class="form-text">
  Your password must be 8-20 characters long, contain letters and numbers, and must not contain spaces, special characters, or emoji.
</div>
```

Inline text can use any typical inline HTML element (be it a `<span>`, `<small>`, or something else) with nothing more than the `.form-text` class.

```html
<div class="row g-4 align-items-center">
  <div class="col-auto">
    <label for="inputPassword6" class="col-form-label">Password</label>
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <input type="password" id="inputPassword6" class="form-control" aria-describedby="passwordHelpInline">
  </div>
  <div class="col-auto">
    <span id="passwordHelpInline" class="form-text">
      Must be 8-20 characters long.
    </span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Disabled forms

Add the `disabled` boolean attribute on an input to prevent user interactions and make it appear lighter.

```html
<input class="form-control" id="disabledInput" type="text" placeholder="Disabled input here..." disabled>
```

Add the `disabled` attribute to a `<fieldset>` to disable all the controls within. Browsers treat all native form controls (`<input />`, `<select>`, and `<button>` elements) inside a `<fieldset disabled>` as disabled, preventing both keyboard and mouse interactions on them.

However, if your form also includes custom button-like elements such as `<a class="btn btn-*">...</a>`, these will only be given a style of `pointer-events: none`, meaning they are still focusable and operable using the keyboard. In this case, you must manually modify these controls by adding `tabindex="-1"` to prevent them from receiving focus and `aria-disabled="disabled"` to signal their state to assistive technologies.

```html
<form>
  <fieldset disabled>
    <legend>Disabled fieldset example</legend>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <label for="disabledTextInput" class="form-label">Disabled input</label>
      <input type="text" id="disabledTextInput" class="form-control" placeholder="Disabled input">
    </div>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <label for="disabledSelect" class="form-label">Disabled select menu</label>
      <select id="disabledSelect" class="form-control">
        <option>Disabled select</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="mb-4">
      <div class="form-field">
        <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="disabledFieldsetCheck" disabled>
        <label for="disabledFieldsetCheck">
          Can't check this
        </label>
      </div>
    </div>
    <button type="submit" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Submit</button>
  </fieldset>
</form>
```

## Accessibility

Ensure that all form controls have an appropriate accessible name so that their purpose can be conveyed to users of assistive technologies. The simplest way to achieve this is to use a `<label>` element, or—in the case of buttons—to include sufficiently descriptive text as part of the `<button>...</button>` content.

For situations where it's not possible to include a visible `<label>` or appropriate text content, there are alternative ways of still providing an accessible name, such as:

- `<label>` elements hidden using the `.visually-hidden` class
- Pointing to an existing element that can act as a label using `aria-labelledby`
- Providing a `title` attribute
- Explicitly setting the accessible name on an element using `aria-label`

If none of these are present, assistive technologies may resort to using the `placeholder` attribute as a fallback for the accessible name on `<input />` and `<textarea>` elements. The examples in this section provide a few suggested, case-specific approaches.

While using visually hidden content (`.visually-hidden`, `aria-label`, and even `placeholder` content, which disappears once a form field has content) will benefit assistive technology users, a lack of visible label text may still be problematic for certain users. Some form of visible label is generally the best approach, both for accessibility and usability.

## Customizing

Many form values are set once on `:root` as `--cui-btn-input-*` tokens and re-used by every form component. Each field points its own `--cui-control-*` tokens at them and declares those on itself, so one field is restyled through its `--cui-control-*` tokens and every field at once through `--cui-btn-input-*`. The checkbox, radio and switch share a few `--cui-control-*` tokens on `:root` as well.

### CSS variables

Buttons and form controls share the size and type of one frame, declared once on `:root`: padding, minimum height, font size, weight and line height, border width and radius, and the transition duration and timing. Retuning those there moves buttons and fields together. The color tokens (`-fg`, `-bg`, `-border-color`, `-box-shadow` and `-focus-*`) belong to the fields; a button takes its colors from its variant. A component that needs its own frame overrides the token on itself.


# Bootstrap 6 Autocomplete

> Create intelligent, responsive input fields using the Bootstrap Autocomplete plugin. This component enhances user input with dynamic dropdown suggestions, flexible data providers, and callback support.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

The **Bootstrap Autocomplete Dropdown** component is a powerful autocomplete dropdown plugin that enhances form control usability by suggesting completions as the user types. Whether you're integrating with local JavaScript arrays or fetching live server responses via AJAX, this plugin enables rich, dynamic user interactions.

## Basic example

A straightforward demonstration of how to implement a basic Bootstrap Autocomplete input field, highlighting essential attributes and configurations.

```html
<div
  data-coreui-autocomplete
  data-coreui-cleaner="true"
  data-coreui-highlight-options-on-search="true"
  data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js"
  data-coreui-picker-icon="true"
  data-coreui-placeholder="Search technologies..."
  data-coreui-search-no-results-label="No results found"
  data-coreui-show-hints="true"
  data-coreui-value="React.js"
></div>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="autocompleteField" class="form-label">Framework</label>
  <div
    data-coreui-autocomplete
    data-coreui-id="autocompleteField"
    data-coreui-name="framework"
    data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js"
    data-coreui-placeholder="Search frameworks..."
  ></div>
  <div class="form-text">Start typing to filter the list.</div>
</div>
```

Inside a `<form>`, <kbd>Enter</kbd> with the list closed submits the form. A form reset brings the autocomplete back to the `value` it was created with, or to the first option marked `selected`, or to an empty field, and fires `change.coreui.autocomplete` when that differs from what the field held, typed text included. A reset that a listener cancels changes nothing.

## Data source

Learn how to populate the autocomplete component with data from various sources, including arrays and objects, for dynamic content integration.

### Array data

To dynamically populate an autocomplete input with suggestions from an array, use JavaScript to configure the component with predefined options.

```html
<div id="myAutoComplete"></div>
```

We use the following JavaScript to set up our autocomplete:

```js
const myAutoComplete = document.getElementById('myAutoComplete')

new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutoComplete, {
  name: 'autocomplete',
  options: [
    'Angular',
    'Bootstrap',
    {
      label: 'React.js',
      disabled: true
    },
    'Vue.js',
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: ['Django', 'Laravel', 'Node.js']
    }
  ],
  value: 'Laravel'
})
```

### Object data with groups

You can organize suggestions into groups using optgroups for better categorization and user experience.

```html
<div id="myAutoCompleteGrouped"></div>
```

```js
const myAutoCompleteGrouped = document.getElementById('myAutoCompleteGrouped')

new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutoCompleteGrouped, {
  name: 'autocomplete-grouped',
  options: [
    'Angular',
    {
      label: 'Bootstrap',
      selected: true
    },
    {
      label: 'React.js',
      disabled: true
    },
    'Vue.js',
    {
      label: 'backend',
      options: ['Django', 'Laravel', 'Node.js']
    }
  ]
})
```

### Options with values

You can use values in your options array. This is particularly useful when working with database IDs, product codes, or any numeric identifiers. Note that the component internally converts number values to strings for consistency and DOM compatibility.

```html
<div id="myAutoCompleteValues"></div>
```

```js
const myAutoCompleteValues = document.getElementById('myAutoCompleteValues')

new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutoCompleteValues, {
  cleaner: true,
  name: 'autocomplete-option-values',
  options: [
    { label: 'Product A', value: 1 },
    { label: 'Product B', value: 2 },
    { label: 'Product C', value: 3.5 },
    { label: 'Product D', value: 42 },
    {
      label: 'Categories',
      options: [
        { label: 'Electronics', value: 100 },
        { label: 'Books', value: 200 },
        { label: 'Clothing', value: 300 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  pickerIcon: true,
  placeholder: 'Select product by ID...',
  value: 100
})

// Log the selected value to demonstrate that numbers are converted to strings
myAutoCompleteValues.addEventListener('change.coreui.autocomplete', event => {
  console.log('Selected value:', event.value.value)

  console.log('Selected label:', event.value.label)
})
```

> **Important:** While you can pass number values in your options, the component internally converts all values to strings using `String(value)`. When handling selection events, remember that `event.value.value` will always be a string representation of your original number.
> 
> For example:
> - Input: `{ label: 'Product A', value: 42 }`
> - Internal storage: `{ label: 'Product A', value: '42' }`
> - Event output: `event.value.value === '42'` (string)

### External data

You can configure CoreUI's AutoComplete component to fetch and display options dynamically from an external API. This is useful when you need to autocomplete data that changes frequently or is too large to preload. 

This example shows how to connect the AutoComplete to a remote API to search users by first name.

```html
<div id="myAutoCompleteExternalData"></div>
```

To fetch data from an external source, you must set the search option to `'external'`.
This disables internal filtering and allows you to provide custom data (e.g., from an API) based on user input.

## Search functionality

The field filters the options as the user types.

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-placeholder="Search technologies..."></div>
```

### Where typing goes

Typing reaches the field from anywhere in the component — the picker button, the clear button, the options panel — so a keystroke never depends on where the focus happens to be. The space bar and keyboard shortcuts stay with whatever has the focus.

Add `data-coreui-global-search="false"` to keep typing local: a keystroke then counts only while the field has the focus.

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-global-search="false" data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-picker-icon="true" data-coreui-placeholder="Typing stays local..."></div>
```

### External search

Use external search mode to fetch data dynamically from a server or API. This disables internal filtering and delegates the search logic entirely to your application via JavaScript:

```html
<div id="myAutoCompleteExternalDataExample"></div>
```

```js
const autocomplete = new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutoCompleteExternalDataExample, {
  search: 'external', // Required for remote data sources
  options: [],
  placeholder: 'Search technologies...'
})

myAutoCompleteExternalDataExample.addEventListener('input.coreui.autocomplete', async event => {
  const query = event.value
  const response = await fetch(`https://example.com/api?q=${query}`)
  const results = await response.json()

  autocomplete.setOptions(results.map(item => ({
    value: item.id,
    label: item.name
  })))
})
```

> When `search: 'external'` is used, the component no longer filters options internally — you must handle all data fetching and filtering logic manually. It opens the panel for whatever options you set, whether or not they contain the typed text.

## Restricted selection

Restrict users to only select from predefined options by setting `data-coreui-allow-only-defined-options="true"`:

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-allow-only-defined-options="true" data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-placeholder="Only predefined options allowed..."></div>
```

Text that names no option a user can select is cleared when the field loses focus, unless it is the label of the current selection, and <kbd>Enter</kbd> does not submit the form while the field holds it.

## Hints and completion

Enable intelligent hints and auto-completion features to improve user experience.

### Show hints

Display completion hints as users type:

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-placeholder="Type to see hints..." data-coreui-show-hints="true"></div>
```

### Highlight matching text

Highlight matching portions of suggestions during search:

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-highlight-options-on-search="true" data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-placeholder="Search with highlighting..."></div>
```

## Validation

The text input carries the value, so `required` blocks the submit of an empty field and the browser shows its message over the input. The state shows on the frame as `.is-{state}`, and while it is `'invalid'` the input carries `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by the message that follows the frame, the way the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/) does for a native field.

```html
<form class="row g-4" data-coreui-validate novalidate>
  <div class="col-12">
    <label class="form-label" for="autocompleteValidationCountry">Country</label>
    <div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-id="autocompleteValidationCountry" data-coreui-name="country" data-coreui-options="Germany, Poland, Spain" data-coreui-required="true"></div>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">Pick a country.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-12">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Submit</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

The state comes from four places, in this order:

- The `validationState` option: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`. The `invalid` and `valid` options still work as aliases; `invalid` wins when both are set, and both are ignored once `validationState` is set.
- An `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the autocomplete in the markup, for example by a server that has already checked the value. It is read once, when the component starts.
- A validation that reports the input invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which the form plugin and the [stepper](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/stepper/) call as well. From then on the autocomplete shows it invalid whenever its value is invalid, until a native reset of the form.
- In a form with `data-coreui-validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the input, and with `data-coreui-validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

```html
<label class="form-label" for="autocompleteServerCountry">Country</label>
<div class="is-invalid" data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-id="autocompleteServerCountry" data-coreui-name="country" data-coreui-options="Germany, Poland, Spain" data-coreui-value="Spain"></div>
<div class="invalid-feedback">We do not ship to Spain yet.</div>
```

A state you give, with the option or with the class, is a verdict on the value it was given for, so the next change of the value the user makes drops it: typing, a pick of a different option, the cleaner, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd> on the selected option, and with `allowOnlyDefinedOptions` an <kbd>Escape</kbd>, a click outside or leaving the field that empties it. A pick of the option already selected keeps it. One action drops the state once, at its first change, so a state you give from a `change.coreui.autocomplete` listener while the action runs stays. A change your own code makes, with `clear()`, `deselectAll()`, `setValue()` or options that arrive later, keeps it. To set it again, call `setValidationState()`: it updates the state without rebuilding the field and replaces a class written on the autocomplete or a state given with `invalid` or `valid`, so `setValidationState(null)` withdraws them. The component never reads `aria-invalid` on the autocomplete, and a state class written after it started only paints the frame: the input gets no `aria-invalid` and the submit is not blocked, so change the state after start with `setValidationState()`. A message placed where the stylesheet does not show it for the autocomplete can be named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` on the autocomplete. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the input blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none; a disabled autocomplete does not block. A native reset of the form puts back the selection the autocomplete started with and drops a state given before it; a state you give from a `reset` listener on the form, or right after `form.reset()`, stays.

## Disabled

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-disabled="true" data-coreui-options="" data-coreui-placeholder="Disabled autocomplete..." ></div>
```

## Floating labels

Autocomplete supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/). Wrap the component in `.form-floating` and put a `<label>` beside it. The component's own `placeholder` is hidden while the label rests inside the field, so the two never overlap.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingAutocomplete">Framework</label>
  <div
    data-coreui-autocomplete
    data-coreui-id="floatingAutocomplete"
    data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js"
    data-coreui-placeholder="Search frameworks..."
  ></div>
</div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the wrapper, or to any ancestor, to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Cleaner functionality

Enable a cleaner button to quickly clear input element:

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-cleaner="true" data-coreui-options="Angular, Bootstrap, React.js, Vue.js" data-coreui-placeholder="With cleaner button..."></div>
```

## Custom templates

The CoreUI Bootstrap Autocomplete Component provides the flexibility to personalize options and group labels by utilizing custom templates. You can easily customize the options using the `optionsTemplate`, and for groups, you can use `optionsGroupsTemplate`, as demonstrated in the examples below:

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <div id="myAutocompleteCountries"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <div id="myAutocompleteCountriesAndCities"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

We use the following JavaScript to set up our autocomplete:

```js
const myAutocompleteCountries = document.getElementById('myAutocompleteCountries')
const myAutocompleteCountriesAndCities = document.getElementById('myAutocompleteCountriesAndCities')

const countries = [
  {
    value: 'pl',
    label: 'Poland',
    flag: '🇵🇱'
  },
  {
    value: 'de',
    label: 'Germany',
    flag: '🇩🇪'
  },
  {
    value: 'us',
    label: 'United States',
    flag: '🇺🇸'
  },
  {
    value: 'es',
    label: 'Spain',
    flag: '🇪🇸'
  },
  {
    value: 'gb',
    label: 'United Kingdom',
    flag: '🇬🇧'
  }
]

const cities = [
  {
    label: 'United States',
    code: 'us',
    flag: '🇺🇸',
    options: [
      {
        value: 'au',
        label: 'Austin'
      },
      {
        value: 'ch',
        label: 'Chicago'
      },
      {
        value: 'la',
        label: 'Los Angeles'
      },
      {
        value: 'ny',
        label: 'New York'
      },
      {
        value: 'sa',
        label: 'San Jose'
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    label: 'United Kingdom',
    code: 'gb',
    flag: '🇬🇧',
    options: [
      {
        value: 'li',
        label: 'Liverpool'
      },
      {
        value: 'lo',
        label: 'London'
      },
      {
        value: 'ma',
        label: 'Manchester'
      }
    ]
  }
]

new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutocompleteCountries, {
  cleaner: true,
  options: countries,
  optionsTemplate(option) {
    return `<div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3"><span class="fs-5">${option.flag}</span><span>${option.label}</span></div>`
  },
  pickerIcon: true,
  placeholder: 'Select country',
  showHints: true

new coreui.Autocomplete(myAutocompleteCountriesAndCities, {
  cleaner: true,
  options: cities,
  optionsGroupsTemplate(optionGroup) {
    return `<div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3"><span class="fg-body fs-5">${optionGroup.flag}</span><span>${optionGroup.label}</span></div>`
  },
  pickerIcon: true,
  placeholder: 'Select city',
  showHints: true
})
```

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add the `data-coreui-autocomplete` attribute to a container element:

```html
<div data-coreui-autocomplete data-coreui-name="framework" data-coreui-options="JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Vue.js, Angular"></div>
```

### Via JavaScript

Initialize the autocomplete component via JavaScript:

```html
<div id="myAutocomplete"></div>
```

```js
const autoCompleteElement = document.getElementById('myAutocomplete')
const autoComplete = new coreui.Autocomplete(autoCompleteElement, {
  name: 'framework',
  options: [
    'JavaScript',
    'TypeScript',
    'React',
    'Vue.js',
    'Angular'
  ]
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-animation="{value}"`. Remember to convert the case of the option name from "_camelCase_" to "_kebab-case_" when using data attributes. For instance, you should write `data-coreui-custom-class="beautifier"` rather than `data-coreui-customClass="beautifier"`.

Starting with CoreUI 4.2.6, all components support an **experimental** reserved data attribute named `data-coreui-config`, which can contain simple component configurations as a JSON string. If an element has attributes `data-coreui-config='{"delay":50, "title":689}'` and `data-coreui-title="Custom Title"`, then the final value for `title` will be `Custom Title`, as the standard data attributes will take precedence over values specified in `data-coreui-config`. Moreover, existing data attributes can also hold JSON values like `data-coreui-delay='{"show":50, "hide":250}'`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `DefaultAllowlist` | Object containing allowed tags and attributes for HTML sanitization when using custom templates. |
| `allowOnlyDefinedOptions` | boolean | `false` | Restricts selection to only predefined options when set to `true`. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | string | `'Clear selection'` | Accessible label for the cleaner button, read by screen readers. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | string | `'Toggle options list'` | Accessible label for the picker button, read by screen readers. |
| `cleaner` | boolean | `false` | Enables the selection cleaner button. |
| `clearSearchOnSelect` | boolean | `true` | Clears the search input when an option is selected. |
| `container` | string, element, boolean | `false` | Where the panel is mounted while open. `true` means `<body>`; leave it alone and the panel goes next to the toggle unless an ancestor would clip it. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the component when set to `true`. |
| `globalSearch` | boolean | `true` | Routes typing to the field from anywhere in the component, so a keystroke never depends on where the focus sits. Set to `false` to keep it local: a keystroke then counts only while the field has the focus. |
| `highlightOptionsOnSearch` | boolean | `false` | Highlights matching text in options during search. |
| `id` | string, null | `null` | Sets a custom ID for the component. If not provided, a unique ID is auto-generated. |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'invalid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `name` | string, null | `null` | Name of the text input the form posts. That input holds what the user sees — the selected option's label, or their own text when `allowOnlyDefinedOptions` is off — so `{ value: 'ng', label: 'Angular' }` posts `Angular`, not `ng`. Without a name the autocomplete is not submitted with the form. |
| `options` | array, string, null | `[]` | Array of options or option objects to populate the dropdown. An option marked `selected: true` is applied the first time it appears, and again after a form reset. It replaces the current selection and the field's text, a pick or typing of the user's included, and fires `change.coreui.autocomplete` only when it fills a field a form reset left empty. While `value` holds anything but `''` or `null`, the flags are ignored. A group with `disabled: true` disables every option in it. |
| `optionsGroupsTemplate` | function, null | `null` | Custom template function for rendering option group labels. Receives the group object as parameter. |
| `optionsMaxHeight` | number, string | `'auto'` | Sets the maximum height of the options dropdown. |
| `optionsTemplate` | function, null | `null` | Custom template function for rendering individual options. Receives the option object as parameter. |
| `pickerIcon` | string, boolean | `false` | The button that opens the options menu: `true` for the built-in icon, an inline SVG string for your own (sanitized), `false` for no button. |
| `placeholder` | string, null | `null` | Placeholder text displayed in the input field. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Makes the input field required for form validation. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Enables HTML sanitization for custom templates to prevent XSS attacks. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function, null | `null` | Custom sanitization function. If provided, it will be used instead of the built-in sanitizer. |
| `search` | string, null | `null` | `'external'` hands the filtering to your code: the component shows the options you set and reports what the user types through `input.coreui.autocomplete`. |
| `searchNoResultsLabel` | boolean, string | `false` | Text displayed when no search results are found; `true` shows "No results found". |
| `showHints` | boolean | `false` | Shows completion hints as users type. |
| `valid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'valid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The state the autocomplete shows: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` blocks the submit. The user's next change of the value drops it. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `value` | number, string, null | `null` | Sets the initial value of the component: the option whose value, compared as text, equals it, so `1` and `'1'` select the same option. It is applied once, as soon as the options contain it, unless the user picks, types or clears the field first; pass it to `setValue()` to select another option, or `null` to clear the field. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Deselects the option, a disabled one included, and empties the typed text. The cleaner, typing over the selection, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd> on it and a native form reset back to no value drop a disabled option the same way. |
| `deselectAll` | Deselects all currently selected options. |
| `dispose` | Destroys the instance and removes the input, buttons and panel it created. An autocomplete disposed while open is closed first; the other classes it wrote on the host stay, and a new instance writes them again from its options. |
| `getInstance` | Static method to get the Bootstrap autocomplete instance associated with a DOM element. |
| `hide` | Hides the Bootstrap autocomplete dropdown options. |
| `search` | Performs a search with the provided text parameter. |
| `disable()` | Disables the field. |
| `enable()` | Enables the field. |
| `setOptions(options)` | Replaces the options, as an array or a comma-separated string. The value stays unless the new options mark another option `selected`, and a value `setValue()` gave that the earlier options lacked is picked without an event; a start value a form reset waits for is reported with `change` when the options bring it. A pick, typing or clearing ends the wait of either value. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the field a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setValue(value)` | Sets the value without firing a change event, also after a form reset; a value the options lack waits for `setOptions()` until the user picks, types or the field is cleared. It replaces the whole selection, a disabled option included, as a native select takes a value from a script. |
| `show` | Shows the Bootstrap autocomplete dropdown options. |
| `toggle` | Toggles the visibility of the dropdown options. |

### Events

The Autocomplete component exposes several events for integrating with application logic.

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.autocomplete` | Fires when the user selects an option, types over a selection or clears it, and when `clear()` empties a field that held a value or text. The initial `value`, a preselected option and a `setValue()` call do not fire it. |
| `hidden.coreui.autocomplete` | Fired when the dropdown has been hidden and CSS transitions completed. |
| `hide.coreui.autocomplete` | Event fires immediately when the hide method is called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the menu open. |
| `input.coreui.autocomplete` | Fires when the search input value changes. |
| `show.coreui.autocomplete` | Event fires immediately when the show method is called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the menu closed. |
| `shown.coreui.autocomplete` | Fired when the dropdown has been made visible and CSS transitions completed. |

```js
const myAutocomplete = document.getElementById('myAutocomplete')
myAutocomplete.addEventListener('change.coreui.autocomplete', event => {
  // Get the selected value
  const selectedValue = event.value
  // Your callback function to handle change
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('Selected:', selectedValue)
})

myAutocomplete.addEventListener('input.coreui.autocomplete', event => {
  // Get the current input value
  const inputValue = event.value
  // Your callback function to handle input
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('Input changed:', inputValue)
})
```

## Accessibility

The Autocomplete component includes several accessibility features:

- **ARIA attributes**: Proper `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, and `aria-autocomplete` attributes
- **Screen reader support**: Descriptive labels and announcements for state changes
- **Name**: `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-description`, `aria-details`, `aria-errormessage`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-required` on the autocomplete element move to the input, which is the combobox, and the element gets them back on dispose; attributes that apply to the whole control, such as `aria-hidden`, stay on the element. Without a name there, point a `<label>` at the input through `data-coreui-id`
- **Description**: an `aria-describedby` on the autocomplete element moves to the input, after the ids the input already has, and the element gets it back on dispose; while the state is `'invalid'` the error message follows it
- **Keyboard navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, Enter, Escape, and Tab
- **Focus management**: The focus never leaves the input — `aria-activedescendant` points at the highlighted option, so typing and choosing happen in one place. <kbd>Home</kbd>, <kbd>End</kbd> and the space bar stay with the text.
- **Semantic markup**: Uses appropriate HTML elements and structure

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Highlight the next option or open dropdown |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> | Highlight the previous option |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Select the highlighted option, or commit the typed text; with the list closed, also submit the form |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the dropdown; the input keeps focus and the highlighted option clears |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Accept hint completion (when hints are enabled) |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd>/<kbd>Delete</kbd> | Delete one character and search with what's left; a held selection is deselected first |
| Any character, <kbd>Backspace</kbd>, <kbd>Delete</kbd> on the picker or clear button | Move the focus to the field and type there, unless `globalSearch` is `false` |

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Autocomplete has no variables of its own: the field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/) and takes the `--cui-control-*` properties, while the options panel is the shared combobox surface, which only sizes itself.

```scss
$combobox-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-popup-min-width: 100%,
  ),
  $combobox-tokens
);
```

Its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the `.popup` tokens it shares with the pickers. `.popup` declares them itself, so set them on `.combobox-popup` or on `.popup`; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` does not reach it.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

The options themselves are a [List box](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/), so their padding, colors, indicator and section labels come from its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike.

# Bootstrap 6 Checkbox

> Create consistent cross-browser and cross-device checkboxes with CoreUI's custom checkbox component.

## Approach

Put `.check` on the `<input type="checkbox">`. That is the whole control — no wrapper, no extra element. Checkboxes are for selecting one or several options in a list; for one option out of many, reach for a [radio](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/radio/).

The input and its `<label>` stay siblings rather than the input sitting inside the label, so the label can be styled from the input's state (`:checked`, `:disabled`) with the sibling selector. Relate them with `id` and `for`, and reach for [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) when you want the label, a description and validation feedback laid out for you.

The check and indeterminate marks are drawn with a CSS mask on the input's own `::before`, which is why their colour is a token (`--cui-check-mark-color`) rather than a value baked into an SVG.

## Basic checkbox

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="checkDefault">
  <label for="checkDefault">Default checkbox</label>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="checkChecked" checked>
  <label for="checkChecked">Checked checkbox</label>
</div>
```

## Indeterminate

Checkboxes can use the `:indeterminate` pseudo-class when it is set from JavaScript — there is no HTML attribute for it.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="checkIndeterminate">
  <label for="checkIndeterminate">Indeterminate checkbox</label>
</div>
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` attribute; the associated `<label>` is styled to match, in a lighter color, to indicate the state.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="checkDisabled" disabled>
  <label for="checkDisabled">Disabled checkbox</label>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="checkCheckedDisabled" checked disabled>
  <label for="checkCheckedDisabled">Disabled checked checkbox</label>
</div>
```

## Stacked

Any number of checkboxes that are immediate siblings stack vertically and are spaced by `.form-field`.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="defaultCheck1">
  <label for="defaultCheck1">Default checkbox</label>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="defaultCheck2" disabled>
  <label for="defaultCheck2">Disabled checkbox</label>
</div>
```

## Inline

There is no inline modifier: the control is an inline element, so a row is a flex container with a gap.

```html
<div class="d-flex gap-4">
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="inlineCheckbox1" value="option1">
    <label for="inlineCheckbox1">1</label>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="inlineCheckbox2" value="option2">
    <label for="inlineCheckbox2">2</label>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="inlineCheckbox3" value="option3" disabled>
    <label for="inlineCheckbox3">3 (disabled)</label>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Sizing

`.check-sm` and `.check-lg` size the whole row — the box, its label, and the space they sit in. Each sets one font size: the box is `1em`, so it follows, and so does the alignment margin, which is computed from the line. Nothing needs re-tuning per size, and a size of your own is one custom property.

```html
<div class="d-flex align-items-start gap-4">
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check check-sm" type="checkbox" id="checkSm" checked>
    <label for="checkSm">Small</label>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="checkMd" checked>
    <label for="checkMd">Default</label>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="check check-lg" type="checkbox" id="checkLg" checked>
    <label for="checkLg">Large</label>
  </div>
</div>
```

Any other size is one custom property, and the alignment follows it:

```html
<input class="check" type="checkbox" style="--cui-check-size: 2em" aria-label="...">
```

## Without a label

A checkbox with no label text is the input on its own. Give it an accessible name some other way — `aria-label`, for instance. The name says what the checkbox does, like `aria-label="Select all rows"`, and replaces the `...` placeholder in the example below. See the [forms overview](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/overview/#accessibility) for details.

```html
<input class="check" type="checkbox" id="checkboxNoLabel" value="" aria-label="...">
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" value="" id="fieldCheck">
  <label for="fieldCheck">Subscribe to the newsletter</label>
  <div class="form-text">We send one email a month, and never share your address.</div>
</div>
```
## Description

Add a description after the label and wrap both in a `.form-field-content`, so the description sits under the label rather than beside the checkbox.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input type="checkbox" id="checkDescription" class="check" checked />
  <div class="form-field-content">
    <label for="checkDescription">Example checkbox</label>
    <small class="form-text">Supporting description for the label above.</small>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Toggle buttons

Create button-like checkboxes by putting `.btn-check` on a `<label>` with the button classes, and nesting the input inside it. The label is the button, so there is no `id`/`for` pair to keep in sync. They can be grouped in a [button group](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/button-group/).

```html
<label class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-check">
  <input type="checkbox" autocomplete="off">
  Single toggle
</label>

<label class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked autocomplete="off">
  Checked
</label>

<label class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-check">
  <input type="checkbox" disabled autocomplete="off">
  Disabled
</label>
```

```html
<label class="btn-outline theme-primary btn-check">
  <input type="checkbox" autocomplete="off">
  Single toggle
</label>

<label class="btn-outline theme-secondary btn-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked autocomplete="off">
  Checked
</label>
```

> Visually, these checkbox toggle buttons are identical to the [button plugin toggle buttons](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/button/#button-plugin). However, they are conveyed differently by assistive technologies: the checkbox toggles will be announced by screen readers as "checked"/"not checked" (since, despite their appearance, they are fundamentally still checkboxes), whereas the button plugin toggle buttons will be announced as "button"/"button pressed". The choice between these two approaches will depend on the type of toggle you are creating, and whether or not the toggle will make sense to users when announced as a checkbox or as an actual button.

## Deprecated markup

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

The v5 spelling — `.form-check` wrapping a `.form-check-input` and a `.form-check-label`, with `.form-check-inline` — still works and lays out exactly as it did; it is an alias of the new controls now rather than a second implementation. It ships in the opt-in [`coreui-legacy.css`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/install/#v5-compatibility-css) rather than in `coreui.css`, and is removed in v7.

`.form-check-reverse` is **gone**. It right-flushed the label and the control as a pair, and it was never the settings row — label on the left, control on the right — people reach for. That row is `justify-content: space-between` on the field.

```html
<div class="form-check">
  <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" value="" id="deprecatedCheck" checked>
  <label class="form-check-label" for="deprecatedCheck">
    Deprecated markup
  </label>
</div>
```

```diff
- <div class="form-check">
-   <input class="form-check-input" type="checkbox" id="c">
-   <label class="form-check-label" for="c">Label</label>
- </div>
+ <div class="form-field">
+   <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="c">
+   <label for="c">Label</label>
+ </div>
```

The v5 toggle button — `.btn-check` on the input, with a sibling `.btn` label tied to it by `id`/`for` — also still works and renders identically.

See the [v6 migration guide](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/migration/v6/) for the full picture.

## Theme variants

Modify the appearance of checked checkboxes by adding a [`.theme-{color}` class](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) to the `.check` input, or to any element above it. This sets the checked background and border color to the theme color.

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Checkboxes read their own custom properties, so restyling one control does not touch the other two. Set them on the control itself — an ancestor cannot override a token the element declares for itself.

```scss
$check-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-check-size: var(--cui-control-size),
    --cui-check-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-check-border: var(--cui-border-width) solid var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-check-border-radius: .25em,
    --cui-check-mark-color: var(--cui-primary-contrast),
    --cui-check-mark-checked: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='m6 10 3 3 6-6'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-mark-indeterminate: #{escape-svg(url("data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 20 20'><path fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-linecap='round' stroke-linejoin='round' stroke-width='3' d='M6 10h8'/></svg>"))},
    --cui-check-checked-bg: var(--cui-control-checked-bg),
    --cui-check-checked-border-color: var(--cui-control-checked-border-color),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-bg),
    --cui-check-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color),
    --cui-check-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-disabled-opacity),
    --cui-check-margin-top: calc((var(--cui-body-line-height) * 1em - var(--cui-check-size)) * .5),
    --cui-check-active-filter: var(--cui-control-active-filter),
    --cui-check-label-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $check-tokens
);
```

### Shared variables

The checkbox, the radio and the switch share their size and their focus, active and disabled states. Those live on `:root` as `--cui-control-*`, so one declaration retunes all three at runtime:

```scss
--cui-control-size: 1em,
--cui-control-checked-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-checked-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-bg: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-indeterminate-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
--cui-control-active-filter: brightness(90%),
--cui-control-focus-border-color: var(--cui-btn-input-focus-border-color),
--cui-control-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-3),
--cui-control-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-label-disabled-opacity: .5,
--cui-control-transition-duration: .15s,
--cui-control-transition-timing: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1),
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one size class, and the same map drives both `.check-{size}` and `.radio-{size}` — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$check-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: (size: .875rem, margin-top: .21875rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm)),
    lg: (size: 1.25rem, margin-top: .3125rem, font-size: var(--cui-font-size-lg))
  ),
  $check-sizes
);
```
