# Bootstrap 6 Date Input

> Create date fields with a section-based input mask. Users type the day, month, and year in separate sections with automatic navigation and validation — like the native date input, but with full control over the format.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

Use an empty container with `data-coreui-date-input` to create a masked date field. The mask is split into day, month, and year sections — click or focus a section and type, use arrow keys to adjust values, and the caret moves to the next section automatically.

By default, the section order and separators are derived from the user's locale, so `12/31/2026` in `en-US` becomes `31.12.2026` in `de-DE` without any configuration.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="basicDateInputLabel">Delivery date</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-name="delivery-date" aria-labelledby="basicDateInputLabel"></div>
```

## Date and time

Set `data-coreui-type="datetime"` and the field carries the time as well. The hour cycle follows the locale, so a 12-hour locale gets an AM/PM section and a 24-hour one does not. Everything else on this page applies unchanged: the same typing, the same arrow keys, the same events.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputAppointmentLabel">Appointment</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-type="datetime" data-coreui-name="appointment" aria-labelledby="dateInputAppointmentLabel"></div>
```

Add `data-coreui-seconds="true"` for a seconds section:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputTimestampLabel">Timestamp</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-type="datetime" data-coreui-seconds="true" aria-labelledby="dateInputTimestampLabel"></div>
```

`data-coreui-type="time"` keeps only the time sections. That is the field [time input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/time-input/) renders; it reports a change through `timeChange` instead of `dateChange`.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputTimeLabel">Opening hour</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-type="time" data-coreui-name="opening-hour" aria-labelledby="dateInputTimeLabel"></div>
```

A `format` overrides the type, because it names the sections itself. [Date range input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-range-input/) takes both options too, so a range with time is the same two attributes on the range container.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <span class="form-label" id="dateInputDeliveryDateLabel">Delivery date</span>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-name="delivery-date" aria-labelledby="dateInputDeliveryDateLabel"></div>
  <div class="form-text">We deliver on working days only.</div>
</div>
```

## Formats

Set an explicit format with the `data-coreui-format` attribute. The parser accepts both dayjs/moment-style tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`, `YY`) and date-fns/Unicode-style tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`, `yy`), plus `ww` for ISO week numbers and `q` (numeric) or `QQQ` (`Q1`–`Q4`) for quarters, so you can reuse the format strings from the date library you already use. Any other character becomes a literal separator — a fixed, non-editable part of the mask — and text wrapped in single quotes is always a literal, even when it contains token letters (`'Week' ww` renders `Week 29`; escape a quote by doubling it, `''`).

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputDdMMYyyyLabel">dd.MM.yyyy</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputDdMMYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputYYYYMMDDLabel">YYYY-MM-DD</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="YYYY-MM-DD" aria-labelledby="dateInputYYYYMMDDLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputMMDDYYLabel">MM/DD/YY</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="MM/DD/YY" aria-labelledby="dateInputMMDDYYLabel"></div>
</div>
```

Two-digit year sections expand with smart century assignment — values up to 50 years in the future resolve to the current century, older ones to the previous century.

The format doesn't have to include every section — a month-and-year mask works like the native `month` input and reports the first day of the month:

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputMMYyyyLabel">MM.yyyy</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputMMYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputMMMMYyyyLabel">MMMM yyyy</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="MMMM yyyy" data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateInputMMMMYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
```

Week and quarter masks work the same way. A week mask edits the ISO week directly and reports the Monday of that week; its year section holds the ISO week-numbering year, which can differ from the calendar year around January 1st. Combine a quoted label with the `ww` token for the native week input's presentation, or use `yyyy-Www` (the uppercase `W` is a literal) for the ISO wire format. A quarter mask reports the first day of the quarter:

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputWeekWwYyyyLabel">'Week' ww, yyyy</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="'Week' ww, yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputWeekWwYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputYyyyWwwLabel">yyyy-Www</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="yyyy-Www" aria-labelledby="dateInputYyyyWwwLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputQQQYyyyLabel">QQQ yyyy</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="QQQ yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputQQQYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections with localized short or full month names. Type letters to match a month by prefix — `m` selects <strong>M</strong>arch, continuing with `may` switches to <strong>May</strong> — and the caret moves on as soon as the prefix is unambiguous. Digits and arrow keys keep working too.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputDDMMMMYYYYLabel">DD MMMM YYYY</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="DD MMMM YYYY" data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateInputDDMMMMYYYYLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputMMMDYYYYLabel">MMM D, YYYY</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="MMM D, YYYY" data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateInputMMMDYYYYLabel"></div>
</div>
```

Month names default to the grammatical form used inside a full date — e.g. Polish shows the genitive `14 lipca 2026`, not the standalone `lipiec`. To use a different form (or your own localization), pass all twelve names through the `monthNames` option; they are used for display, letter matching, and paste alike.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputStandalonePolishMonthNamesLabel">Standalone Polish month names</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="DD MMMM YYYY" data-coreui-locale="pl-PL"
     data-coreui-month-names='["styczeń", "luty", "marzec", "kwiecień", "maj", "czerwiec", "lipiec", "sierpień", "wrzesień", "październik", "listopad", "grudzień"]' aria-labelledby="dateInputStandalonePolishMonthNamesLabel"></div>
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, the mask follows the locale set via `data-coreui-locale`.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputEnUSLabel">en-US</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateInputEnUSLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputPlPLLabel">pl-PL</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-locale="pl-PL" data-coreui-day-placeholder="DD" data-coreui-month-placeholder="MM" data-coreui-year-placeholder="RRRR" aria-labelledby="dateInputPlPLLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputJaJPLabel">ja-JP</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-locale="ja-JP" aria-labelledby="dateInputJaJPLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Initial value

Set the initial date with the `data-coreui-date` attribute.

A field holds what its format shows. A date given with a time of day to a field without a time keeps only its day: `getDate()` and `dateChange` report midnight. Use a format with a time when the time matters.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputDateOfBirthLabel">Date of birth</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-date="2000-01-15" aria-labelledby="dateInputDateOfBirthLabel"></div>
```

## Min and max dates

Constrain the selectable range with `minDate` and `maxDate`. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected. A date field compares the limits by the day. A field with a time compares them to the smallest unit it shows, and there a `maxDate` without a time of day covers its whole day.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputDateInJuly2026Label">Date in July 2026</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-min-date="2026-07-01" data-coreui-max-date="2026-07-31" aria-labelledby="dateInputDateInJuly2026Label"></div>
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, the `disabledDates` option excludes specific dates — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function. Unlike in the [date picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-picker/#disabled-dates), there is no calendar to gray out: a completed date that hits a disabled entry gets the `.is-invalid` class and the component reports `null` until the value is corrected.

In this example July 4–7 and July 16 can't be entered — try typing one of them:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputDeliveryDateLabel2">Delivery date</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" id="myDateInputDisabledDates" aria-labelledby="dateInputDeliveryDateLabel2"></div>
```

```js
const myDateInputDisabledDates = document.getElementById('myDateInputDisabledDates')

const optionsDateInputDisabledDates = {
  locale: 'en-US',
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  date: new Date(2026, 6, 10),
  disabledDates: [
    [new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)],
    new Date(2026, 6, 16)
  ],
  minDate: new Date(2026, 6, 1),
  maxDate: new Date(2026, 6, 31)
}

new coreui.DateInput(myDateInputDisabledDates, optionsDateInputDisabledDates)
```

### Disabling weekends

Pass a function to disable dates by rule — here Saturdays and Sundays:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputBusinessDayLabel">Business day</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" id="myDateInputDisabledDates2" aria-labelledby="dateInputBusinessDayLabel"></div>
```

```js
const myDateInputDisabledDates2 = document.getElementById('myDateInputDisabledDates2')

const optionsDateInputDisabledDates2 = {
  disabledDates(date) {
    const day = date.getDay()
    return day === 0 || day === 6
  },
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  locale: 'en-US'
}

new coreui.DateInput(myDateInputDisabledDates2, optionsDateInputDisabledDates2)
```

## Custom formats

The built-in token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings for date masks, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the mask. Pair it with `inputDateParse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into the field.

In this example the mask uses the dayjs format `MMMM DD, YYYY`, and dayjs (with the `customParseFormat` plugin) parses pasted strings:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputDayjsFormatLabel">dayjs format</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" id="myDateInputCustomFormats1" aria-labelledby="dateInputDayjsFormatLabel"></div>
```

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/dayjs.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/plugin/customParseFormat.js"></script>
```

```js
const myDateInputCustomFormats1 = document.getElementById('myDateInputCustomFormats1')

dayjs.extend(window.dayjs_plugin_customParseFormat)
const optionsDateInputCustomFormats1 = {
  locale: 'en-US',
  date: new Date(2022, 8, 3),
  format: 'MMMM DD, YYYY',
  inputDateParse: value => dayjs(value, 'MMMM DD, YYYY', 'en').toDate()
}

new coreui.DateInput(myDateInputCustomFormats1, optionsDateInputCustomFormats1)
```

Localized formats work the same way — the section names come from the component's `locale` (or the `monthNames` option), while the dayjs locale file handles parsing pasted text, here in Spanish:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateInputLocalizedDayjsFormatLabel">Localized dayjs format</label>
<div class="form-control form-date-time" id="myDateInputCustomFormats2" aria-labelledby="dateInputLocalizedDayjsFormatLabel"></div>
```

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/dayjs.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/plugin/customParseFormat.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/locale/es.js"></script>
```

```js
const myDateInputCustomFormats2 = document.getElementById('myDateInputCustomFormats2')

dayjs.extend(window.dayjs_plugin_customParseFormat)
dayjs.locale('es')
const optionsDateInputCustomFormats2 = {
  locale: 'es-ES',
  date: new Date(2022, 8, 3),
  format: 'YYYY MMMM DD',
  inputDateParse: value => dayjs(value, 'YYYY MMMM DD', 'es').toDate()
}

new coreui.DateInput(myDateInputCustomFormats2, optionsDateInputCustomFormats2)
```

## Validation

The field shows its validation state on the element and on its sections, and links the message that follows it, the way the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/) does for a native field. It keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over the field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` field that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/#usage), puts focus on its first empty section, the browser with its own message over the field. A field that is not required does not block, and submits no date while it rejects one.

The state comes from five places, in this order:

- The limits: a completed date outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` makes the field invalid until it is corrected, whatever else is set, and until then the value field submits no date, as `getDate()` returns none; a read-only field holding such a date submits none either. A date before year 1 counts as before `minDate` even without that option; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- The `validationState` option: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`.
- An `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the element in the markup, for example by a server that has already checked the date. It is read once, when the component starts.
- A validation that reports the field invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which the form plugin and the [stepper](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/stepper/) call as well. From then on the field shows it invalid whenever its date is invalid, until a native reset of the form.
- In a form with `data-coreui-validate`, the `:user-invalid` and `:user-valid` states of the value field, the same states the stylesheet reads on a native field. A field becomes `.is-valid` after a submit only when the form opts into success styling with `data-coreui-validate="valid"`.

A state you give, with the option or with the class, is a verdict on the date it was given for, so the next change of the date the user makes drops it: a typed digit or letter, an arrow, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or <kbd>Delete</kbd>, a paste or a cut that changes what the field holds. A key that leaves the field as it is keeps the state. A change your own code makes, with `setDate()`, `clear()` or `reset()`, keeps it. To set it again, from a `dateChange.coreui.date-input` or `change` listener or after a server response, call `setValidationState()`. It updates the state without rebuilding the field and replaces a class written on the element, so `setValidationState(null)` withdraws that class. A class or an `aria-invalid` written on the element after the component starts is not read. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the field blocks the submit like any invalid field, with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none; a custom validity you set on the value field yourself stays as it is, and a disabled or read-only field does not block. A native form reset returns the field to the date it was created with and drops the state; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset.

Sibling `.valid-feedback`/`.invalid-feedback` elements work as with any other form control. While the field is invalid, its error message, an `.invalid-feedback` or `.invalid-tooltip` after the field, after the frame around it or in its `.form-field`, describes every section, so a screen reader reads the error with the field. A message placed anywhere else can be named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` on the field, and one with the `hidden` attribute is left out, so an `errorChange` listener can show the message that matches `event.error` and hide the rest. A message the page adds later, while the field stays invalid, is picked up the next time the field changes, or right away when it is added in an `errorChange` listener.

```html
<div class="mb-4 form-field">
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-validation-state="valid"></div>
  <div class="valid-feedback">Looks good!</div>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <div class="form-control form-date-time is-invalid" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-date="2026-07-20"></div>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">We have no delivery slots left on this date.</div>
</div>
```

```html
<form data-coreui-validate novalidate>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-name="delivery" data-coreui-required="true"></div>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">Please provide a delivery date.</div>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

## Floating labels

The date input supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/). When the field is empty and not focused, the mask placeholders are hidden so the label can rest inside the field; focusing the field floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingDateInput">Delivery date</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" id="floatingDateInput"></div>
</div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the wrapper, or to any ancestor, to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

The field renders as a `.form-control`, so the standard sizing classes work — add `.form-control-sm` or `.form-control-lg` to the container. Validation states (`.is-invalid` set automatically for out-of-range dates, or your own `.is-valid`) and input groups work the same way.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputLargeLabel">Large</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time form-control-lg" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputLargeLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputDefaultLabel">Default</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputDefaultLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputSmallLabel">Small</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time form-control-sm" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateInputSmallLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Disabled and readonly

Add `data-coreui-disabled="true"` to disable the field, or `data-coreui-readonly="true"` to make it focusable but non-editable.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputDisabledLabel">Disabled</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-disabled="true" aria-labelledby="dateInputDisabledLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateInputReadonlyLabel">Readonly</label>
  <div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-readonly="true" aria-labelledby="dateInputReadonlyLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

The date input implements the [spinbutton pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/) per section, mirroring the internal structure of the native date input:

- **Role attributes**: the container has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, and `aria-valuetext` (month sections announce the localized month name).
- **Roving tabindex**: the whole field is a single tab stop; arrow keys move between sections.
- **Labels**: point `aria-labelledby` at the visible label, as the examples on this page do, because a `<label for>` does not name a group. An `aria-label` written on the element stays as it is, and the `ariaLabel` option fills it in only when the element has none. Sections receive `aria-label`s (`Day`, `Month`, `Year`), each replaceable on its own — `ariaDayLabel`, `ariaMonthLabel`, `ariaYearLabel` — for localization.
- **Label click**: clicking a label that names the field, through `aria-labelledby` or a `<label for>` pointing at the element, moves focus to the first empty section, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Validity**: while the field is invalid (a date outside `minDate` / `maxDate` or in `disabledDates`, a date before year 1, a given `'invalid'` state, or a validation that reported the field), every section carries `aria-invalid="true"`. The group does not, since ARIA defines no invalid state for a group, and an `aria-invalid` you write on the element is left as it is and does not change the state; set it with `validationState`. A disabled or read-only field is never reported as missing. With `required`, every section carries `aria-required="true"`.
- **Description**: the `aria-describedby` the field has when it starts, pointing at its help text or feedback message, reaches the first section, and every section while the field is invalid, together with the error message shown for the field, so the reason for an error is read wherever the focus sits without the help text repeating on each section. A description the page sets on the field later stays on the field.
- **Mobile input**: sections use `inputmode="numeric"`, so touch devices show the numeric keyboard.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix; the caret advances when the prefix is unambiguous |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section, wrapping day and month around their bounds; an empty year starts at the current year |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value; <kbd>Backspace</kbd> then clears all sections, typing restarts from the first section |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | Copy the selection — the whole formatted value after <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date and fill all sections |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-date-input` to an empty `div`. The component renders the sections, separators, and a value input, which is submitted with the form once you give it a `name`. Include the `form-control form-date-time` classes in the markup — the component adds them on initialization anyway, but having them from the start keeps the field styled and full-height before the JavaScript runs (no flash of an unstyled element on load).

```html
<div class="form-control form-date-time" data-coreui-date-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-name="date"></div>
```

### Via JavaScript

```javascript
const dateInput = new coreui.DateInput(document.querySelector('#myDateInput'), {
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  date: new Date(2026, 6, 14)
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript. For data attributes, append the option name to `data-coreui-`, as in `data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaDayLabel` | string | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaHourLabel` | string | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `'Date input'` | The `aria-label` of the `role="group"` container when the element carries no `aria-label` of its own. On `type="datetime"` the default becomes `'Date and time input'`, on `type="time"` `'Time input'`. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | string | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | string | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | string | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | string | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | string | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | string | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | string | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autofocus` | boolean | `false` | Focus the first section right after initialization |
| `date` | date, number, string, null | `null` | Initial date |
| `dayPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disable the component. |
| `disabledDates` | array, date, function, null | `null` | Dates (or a matcher function) that can't be selected |
| `format` | function, string, null | `null` | Mask layout: `null` derives it from the locale, a string is parsed as format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout |
| `hourPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | function, null | `null` | Custom parser used for pasted text, e.g. a date library |
| `locale` | string | `'default'` | Locale used to derive the mask layout and month names |
| `maxDate` | date, number, string, null | `null` | Latest selectable date |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | date, number, string, null | `null` | Earliest selectable date |
| `minutePlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | array, null | `null` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`), overriding the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form |
| `monthPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `name` | string, null | `null` | Name of the value input the value is submitted under. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readonly` | boolean | `false` | Make the field focusable but non-editable |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Required attribute of the value input |
| `secondPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | boolean | `false` | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived layout of `type="datetime"` and `type="time"` |
| `type` | string | `'date'` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries: `'date'`, `'datetime'` or `'time'`. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The validation state the field shows: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. The next change of the date by the user clears it, see [Validation](#validation). |
| `weekPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Clear all sections |
| `getDate` | Return the current date, or `null` when incomplete or invalid |
| `reset` | Reset the field to the date it was created with, emitting `dateChange` and the native `input` and `change` of the value field when the value moves. A native form reset does the same. |
| `disable()` | Disables the field. |
| `enable()` | Enables the field. |
| `setDate(date, triggerChange)` | Sets the date. By default it fires no `dateChange` and no native `input` or `change` of the value field, since the code that calls it already knows the value; `errorChange` still reports a date the field refuses. Pass `true` as `triggerChange` when the date comes from the user through another control, such as a calendar of your own: the field then fires the events typing that date would; a given validation state stays, as with any change from code. The focused section stays. Without a call the field keeps what the user typed. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the field a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |

```javascript
const dateInput = coreui.DateInput.getInstance(document.querySelector('#myDateInput'))
dateInput.clear()
dateInput.getDate()
dateInput.setDate('2026-10-19')
```

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dateChange.coreui.date-input` | Fired when the date changes; `event.date` is a `Date`, or `null` when the field is incomplete or invalid |
| `errorChange.coreui.date-input` | Fired when the validation state changes; `event.error` is `'incomplete'`, `'minDate'`, `'maxDate'`, `'disabledDate'`, or `null` when the value is valid or the field is empty |

When one change moves both the value and the validation state, `dateChange` fires first and `errorChange` after it, so a date an `errorChange` listener sets replaces the one just reported.

```javascript
document.addEventListener('dateChange.coreui.date-input', event => {
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('Date changed:', event.date)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The date, time, and date-time inputs share one set of styles under the `form-date-time` name. The field is a [`.form-control`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control/#css-variables), so its frame comes from the `--cui-control-*` tokens; the ones below style the sections inside it. Both sets sit on the field and can be set on a single element.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```


---

# Bootstrap 6 Date Picker

> Create a date field with a calendar popup. Users type the date into a section-based mask or pick it from the calendar, and the two stay in sync.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

Below is an example of a basic Date Picker.

### Days

The input is a section-based mask — type the date directly, adjust a section
with the arrow keys, or pick a day from the calendar. There is no free-text
parsing and no debounce: the field always holds a valid partial date.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-date="2026/03/15" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### With footer

There is no `footer` option. Project a `<template data-coreui-template="footer">`
child instead — its content is cloned into the dropdown. Buttons act through
`data-coreui-picker-action` (`today`, `clear`, `reset`, `close`), so labels,
order, and translations are yours. A button opting into the `today` action
opts into its state too: it is disabled at initialization when today falls
outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates`. This is one-way — the picker only
ever sets `disabled`, so a button you disable in the template stays disabled.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker>
      <template data-coreui-template="footer">
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-danger btn-sm me-auto" data-coreui-picker-action="today">Today</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="clear">Clear</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="close">OK</button>
      </template>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Here `maxDate` is the end of last month, so the `today` button disables
itself. The state of any other button is yours — the slot context exposes
`isDateSelectable(date)`, which answers whether a date, expressed in the
field's mask, passes the `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` validation (a day
mask checks the calendar day, so `new Date()` passes with a `maxDate` of
today, and a month, quarter or year mask checks the whole period) — and every
programmatic date still runs through the field's
validation: out of range, the field turns `is-invalid`, `errorChange` reports
the reason, and `getDate()` reports `null`, the same outcome as typing that
date. `setDate()` fires no `dateChange`; an action such as `today` fires it
with `null`.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div id="myDatePickerFooterToday">
      <template data-coreui-template="footer">
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-danger btn-sm me-auto" data-coreui-picker-action="today">Today</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="close">OK</button>
      </template>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const myDatePickerFooterToday = document.getElementById('myDatePickerFooterToday')

const datePickerFooterToday = new coreui.DatePicker(myDatePickerFooterToday, {
  locale: 'en-US',
  maxDate: new Date(new Date().getFullYear(), new Date().getMonth(), 0)
})
```

### Weeks

Add `data-coreui-selection-type="week"` to select week numbers, and
`data-coreui-show-week-number="true"` to show them in the grid. The field
renders the native `<input type="week">` presentation — a fixed, non-editable
localized label followed by the week and year sections (`Week 29, 2026`,
`Tydzień 29, 2026`, …). The year is the ISO week-numbering year, which can
differ from the calendar year around January 1st, and the reported `Date` is
the Monday of the selected week. Prefer the ISO wire format in the field?
Set `data-coreui-format="yyyy-Www"`.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-selection-type="week"
      data-coreui-show-week-number="true"
      data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Months

Add `data-coreui-selection-type="month"` to select months. The field mask
narrows to month and year automatically.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-selection-type="month"
      data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Quarters

Add `data-coreui-selection-type="quarter"` to select quarters — the equivalent
of the `<input type="quarter">` that HTML never shipped. The field mask narrows
to a quarter and year section (`Q4 2026`), and the reported `Date` is the
first day of the selected quarter.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-selection-type="quarter"
      data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Years

Add `data-coreui-selection-type="year"` to select years. The field mask narrows
to the year automatically.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-selection-type="year"
      data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## With time

Set `timepicker` to add the time half. The field switches to a date and time
mask, the panel grows a row of time selects under the calendar, and picking a
day no longer closes the panel — the two halves own different parts of one
value, so the interaction is not over until the user says so. While no time is
picked, or the field holds a time a list does not offer, each select stands on a
`--` placeholder, so every enabled option, the first allowed one included, sets
the time.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-timepicker="true" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

`hours`, `minutes` and `seconds` narrow what the time half offers, and are
ignored without `timepicker`. Hours are 0 to 23 in every locale; on a 12-hour
clock an hour that only one period allows sets that period. The four `ariaSelect*Label` options name its
selects, and with the flag on the field actions call themselves "Clear date and
time" and "Toggle calendar and time selection" unless the page passed its own
label.

`minDate` and `maxDate` can carry a time of day. Their day stays selectable in
the calendar and the time selects disable the hours, minutes and seconds before
`minDate` or after `maxDate` on that day. A time the panel sets beyond a limit,
such as the current time when the day of `minDate` is picked, moves to the
limit; a typed time beyond it marks the field invalid. Until a date is picked,
the time selects work on today moved into the limits. A limit without a time of
day covers its whole day.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-timepicker="true" data-coreui-min-date="2026-10-15T09:30" data-coreui-max-date="2026-10-30T17:00" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <span class="form-label" id="datePickerDeliveryDateLabel">Delivery date</span>
  <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker aria-labelledby="datePickerDeliveryDateLabel"></div>
  <div class="form-text">We deliver on working days only.</div>
</div>
```

## Composing the markup

The picker is built from other components — the [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/) field, the [calendar](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/calendar/) and a popup — held together by the date it owns. The markup is where you choose the parts: mark an element with a role attribute and the picker adopts it instead of building its own; leave a part out and it is generated as in the examples above.

| Role | Element | What the picker does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-coreui-picker-field` | a `div` | Hosts the date input's sections. Without it the field is generated (and wrapped in `.form-floating` when `floatingLabel` is set). |
| `data-coreui-picker-toggle` | a `button` or any element | Opens and closes the calendar. Gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`, and `aria-controls` while the calendar is open, and `ariaPickerLabel` as its name unless it has one or shows text of its own. |
| `data-coreui-picker-cleaner` | a `button` | Clears the value. Gets `ariaCleanerLabel` as its name unless it has one or shows text of its own. |

A decorative `<svg>` inside an adopted button is marked `aria-hidden` for you. So a trigger can be a regular button with its own text and icon, the way a combobox has one:

```html
<div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker>
  <div data-coreui-picker-field></div>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-cleaner>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M3 3l10 10M13 3L3 13"/></svg>
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-toggle>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><rect x="1.5" y="2.5" width="13" height="12" rx="1.5"/><path d="M1.5 6.5h13M5 1v3M11 1v3"/></svg>
    Pick a date
  </button>
</div>
```

The `cleanerIcon` and `pickerIcon` options only feed the generated buttons; with your own markup the icon is whatever you put in the HTML, and nothing is sanitized because nothing is rendered from a string.

## Floating labels

The date picker supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/): set `floatingLabel` and the component renders the label itself — no wrapper markup needed — and the text also becomes the field's accessible name. The mask placeholders stay hidden while the label rests inside the field; focusing any part of the field — the sections or the picker button — floats the label and reveals the mask.

```html
<div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-floating-label="Delivery date" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the component element to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the mask showing.

## Sizing

Set heights using the `data-coreui-size` attribute like `data-coreui-size="lg"`
and `data-coreui-size="sm"`.

```html
<div class="row mb-4">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-size="lg" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-size="sm" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Disabled

Add the `data-coreui-disabled="true"` attribute to give the picker a grayed out
appearance and remove pointer events.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-disabled="true" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Disabled dates

The `disabledDates` option excludes specific dates — single `Date`s,
`[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function. The calendar grays them out and
the field refuses them: a completed date that hits a disabled entry gets the
`.is-invalid` class and the picker reports `null`, and submits no date, until it is corrected.
In week, month, quarter and year selection the calendar and the field judge the
whole period: it is refused only when it lies wholly before `minDate` or after
`maxDate`, or `disabledDates` covers every day of it that the limits leave. In week selection the limits count as whole weeks, so for a week that is all seven days.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div id="myDatePickerDisabledDates"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const myDatePickerDisabledDates = document.getElementById('myDatePickerDisabledDates')

const datePickerDisabledDates = new coreui.DatePicker(myDatePickerDisabledDates, {
  locale: 'en-US',
  date: new Date(2026, 6, 10),
  disabledDates: [
    [new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)],
    new Date(2026, 6, 16)
  ],
  minDate: new Date(2026, 6, 1),
  maxDate: new Date(2026, 6, 31)
})

myDatePickerDisabledDates.addEventListener('dateChange.coreui.date-picker', event => {
  console.log('dateChange', event.date)
})
```

### Disabling weekends

Pass a function to disable every date that matches a rule.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div id="myDatePickerWeekends"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const myDatePickerWeekends = document.getElementById('myDatePickerWeekends')

const datePickerWeekends = new coreui.DatePicker(myDatePickerWeekends, {
  locale: 'en-US',
  disabledDates: date => date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6
})
```

## Validation

The picker shows its validation state on the frame and on the sections of its field, which the message after the picker describes, the way the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/) does for a native field. The field keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over it, so a `required` picker that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, as the [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#validation) does.

You give a state with the `validationState` option (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases) or with an `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the picker element, the server-side route, which is read once, when the picker starts; the option wins over the class. A given state is a verdict on the date it was given for, so the next change of the date the user makes drops it: a day picked in the calendar, a time picked with `timepicker`, the cleaner, a footer button that changes the date through the context, or typing in the field. An action that leaves the date as it is keeps the state. A change your own code makes, with `setDate()`, `clear()`, `reset()` or `today()`, keeps it. `setValidationState()` sets it again without rebuilding the picker. A class or an `aria-invalid` written on the picker element after it starts is not read. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the picker blocks the submit with the text of the message after it, or `Invalid value.` when there is none. A native form reset puts back the date the picker started with and drops the state.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5 form-field">
    <div class="is-invalid" data-coreui-date-picker data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date="2026-07-14"></div>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">We have no delivery slots left on this date.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Right to left support

RTL support is built-in and can be explicitly controlled through the
`$enable-rtl` variable in Sass. The popup flips its anchoring side with the
document direction.

### Hebrew

```html
<div class="row" dir="rtl">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="he-IL" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Persian

The date picker is Gregorian: with a locale whose own calendar has different months, like Persian, its calendar shows the Gregorian months in that locale's language and digits, and its field holds Gregorian numbers.

```html
<div class="row" dir="rtl">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-locale="fa-IR" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Custom formats

The mask of the field defines the format. Set it with `data-coreui-format` (or
the `format` option), which the field forwards from the shell. The parser accepts both dayjs/moment-style tokens
(`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`, `YY`) and date-fns/Unicode-style tokens (`dd`, `MM`,
`yyyy`, `yy`), plus `ww` for ISO week numbers and `q` (numeric) or `QQQ`
(`Q1`–`Q4`) for quarters; any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5 mb-4 mb-sm-0">
    <label class="form-label" id="datePickerDdMMYyyyLabel">dd.MM.yyyy</label>
    <div data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker aria-labelledby="datePickerDdMMYyyyLabel"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6 col-lg-5">
    <label class="form-label" id="datePickerYYYYMMDDLabel">YYYY-MM-DD</label>
    <div data-coreui-format="YYYY-MM-DD" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker aria-labelledby="datePickerYYYYMMDDLabel"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

A format does not have to include every section — a month-and-year mask reports
the first day of the month.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-5">
    <div data-coreui-format="MMMM yyyy" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

The field is a [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#accessibility) — a group of spinbutton sections — so its own arrow keys belong to the value, and the popup opens on the native control's dropdown keys. Focus enters the calendar on the selected date, else on today or on the `minDate` / `maxDate` today falls outside of, also when that date cannot be picked: it is announced as unavailable and the arrows move on from it. In week selection it enters on the row of that week.

Clicking a label that names the field, through `aria-labelledby` or a `<label for>` pointing at the element, moves focus to the first empty section of the field.

An `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` on the picker element moves to the field, so a screen reader announces the name and the description when focus enters it, and the picker element gets them back on dispose. Point `aria-labelledby` at the visible label, as the examples on this page do; it names the field over `floatingLabel` and an `ariaLabel` in `inputOptions`, the way the browser ranks names. A `data-coreui-picker-field` you wrote that already has an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` keeps its own name, and its own `aria-describedby` comes first, followed by the one that moves.

While the picker shows an invalid state, the sections of its field carry `aria-invalid="true"` and are described by the error message after the picker, see [Validation](#validation). An `aria-invalid` written on the picker element is not read; give the state with `validationState` or with the class.

The toggle's name ends with the date the picker holds, written in full (`Toggle calendar, Friday, August 14, 2026`, with the time after it with `timepicker`), so a screen reader reads the picked date when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce a pick that closes the popup onto that toggle. With `timepicker` the popup stays open, and the calendar announces the pick through `ariaSelectedDateAnnouncement`; it does the same without a toggle (`pickerIcon: false`) and with a `data-coreui-picker-toggle` that has a name or text of its own, which keeps it unchanged.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>F4</kbd> | Open the calendar popup and move focus into the grid |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the popup and return focus to the field or the toggle that opened it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move within the open calendar; the field is outside the dialog and stays out of the cycle |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous day; crossing the edge of the grid moves to the adjacent month |
| <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> | Move focus to the same day of the next / previous week |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last day of the week inside `minDate` / `maxDate`, into the previous / next month when the week starts or ends there |
| <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> | Move focus to the same day of the next / previous month, keeping the day number when the target month is long enough; a series of presses keeps the day it started from, so January 31 goes to February 28 and then March 31, also across a stop at `minDate` / `maxDate`; any other key or a click starts a new series |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Page Up</kbd> | Move focus to the same day of the next / previous year, keeping the day of a series the same way |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | Select the focused date, and close the popup unless `timepicker` is on, where the time half still has to be set; nothing happens on a date that cannot be picked |

In the calendar grid, a key from the table pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> is neither handled nor cancelled: focus stays where it is and the key stays free for the browser and assistive technology.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-date-picker` to a `div` element.

```html
<div data-coreui-date-picker></div>
```

Inside it, `data-coreui-picker-field`, `data-coreui-picker-toggle` and `data-coreui-picker-cleaner` name the parts you supply yourself — see [Composing the markup](#composing-the-markup).

### Via JavaScript

```html
<div class="my-date-picker"></div>
```

```js
const datePickerElementList = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.my-date-picker'))
const datePickerList = datePickerElementList.map(datePickerEl => {
  return new coreui.DatePicker(datePickerEl)
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript. For data attributes,
append the option name to `data-coreui-`, converting "_camelCase_" to
"_kebab-case_" — write `data-coreui-selection-type="week"`, not
`data-coreui-selectionType="week"`.

Options belonging to the inner [calendar](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/calendar/#options),
[date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#options) or, with `timepicker`, the time
columns of the [time picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/time-picker/#options) are forwarded by
name, so their data attributes work on the picker element too. The calendar's
`startDate` and the time columns' `hourCycle`, `onChange` and `time` are set
by the picker itself.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `SVGAllowlist` | Allowlist used when sanitizing the icon markup. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | string | `'Clear date'` | Accessible label of the cleaner button. `'Clear date and time'` with `timepicker` while the default is kept. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `'Date input'` | Accessible name of the field. It lands on the `role="group"` container the sections sit in, so it names the whole control rather than one part of it. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | string | `'Toggle calendar'` | Accessible label of the picker button, followed by the date the picker holds. `'Toggle calendar and time selection'` with `timepicker` while the default is kept. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | string | `'Calendar'` | Accessible name of the calendar panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. `'Calendar and time selection'` with `timepicker` while the default is kept. |
| `calendarOptions` | object | `{}` | Programmatic escape hatch for calendar options. |
| `cleaner` | boolean | `true` | Renders a button that clears the value. It appears only once the field holds one. |
| `cleanerIcon` | string | cross SVG | Inline SVG of the generated cleaner (sanitized). Not used for a `data-coreui-picker-cleaner` you wrote. |
| `container` | string, element, false | `false` | Teleport target for the dropdown. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `date` | date, string, null | `null` | Initial value. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the field and the popup. |
| `floatingLabel` | string, null | `null` | Renders a floating label over the field, which also becomes its accessible name. Not rendered for a `data-coreui-picker-field` you wrote, which only takes the name, and not even that when the field carries an `aria-label` of its own. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the picker element names the field instead. |
| `format` | function, string, null | `null` | Mask layout of the field: `null` derives it from the locale (or, for week, month, quarter and year selection, uses the matching default mask), a string is parsed as format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout. |
| `inputOptions` | object | `{}` | Programmatic escape hatch for date input options, except `validationState`, which the picker owns. |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'invalid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `locale` | string | browser locale | Drives section order, separators, and calendar labels. |
| `maxDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Upper bound, enforced by both layers. With `timepicker`, a time of day bounds the time on that day, and a date without one covers its whole day. |
| `minDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Lower bound, enforced by both layers. With `timepicker`, a time of day bounds the time on that day. |
| `monthNames` | array, null | `null` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`). |
| `name` | string, null | `null` | Name of the generated value input. Without it the field is not submitted with the form. |
| `pickerIcon` | string, boolean | `true` | The button that opens the calendar: `true` for the built-in icon, an inline SVG string for your own (sanitized), `false` for no button. Not used for a `data-coreui-picker-toggle` you wrote. Without either the popup has no pointer opener and nothing reports the expanded state, though the field keeps the keyboard openers below. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize the icon markup. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function, null | `null` | Custom sanitizer. |
| `seconds` | array, boolean, function | `true` | Seconds offered by the time half. Ignored without `timepicker`. |
| `selectionOptions` | object | `{}` | Programmatic escape hatch for the time half, except `onChange`, `time` and, when the field shows hours, `hourCycle`, which the picker owns. |
| `selectionType` | string | `'day'` | What the picker selects: `'day'`, `'week'`, `'month'`, `'quarter'` or `'year'`. The calendar and the field mask follow it. |
| `size` | string, null | `null` | `'sm'` or `'lg'`. |
| `timepicker` | boolean | `false` | Add a time half to the panel and switch the field to a date and time mask. |
| `valid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'valid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The validation state the picker shows: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. The next change the user makes clears it, see [Validation](#validation). |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Clears the value. |
| `dispose` | Destroys the picker and its inner components. |
| `getContext` | Returns the slot context (see below). |
| `getDate` | Returns the current value (`Date` or `null`). |
| `getInstance` | Static — returns the instance for a DOM element. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | Static — returns the instance, creating it if needed. |
| `hide` | Closes the popup. |
| `reset` | Restores the initial value. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the picker a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setDate` | Sets the value without firing `dateChange`. The open calendar, the time selection and the name of the toggle follow it. |
| `show` | Opens the popup. |
| `today` | Sets today's date. |
| `toggle` | Toggles the popup. |

#### Slot context

Projected regions (and any custom code) drive the picker through a small
imperative contract instead of configuration:

```js
const picker = coreui.DatePicker.getOrCreateInstance(element)
const context = picker.getContext()

context.today()          // set today's date
context.setDate(date)    // set any date
context.clear()          // clear the value
context.reset()          // restore the initial value
context.close()          // close the popup
context.date             // current value (Date | null)
context.disabled         // disabled state
```

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dateChange.coreui.date-picker` | Fired when the value changes — from the calendar, the field, or a context action. `event.date` is the validated `Date`, or `null`; `event.formattedDate` is the same value in the shape of `selectionType` (`2026-01`, `2026W03`, `2026Q1`, `2026`, or the `Date` itself for `day`), with the year in at least four digits (`0026-01`). |
| `hidden.coreui.date-picker` | Fired once the popup has finished its exit transition and left the page. Skipped when the popup reopens first. |
| `hide.coreui.date-picker` | Fired immediately when `hide` is called — by the API, the indicator, Escape or an outside click. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the popup open. |
| `show.coreui.date-picker` | Fired immediately when `show` is called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the popup closed. |
| `shown.coreui.date-picker` | Fired once the popup has finished its entry transition. Skipped when the popup closes first. |

The field's own events (`dateChange.coreui.date-input`,
`errorChange.coreui.date-input`) still bubble from the inner element — the shell
does not duplicate them. `dateChange.coreui.date-picker` fires before the
field's `errorChange` for the same change, whether it comes from the calendar,
the field or an action, so a date an `errorChange` listener sets replaces the one
just reported.

```js
const myDatePicker = document.getElementById('myDatePicker')
myDatePicker.addEventListener('dateChange.coreui.date-picker', event => {
  console.log(event.date)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/#css-variables) on the picker element itself, so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. Set them on the picker element to restyle one field.

The picker declares its local CSS variables on its panel, `.date-picker-popup`,
for real-time customization. Values are set via Sass, so Sass customization is
supported too.

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

The time half declares its own on `.date-picker-time-body`, so it can be
restyled without touching the panel around it.

```scss
$date-picker-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-body-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-width: 2.5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-date-picker-time-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-4),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-font-size: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-font-size),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-color: var(--cui-btn-input-fg),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-padding-y: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-x),
    --cui-date-picker-time-select-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
  ),
  $date-picker-time-tokens
);
```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select. `.popup` declares them itself, so set them on `.date-picker-popup` to restyle this panel or on `.popup` for all of them; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` does not reach it.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

```scss
$calendar-tokens: defaults(

    --cui-calendar-table-margin: .5rem,

    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-hover-color: var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-color),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-hover-bg: oklch(from var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-bg) calc(l * var(--cui-theme-hover-lightness)) calc(c * var(--cui-theme-hover-chroma)) h),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-color: var(--cui-primary-fg-emphasis),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-hover-color: var(--cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-color),
    --cui-calendar-cell-selected-adjacent-hover-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-muted),
    --cui-calendar-cell-range-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
    --cui-calendar-cell-range-hover-border-color: var(--cui-primary-base),
    --cui-calendar-cell-today-color: var(--cui-danger-base),
  ),
  $calendar-tokens
);
```
