# Bootstrap 6 Date Range Input

> Create a start and end date field in one frame. Both ends use the section-based mask of the date input, and the range is validated as a whole.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

Use an empty container with `data-coreui-date-range-input` to create a range field. It is two [date inputs](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/) — start and end — and a separator in one frame, held together by the range the component owns: both ends share the mask and the limits, and an end before the start marks the whole field invalid.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStayLabel">Stay</label>
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-name="check-in" data-coreui-end-name="check-out" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel"></div>
```

## Date and time

`data-coreui-type="datetime"` puts the time on both ends, and `data-coreui-seconds="true"` adds a seconds section. The range compares the two ends by instant, so an end earlier in the day than the start on the same date marks the field invalid.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputShiftLabel">Shift</label>
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-type="datetime" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-name="shift-start" data-coreui-end-name="shift-end" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputShiftLabel"></div>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <span class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStayLabel2">Stay</span>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-name="check-in" data-coreui-end-name="check-out" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel2"></div>
  <div class="form-text">Check-out has to be on or after check-in.</div>
</div>
```

## Formats

Set an explicit mask for both ends with the `data-coreui-format` attribute. The parser is the [date input's](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#formats), so dayjs/moment tokens (`DD`, `MM`, `YYYY`) and date-fns/Unicode tokens (`dd`, `MM`, `yyyy`) both work, and any other character becomes a literal separator.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputDdMMYyyyLabel">dd.MM.yyyy</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputDdMMYyyyLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputYYYYMMDDLabel">YYYY-MM-DD</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="YYYY-MM-DD" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputYYYYMMDDLabel"></div>
</div>
```

A mask that leaves out sections works here too — a month-and-year range reports the first day of each month:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputReportingPeriodLabel">Reporting period</label>
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="MM.yyyy" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputReportingPeriodLabel"></div>
```

## Month names

Use the `MMM` or `MMMM` tokens for text month sections in both ends; typing letters matches a month by prefix. Pass all twelve names through `monthNames` to override the locale-derived, date-context grammatical form.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputDDMMMMYYYYLabel">DD MMMM YYYY</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="DD MMMM YYYY" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputDDMMMMYYYYLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStandalonePolishMonthNamesLabel">Standalone Polish month names</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="pl-PL" data-coreui-format="DD MMMM YYYY"
       data-coreui-month-names='["styczeń", "luty", "marzec", "kwiecień", "maj", "czerwiec", "lipiec", "sierpień", "wrzesień", "październik", "listopad", "grudzień"]' aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStandalonePolishMonthNamesLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Locale

Without an explicit format, both masks follow the locale set via `data-coreui-locale`.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputEnUSLabel">en-US</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputEnUSLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputPlPLLabel">pl-PL</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="pl-PL" data-coreui-day-placeholder="DD" data-coreui-month-placeholder="MM" data-coreui-year-placeholder="RRRR" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputPlPLLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputJaJPLabel">ja-JP</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="ja-JP" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputJaJPLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Initial value

Seed either end with `data-coreui-start-date` and `data-coreui-end-date`; a string is parsed like a typed value.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStayLabel3">Stay</label>
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-20" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel3"></div>
```

## Min and max dates

`minDate` and `maxDate` constrain both ends. A completed date outside the range gets the `.is-invalid` class on its own field and that end reports `null` until the value is corrected.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputDatesInJuly2026Label">Dates in July 2026</label>
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-min-date="2026-07-01" data-coreui-max-date="2026-07-31" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputDatesInJuly2026Label"></div>
```

## Disabled dates

Beyond a simple range, `disabledDates` excludes specific dates from both ends — single `Date`s, `[start, end]` ranges, or a matcher function. As in the [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#disabled-dates), a completed date that hits a disabled entry gets `.is-invalid` and that end reports `null`.

In this example July 4–7 and July 16 can't be entered — try typing one of them:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStayLabel4">Stay</label>
<div id="myDateRangeInputDisabledDates" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel4"></div>
```

```js
const myDateRangeInputDisabledDates = document.getElementById('myDateRangeInputDisabledDates')

const optionsDateRangeInputDisabledDates = {
  locale: 'en-US',
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  startDate: new Date(2026, 6, 10),
  disabledDates: [
    [new Date(2026, 6, 4), new Date(2026, 6, 7)],
    new Date(2026, 6, 16)
  ],
  minDate: new Date(2026, 6, 1),
  maxDate: new Date(2026, 6, 31)
}

new coreui.DateRangeInput(myDateRangeInputDisabledDates, optionsDateRangeInputDisabledDates)
```

### Disabling weekends

Pass a function to disable dates by rule — here Saturdays and Sundays, on both ends:

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputBusinessDaysLabel">Business days</label>
<div id="myDateRangeInputDisabledDates2" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputBusinessDaysLabel"></div>
```

```js
const myDateRangeInputDisabledDates2 = document.getElementById('myDateRangeInputDisabledDates2')

const optionsDateRangeInputDisabledDates2 = {
  disabledDates(date) {
    const day = date.getDay()
    return day === 0 || day === 6
  },
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  locale: 'en-US'
}

new coreui.DateRangeInput(myDateRangeInputDisabledDates2, optionsDateRangeInputDisabledDates2)
```

## Custom formats

The token parser covers dayjs, moment, date-fns, and luxon format strings, so you can reuse the format string from the date library you already work with — the library itself isn't required to render or edit the masks. Pair it with `inputDateParse` when you want that library to also parse text pasted into either end.

```html
<label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputStayLabel5">Stay</label>
<div id="myDateRangeInputCustomFormats" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputStayLabel5"></div>
```

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/dayjs.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dayjs@1/plugin/customParseFormat.js"></script>
```

```js
const myDateRangeInputCustomFormats = document.getElementById('myDateRangeInputCustomFormats')

dayjs.extend(window.dayjs_plugin_customParseFormat)
const optionsDateRangeInputCustomFormats = {
  locale: 'en-US',
  startDate: new Date(2026, 6, 14),
  endDate: new Date(2026, 6, 20),
  format: 'MMMM DD, YYYY',
  inputDateParse: value => dayjs(value, 'MMMM DD, YYYY', 'en').toDate()
}

new coreui.DateRangeInput(myDateRangeInputCustomFormats, optionsDateRangeInputCustomFormats)
```

## Validation

The frame shows the state of the range and each field shows its own, the way the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/) does for a native field. Each end keeps its value in a `<textarea>` laid invisibly over its field, which takes part in native constraint validation: a `required` end that is empty, incomplete or holds a rejected date blocks the submit, and the browser, or the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/#usage), puts focus on its first empty section.

The state comes from these places, in this order:

- The order: an end before the start is a state of the range, not of either date, so `.is-invalid` lands on the frame and both fields stay editable. Every section of both fields carries `aria-invalid="true"` until the order is fixed, and neither field is drawn valid meanwhile, whatever else is set. `isRangeValid()` reports it.
- The limits: a completed date outside `minDate`/`maxDate`/`disabledDates` makes its own field invalid, which the frame picks up, and that field's value field submits no date until it is corrected. A date before year 1 counts as before `minDate` even without that option; when the field loses the focus, its year becomes 1.
- The `validationState` option: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`, a verdict on the whole range that lands on the frame and on both ends.
- An `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the frame in the markup, for example by a server that has already checked the range. It is read once, when the component starts.
- A validation that reports a field (a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which the form plugin and the [stepper](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/stepper/) call as well), and in a form with `data-coreui-validate` the `:user-invalid` state of each value field, with `data-coreui-validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state, as for the [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#validation).

A state you give, with the option or with the class, is a verdict on the range it was given for, so the next change the user makes to either end drops it from both ends and the frame. A change your own code makes, with `setRange()`, `clear()` or `reset()`, keeps it. To set it again, call `setValidationState()`: it updates the state without rebuilding the fields and replaces a class written on the frame. A class or an `aria-invalid` written on the frame after the component starts is not read. While the given state is `'invalid'`, both ends block the submit with the text of the message after the frame, or `Invalid value.` when there is none, unless the range is disabled or read-only. A native form reset returns both ends to the dates they were created with and drops the state; a `reset` listener that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the whole reset.

Sibling `.valid-feedback`/`.invalid-feedback` elements work as with any other form control. The error shows when the frame is invalid and when a field inside it is, which is where the state of a single date lands; the success message waits until nothing is invalid. While a field is invalid, the error message describes each of its sections.

```html
<div class="mb-4 form-field">
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-20" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-14"></div>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">Check-out has to be on or after check-in.</div>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-20" data-coreui-validation-state="valid"></div>
  <div class="valid-feedback">Looks good!</div>
</div>
```

```html
<form data-coreui-validate novalidate>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-start-name="from" data-coreui-end-name="to" data-coreui-required="true"></div>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">Please provide both dates.</div>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the range in your `submit` listener; `getStartDate()` and `getEndDate()` return `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```js
const element = document.querySelector('#stayRange')
const range = coreui.DateRangeInput.getOrCreateInstance(element)

element.closest('form').addEventListener('submit', event => {
  const start = range.getStartDate()
  const end = range.getEndDate()

  if (!start || !end || end < start) {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
})
```

## Floating labels

Each end can carry its own [floating label](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/); the text is also that end's accessible name, so the visible and the spoken label stay one thing.

```html
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-floating-label="Check-in" data-coreui-end-floating-label="Check-out"></div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the component element to keep both labels [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the masks showing.

## Sizing

The frame is a `.form-control-group`, so the standard sizing classes work — set `data-coreui-size="lg"` or `data-coreui-size="sm"` and both ends follow.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputLargeLabel">Large</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-size="lg" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputLargeLabel"></div>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputDefaultLabel">Default</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputDefaultLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputSmallLabel">Small</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-size="sm" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputSmallLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Disabled and readonly

Add `data-coreui-disabled="true"` to disable both ends, or `data-coreui-readonly="true"` to make them focusable but non-editable.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputDisabledLabel">Disabled</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-20" data-coreui-disabled="true" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputDisabledLabel"></div>
</div>
<div>
  <label class="form-label" id="dateRangeInputReadonlyLabel">Readonly</label>
  <div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-20" data-coreui-readonly="true" aria-labelledby="dateRangeInputReadonlyLabel"></div>
</div>
```

## Composing the markup

The component adopts the parts you write inside its element and generates the rest, so the separator can be a word, your own icon, or nothing you have to configure. A generated part takes its place around the ones you wrote, so writing only the end still gives start, separator, end, in that order on screen and for <kbd>Tab</kbd>:

| Role | Element | What the component does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-coreui-range-start` | a `div` | Hosts the start field's sections. |
| `data-coreui-range-separator` | any element | Sits between the ends; marked `aria-hidden`. Without it an arrow is generated from `separatorIcon` / `separatorIconRtl`. |
| `data-coreui-range-end` | a `div` | Hosts the end field's sections. |

```html
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-locale="en-US">
  <div data-coreui-range-start></div>
  <span class="mx-3 fg-2" data-coreui-range-separator>to</span>
  <div data-coreui-range-end></div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

Each end is a [date input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#accessibility) with the spinbutton pattern per section, so the range is two labelled groups rather than one opaque control:

- **Role attributes**: the element itself is a `role="group"`, each end has `role="group"`, every section is a `role="spinbutton"` with its value attributes.
- **Label click**: clicking a label that names the field, through `aria-labelledby` or a `<label for>` pointing at the element, moves focus to the first empty section of the start date, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Names**: the start and end are named separately — `ariaStartLabel` and `ariaEndLabel` by default, or the floating label text when one is set. An end you wrote with an `aria-label` of its own keeps it. An `aria-labelledby` on the element, pointing at the visible label as the examples on this page do, names the pair, and an `aria-describedby` on it moves to both fields, after any description a field you wrote carries of its own.
- **Separator**: hidden from assistive technology, as is any `<svg>` inside it.
- **Roving tabindex**: each end is a single tab stop; <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves from the start to the end.

### Keyboard support

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>0</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> | Type into the focused section; the caret advances when the section is complete |
| <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> | In text month sections, match a month name by prefix |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Increment / decrement the focused section |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> / <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to the next / previous section, crossing the separator from the last section of the start date into the end date and back; in a right-to-left layout the two keys swap |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | Move focus to the first / last section of the focused end |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Clear the focused section; move to the previous section when already empty |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the focused section |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move from the start date to the end date |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select the whole value of the focused end |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste a date into the focused end |

Apart from the shortcuts in the table, a key pressed with <kbd>Alt</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> changes nothing in the field and is not cancelled: arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> move no focus and change no section, and a digit or letter is not entered. The key stays free for the browser, assistive technology and the picker around the field, where <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> opens the calendar. A character that <kbd>AltGr</kbd> or <kbd>Option</kbd> composes is still entered.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-date-range-input` to an empty `div`. The component renders both fields, the separator, and a value input per end, each submitted with the form once you give it a `startName` or an `endName`.

```html
<div data-coreui-date-range-input data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-start-name="from" data-coreui-end-name="to"></div>
```

### Via JavaScript

```javascript
const dateRangeInput = new coreui.DateRangeInput(document.querySelector('#myDateRangeInput'), {
  format: 'dd.MM.yyyy',
  startDate: new Date(2026, 6, 14),
  endDate: new Date(2026, 6, 20)
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript. For data attributes, append the option name to `data-coreui-`, as in `data-coreui-start-name="from"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | SVG allow list | Allowed tags and attributes for the generated separator icon |
| `ariaDayLabel` | string | `'Day'` | The `aria-label` of the day section. |
| `ariaEndLabel` | string | `'End date'` | Accessible name of the end field when it has no floating label and no `aria-label` of its own |
| `ariaHourLabel` | string | `'Hour'` | The `aria-label` of the hour section. |
| `ariaMeridiemLabel` | string | `'AM/PM'` | The `aria-label` of the meridiem section. |
| `ariaMinuteLabel` | string | `'Minute'` | The `aria-label` of the minute section. |
| `ariaMonthLabel` | string | `'Month'` | The `aria-label` of the month section. |
| `ariaQuarterLabel` | string | `'Quarter'` | The `aria-label` of the quarter section. |
| `ariaSecondLabel` | string | `'Second'` | The `aria-label` of the second section. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | string | `'Start date'` | Accessible name of the start field when it has no floating label and no `aria-label` of its own |
| `ariaWeekLabel` | string | `'Week'` | The `aria-label` of the week section. |
| `ariaYearLabel` | string | `'Year'` | The `aria-label` of the year section. |
| `autofocus` | boolean | `false` | Focus the first section of the start date right after initialization |
| `dayPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `DD` the day section shows while it is empty. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disable both ends |
| `disabledDates` | array, date, function, null | `null` | Dates (or a matcher function) neither end can hold |
| `endDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Initial end date |
| `endFloatingLabel` | string, null | `null` | Floating label of the end field |
| `endName` | string, null | `null` | Name of the value input carrying the end date. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `format` | function, string, null | `null` | Mask layout for both ends: `null` derives it from the locale, a string is parsed as format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout |
| `hourPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `HH` (`hh` on a 12-hour clock) the hour section shows while it is empty. |
| `inputDateParse` | function, null | `null` | Custom parser used for pasted text, e.g. a date library |
| `inputOptions` | object | `{}` | Extra options passed to both date inputs, except `validationState`: the range gives the state to both. |
| `locale` | string | browser locale | Locale used to derive the masks and month names |
| `maxDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Latest date either end can hold |
| `meridiemPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `AM` the meridiem section shows while it is empty. |
| `minDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Earliest date either end can hold |
| `minutePlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `mm` the minute section shows while it is empty. |
| `monthNames` | array, null | `null` | Twelve custom month names for text month sections (`MMM`/`MMMM`) |
| `monthPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `MM` the month section shows while it is empty. |
| `quarterPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `Q` the quarter section shows while it is empty. |
| `readonly` | boolean | `false` | Make both ends focusable but non-editable |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Required attribute of the value inputs |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize the generated separator icon |
| `sanitizeFn` | function, null | `null` | Custom sanitizer |
| `secondPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `ss` the second section shows while it is empty. |
| `seconds` | boolean | `false` | Include a seconds section in the locale-derived layout of `type="datetime"`; both ends follow |
| `separatorIcon` | string | arrow SVG | Icon of the generated separator; ignored for a `data-coreui-range-separator` you wrote |
| `separatorIconRtl` | string | mirrored arrow SVG | Its right-to-left counterpart |
| `size` | string, null | `null` | `'sm'` or `'lg'` |
| `startDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Initial start date |
| `startFloatingLabel` | string, null | `null` | Floating label of the start field |
| `startName` | string, null | `null` | Name of the value input carrying the start date. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `type` | string | `'date'` | Which sections the locale-derived layout carries on both ends: `'date'` or `'datetime'`. A `format` names the sections itself and overrides this. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The validation state of the range, shown on the frame and on both ends: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. The next change the user makes to either end clears it, see [Validation](#validation). |
| `weekPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `WW` the week section shows while it is empty. |
| `yearPlaceholder` | string, null | `null` | Replaces the `YYYY` the year section shows while it is empty. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Empty both ends |
| `getEndDate` | Return the end date, or `null` when that end is incomplete or invalid |
| `getStartDate` | Return the start date, or `null` when that end is incomplete or invalid |
| `isDateSelectable` | Whether a date passes the shared limits |
| `isRangeValid` | `false` while the end is before the start |
| `reset` | Restore the dates the component was created with, emitting the change events when a value moves. A native form reset does the same and also drops a given validation state. |
| `setEndDate(date, triggerChange)` | Sets the end date and keeps the start, without an event by default; pass `true` as `triggerChange` to fire the events a date the user gives through another control would. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the component a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setStartDate(date, triggerChange)` | Sets the start date and keeps the end, without an event by default; pass `true` as `triggerChange` to fire the events a date the user gives through another control would. |
| `setRange` | Set both ends: `setRange(start, end)`. Each end validates its own date, so what the range keeps is what the fields kept. It fires no `startDateChange` or `endDateChange`, since the code that calls it already knows the range; `setRange(start, end, true)` fires the events a range the user picked would; a given validation state stays, as with any change from code. |

```javascript
const dateRangeInput = coreui.DateRangeInput.getInstance(document.querySelector('#myDateRangeInput'))
dateRangeInput.setRange(new Date(2026, 6, 14), new Date(2026, 6, 20))
dateRangeInput.getStartDate()
dateRangeInput.clear()
```

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `endDateChange.coreui.date-range-input` | Fired when the user changes the end, or `clear()`, `reset()` or a setter called with `triggerChange` does; `event.date` is a `Date`, or `null` when that end is incomplete or invalid |
| `startDateChange.coreui.date-range-input` | Fired when the start changes the same way, with the same payload shape as the end |

`setRange(start, end, true)` writes both ends before either event fires. The range events come before the `errorChange.coreui.date-input` of the fields, whether the dates are typed or set that way, so a range an `errorChange` listener sets replaces the one just reported.

Each event carries the date of its own end; a listener reads the whole range from the instance:

```javascript
for (const name of ['startDateChange', 'endDateChange']) {
  document.addEventListener(`${name}.coreui.date-range-input`, event => {
    const dateRangeInput = coreui.DateRangeInput.getInstance(event.target)
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
    console.log('Range changed:', dateRangeInput.getStartDate(), dateRangeInput.getEndDate())
  })
}
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The two ends are date inputs, so they carry the `form-date-time` tokens, and the frame around them carries the [form control group](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/#css-variables) ones. The range adds no tokens of its own.

```scss
// Redeclaring a --cui-control-* token here would shadow `.form-control`
// on the same element, and with it the validation states.
$form-date-time-tokens: () !default;
$form-date-time-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-date-time-placeholder-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-form-date-time-section-border-radius: .25rem,
    --cui-form-date-time-section-focus-bg: var(--cui-primary-bg-subtle),
  ),
  $form-date-time-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Date Range Picker

> Create a start and end date field with a multi-month calendar popup. Users type both dates into section-based masks or pick the range from the calendar, with optional predefined ranges.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Example

### Days

Two masked fields share one input-group frame; the calendar spans two months and
owns the range mechanics — pick a start day and the selection advances to the
end date automatically. Focusing the end field switches the calendar to
end-date selection, the way clicking the end input does in v1.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7 mb-4">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7">
    <div
      data-coreui-end-date="2026/03/20"
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-start-date="2026/03/15"
      data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### With footer

There is no `footer` option — project a `<template data-coreui-template="footer">`
child. With a footer present, completing a range does **not** auto-close;
closing is the footer's job.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7">
    <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-range-picker>
      <template data-coreui-template="footer">
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="clear">Clear</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="close">OK</button>
      </template>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

localized fixed label) — see the [date picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-picker/#weeks)
note on the ISO week-numbering year.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7">
    <div
      data-coreui-locale="en-US"
      data-coreui-selection-type="week"
      data-coreui-show-week-number="true"

  </div>
</div>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html

  <div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-range-picker aria-labelledby="dateRangePickerReportingPeriodLabel"></div>

</div>
```

## Floating labels

Each field carries its own [floating label](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/): set `startFloatingLabel` and `endFloatingLabel` and the picker renders a label over each date, floating independently — fill in the check-in date and only its label rises. The label text also becomes the field's accessible name, so the visible and spoken labels stay one thing. No wrapper markup is needed.

```html
<div data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-floating-label="Check-in" data-coreui-end-floating-label="Check-out" data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the component element to keep both labels [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the masks showing.

## Validation

The picker takes its validation state the way the [date range input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-range-input/#validation) does: an end before the start makes the frame invalid while it stands and keeps both fields from being drawn valid, and a state you give lands on the frame and on both ends. You give it with the `validationState` option (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`, with `invalid` and `valid` as deprecated aliases) or with an `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the picker element, the server-side route, which is read once, when the picker starts; the option wins over the class. While the given state is `'invalid'`, every section of both fields carries `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by the message after the picker, and both ends block the submit with its text, or `Invalid value.` when there is none.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7 form-field">
    <div class="is-invalid" data-coreui-date-range-picker data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-start-date="2026-07-14" data-coreui-end-date="2026-07-20"></div>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">Those dates are already booked.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

A given state is a verdict on the range it was given for, so the next change of the range the user makes drops it from both ends and from the picker element: a date picked in the calendar, the cleaner, a button in the footer or among the [custom ranges](#custom-ranges) that changes the range through the context, or typing in either field. An action that leaves the range as it is keeps the state. A change your own code makes, with `setRange()`, `clear()` or `reset()`, keeps it. `setValidationState()` sets it again without rebuilding the picker. A class or an `aria-invalid` written on the picker element after it starts is not read. A native form reset puts back the range the picker started with and drops the state.

### Blocking the submit

A `required` end that is empty, incomplete or rejected by the limits blocks the submit by itself. An end before the start does not, since both ends hold dates the browser accepts, and neither does an optional end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, which submits no date. Check the range in your `submit` listener; `getStartDate()` and `getEndDate()` return `null` for an end that is empty, incomplete or rejected, so one condition covers both:

```js
const element = document.querySelector('#stayRange')
const range = coreui.DateRangePicker.getOrCreateInstance(element)

element.closest('form').addEventListener('submit', event => {
  const start = range.getStartDate()
  const end = range.getEndDate()

  if (!start || !end || end < start) {
    event.preventDefault()
  }
})
```

## Custom ranges

There is no `ranges` option. Project a `<template data-coreui-template="ranges">`
child — it renders as a column beside the calendars. Presets take arguments, so
they run through `getContext().setRange()`: the date math, labels, and order are
yours.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-8">
    <div id="myDateRangePickerRanges">
      <template data-coreui-template="ranges">
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" id="rangeLast7">Last 7 days</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" id="rangeLast30">Last 30 days</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" id="rangeThisMonth">This month</button>
      </template>
      <template data-coreui-template="footer">
        <button type="button" class="btn-ghost theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="clear">Clear</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm" data-coreui-picker-action="close">OK</button>
      </template>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const myDateRangePickerRanges = document.getElementById('myDateRangePickerRanges')

const dateRangePickerRanges = new coreui.DateRangePicker(myDateRangePickerRanges, {
  locale: 'en-US',
  startName: 'report-start',
  endName: 'report-end'
})

// Projected ranges act through the slot context — labels, order, and the
// date math are userland, the shell only exposes setRange.
const context = () => dateRangePickerRanges.getContext()
const today = new Date()

const presets = {
  rangeLast7: () => context().setRange(new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - 6), today),
  rangeLast30: () => context().setRange(new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - 29), today),
  rangeThisMonth: () => context().setRange(new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), 1), new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth() + 1, 0))
}

for (const [id, apply] of Object.entries(presets)) {
  myDateRangePickerRanges.querySelector(`#${id}`).addEventListener('click', apply)
}
```

### Persian

The date range picker is Gregorian: with a locale whose own calendar has different months, like Persian, its calendar shows the Gregorian months in that locale's language and digits, and its fields hold Gregorian numbers.

```html

  <div class="col-lg-7">
    <div data-coreui-locale="fa-IR" data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

The separator between the two fields is a directional arrow, so the component
renders its mirrored counterpart (`separatorIconRtl`) whenever the picker sits
in an RTL context — the document direction or any `dir="rtl"` ancestor.

## Custom formats

The mask of the fields defines the format. Set it with `data-coreui-format`,
forwarded to both fields.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-7">
    <div data-coreui-format="dd.MM.yyyy" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

The fields and the popup answer to the [same keys as the date picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-picker/#keyboard-support): <kbd>Alt</kbd> (<kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS) + <kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> or <kbd>F4</kbd> opens the calendars, <kbd>Escape</kbd> closes them and returns focus, and arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd>, and <kbd>Page Down</kbd> / <kbd>Page Up</kbd> (with <kbd>Shift</kbd> for years) move the focused date.

The picker element is a `role="group"`, so an `aria-labelledby` on it, pointing at the visible label as the example on this page does, names the pair of fields, and an `aria-describedby` on it moves to both fields. Clicking that label, or a `<label for>` pointing at the element, moves focus to the first empty section of the start date.

The toggle's name ends with the range the picker holds, written by the locale (`Toggle calendar, Thursday, August 20 – Sunday, August 23, 2026`), so a screen reader reads the picked range when the popup closes and focus goes back to the toggle. A live message would be lost at that moment, so the calendar does not announce the pick of the end that closes the popup. A pick that leaves the popup open, such as a new start that keeps the end or any pick with a footer, is announced through `ariaSelectedRangeAnnouncement`, and so is every pick without a toggle (`pickerIcon: false`).

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-date-range-picker` to a `div` element.

<div data-coreui-date-range-picker></div>
```

### Via JavaScript

```

```js
const pickerElementList = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.my-date-range-picker'))
const pickerList = pickerElementList.map(pickerEl => {
  return new coreui.DateRangePicker(pickerEl)
})
```

### Options

Options belonging to the inner [calendar](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/calendar/#options) or
[date range input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-range-input/#options) are forwarded by name, so
their data attributes work on the picker element too. The calendar's `range`
and `selectEndDate` are set by the picker itself.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `SVGAllowlist` | Allowlist used when sanitizing icon markup. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel` | string | `'Clear date range'` | Accessible label of the cleaner button. |
| `ariaEndLabel` | string | `'End date'` | Accessible name of the end field when it has no floating label. Both halves are the same control, so naming them apart is what tells a screen reader which end of the range it is on. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | string | `'Toggle calendar'` | Accessible label of the picker button, followed by the range the picker holds. |
| `ariaPopupLabel` | string | `'Calendar'` | Accessible name of the calendar panel, which opens as a `role="dialog"`. |
| `ariaStartLabel` | string | `'Start date'` | Accessible name of the start field when it has no floating label. |
| `calendarOptions` | object | `{}` | Programmatic escape hatch for calendar options. |
| `calendars` | number | `2` | Months shown side by side. |
| `cleaner` | boolean | `true` | Renders a button that clears the value. It appears only once the field holds one. |
| `cleanerIcon` | string | cross SVG | Inline SVG rendered by the component (sanitized). |
| `container` | string, element, false | `false` | Teleport target for the dropdown. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disables the fields and the popup. |
| `endDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Initial end of the range. |
| `endFloatingLabel` | string, null | `null` | Renders a floating label over the end field, which also becomes that field's accessible name. |
| `endName` | string, null | `null` | Name of the end value input. Without it the end date is not submitted with the form. |
| `format` | function, string, null | `null` | Mask layout of both fields: `null` derives it from the locale (or, for week, month, quarter and year selection, uses the matching default mask), a string is parsed as format tokens, a function receives the locale and returns the section layout. |
| `inputOptions` | object | `{}` | Programmatic escape hatch for date input options, except `validationState`, which the picker owns. |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'invalid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `locale` | string | browser locale | Drives section order, separators, and calendar labels. |
| `maxDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Upper bound, enforced by both layers. |
| `minDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Lower bound, enforced by both layers. |
| `pickerIcon` | string, boolean | `true` | The button that opens the calendar: `true` for the built-in icon, an inline SVG string for your own (sanitized), `false` for no button. Without it the popup has no pointer opener and nothing reports the expanded state, though the field keeps the keyboard openers below. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize the icon markup. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function, null | `null` | Custom sanitizer. |
| `selectionType` | string | `'day'` | What the picker selects: `'day'`, `'week'`, `'month'`, `'quarter'` or `'year'`. The calendar and the field masks follow it. |
| `separatorIcon` | string | arrow SVG | Inline SVG between the two fields (LTR). |
| `separatorIconRtl` | string | mirrored arrow SVG | Inline SVG used when the picker renders in an RTL context. |
| `size` | string, null | `null` | `'sm'` or `'lg'`. |
| `startDate` | date, string, null | `null` | Initial start of the range. |
| `startFloatingLabel` | string, null | `null` | Renders a floating label over the start field, which also becomes that field's accessible name. |
| `startName` | string, null | `null` | Name of the start value input. Without it the start date is not submitted with the form. |
| `valid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'valid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The validation state of the range, shown on the frame and on both ends: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. The next change the user makes to the range clears it, see [Validation](#validation). |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Clears the range. |
| `dispose` | Destroys the picker and its inner components. |
| `getContext` | Returns the slot context (see below). |
| `getEndDate` | Returns the end of the range (`Date` or `null`). |
| `getInstance` | Static — returns the instance for a DOM element. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | Static — returns the instance, creating it if needed. |
| `getStartDate` | Returns the start of the range (`Date` or `null`). |
| `hide` | Closes the popup. |
| `reset` | Restores the initial range. |
| `setEndDate(date)` | Sets the end date and keeps the start, without an event. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the picker a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setStartDate(date)` | Sets the start date and keeps the end, without an event. |
| `setRange` | Sets both ends without an event. The open calendar and the name of the toggle follow it. |
| `show` | Opens the popup. |
| `toggle` | Toggles the popup. |

#### Slot context

```js
const picker = coreui.DateRangePicker.getOrCreateInstance(element)
const context = picker.getContext()

context.setRange(start, end)   // set both ends (null allowed)
context.clear()                // clear the range
context.reset()                // restore the initial range
context.close()                // close the popup
context.startDate              // current start (Date | null)
context.endDate                // current end (Date | null)
context.disabled               // disabled state
```

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `endDateChange.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired when the end changes, with the same payload shape. |
| `hidden.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired once the popup has finished its exit transition and left the page. Skipped when the popup reopens first. |
| `hide.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired immediately when `hide` is called. |
| `show.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired immediately when `show` is called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the popup closed. |
| `shown.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired once the popup has finished its entry transition. Skipped when the popup closes first. |
| `startDateChange.coreui.date-range-picker` | Fired when the start changes. `event.date` is the validated `Date`, or `null`; `event.formattedDate` is the same value in the shape of `selectionType` (`2026-01`, `2026W03`, `2026Q1`, `2026`, or the `Date` itself for `day`), with the year in at least four digits (`0026-01`). |

`startDateChange` and `endDateChange` fire before the fields' `errorChange.coreui.date-input` for the same change, whether it comes from the calendar, the fields or an action such as `clear()` or `getContext().setRange()`; the setters do not fire them.

```js
const myPicker = document.getElementById('myPicker')
myPicker.addEventListener('endDateChange.coreui.date-range-picker', event => {
  console.log(event.date, event.formattedDate)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/#css-variables), `.form-date-range`, inside the picker element, so its frame, the separator, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. Set them on `.form-date-range`; the group declares them itself, so a value set on the picker element stops there. The two ends are [date inputs](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-input/#css-variables) and carry the `form-date-time` tokens.

The panel is the date picker's, and declares its own on `.date-picker-popup`:

```scss
$date-picker-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-ranges-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-timepickers-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-padding-x: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-date-picker-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $date-picker-tokens
);
```

The panel is a `.popup`: its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the tokens every popup panel shares with the other pickers, Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select. `.popup` declares them itself, so set them on `.date-picker-popup` to restyle the panels of the date and date range pickers, or on `.popup` for all of them; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` does not reach it.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Form Field

> A layout wrapper for a form control, its label, description and validation feedback, built on CSS grid.

`.form-field` gives a control the layout and spacing it needs alongside its label, description and validation feedback — so a form is spaced by the field itself rather than by margin utilities sprinkled over its parts.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="fieldText" class="form-label">Email address</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control" id="fieldText" placeholder="name@example.com">
  <div class="form-text">
    We'll never share your email with anyone else.
  </div>
</div>
```

## How it works

- **Default layout** is a single-column grid: everything stacks vertically with one gap. Use it for text inputs, selects, textareas, ranges, input groups and any of the [PRO field components](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/).
- **Two-column layout** switches on through `:has()` when a `.check`, `.radio` or `.switch` is a direct child — the control pins to the first column, the label and description stack in the second. The deprecated `.form-check-input` triggers it too, so markup that has not moved yet lays out the same way.
- **A field label** (`.form-label`) spans both columns and sits above the control row.
- **Grouped controls** — nest a `.form-field` per control inside an outer one to put several radios or checkboxes under a shared label with a shared description.

## Examples

### Select

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="fieldSelect" class="form-label">Country</label>
  <select class="form-control" id="fieldSelect">
    <option selected>Choose one…</option>
    <option value="1">United States</option>
    <option value="2">Canada</option>
    <option value="3">United Kingdom</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

### Textarea

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="fieldTextarea" class="form-label">Message</label>
  <textarea class="form-control" id="fieldTextarea" rows="3"></textarea>
  <div class="form-text">
    Be sure to include the relevant details.
  </div>
</div>
```

### Checkbox

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="fieldCheck">
  <label for="fieldCheck">Subscribe to the newsletter</label>
  <div class="form-text">We send one email a month, and never share your address.</div>
</div>
```

### Grouped

Nest one `.form-field` per control inside an outer one, and give the group its own `.form-label`.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <span class="form-label">Delivery</span>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="radio" type="radio" name="fieldRadio" id="fieldRadio1" checked>
    <label for="fieldRadio1">Standard</label>
    <div class="form-text">Three to five working days.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input class="radio" type="radio" name="fieldRadio" id="fieldRadio2">
    <label for="fieldRadio2">Express</label>
    <div class="form-text">Next working day, where available.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Switch

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input class="switch" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="fieldSwitch">
  <label for="fieldSwitch">Email notifications</label>
  <div class="form-text">Turn this off and we will only contact you about your account.</div>
</div>
```

## Overhead label

When a check, radio, or switch needs a field title above it, add a `.form-label`. It spans both grid columns automatically, so it sits on its own row above the control while the control's own label and description keep their places:

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label class="form-label">Terms and conditions</label>
  <input class="check" type="checkbox" id="fieldOverheadCheck">
  <label for="fieldOverheadCheck">I agree to the terms</label>
  <div class="form-text">Please read them before agreeing.</div>
</div>
```

## Validation

Feedback elements are children of the field like any other, so they inherit its gap and land under the control. A message right after the control shows as it does anywhere. For a check, a radio, a switch, a `.form-control` or `.form-select` in an input group, or a control placed directly in a component frame or in its floating label, the field shows its messages wherever they sit in it, for example in a `.form-field-content` next to the label; a check, a radio and a switch also colour the label. Give each control its own field: a field that groups others shows every message inside it while one of them is invalid.

### Client-side

Add `data-coreui-validate` to the `<form>` to style fields from `:user-invalid`, which only matches after the user has interacted with a control — so a field is not marked wrong before it has been filled in. `novalidate` suppresses the browser's own tooltips while keeping the constraint validation API available.

```html
<form class="vstack gap-4" data-coreui-validate novalidate>
  <div class="form-field">
    <label for="fieldValidateEmail" class="form-label">Email address</label>
    <input type="email" class="form-control" id="fieldValidateEmail" required>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">Please enter a valid email address.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input type="checkbox" id="fieldValidateTerms" class="check" required>
    <label for="fieldValidateTerms">Accept the terms</label>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">You must accept before submitting.</div>
  </div>
  <button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
```

### Server-side

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="fieldValidation" class="form-label">Username</label>
  <input type="text" class="form-control is-invalid" id="fieldValidation" value="jan kowalski" aria-describedby="fieldValidationFeedback">
  <div id="fieldValidationFeedback" class="invalid-feedback">
    A username cannot contain spaces.
  </div>
</div>
```

See [validation](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/) for the full picture, including the server-side and browser-native flavours.

## Descriptions

Add a `<small class="form-text">` after the label and wrap both in a `.form-field-content` so the description sits under the label rather than beside the control.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <input type="checkbox" id="fieldCheckDesc" class="check" />
  <div class="form-field-content">
    <label for="fieldCheckDesc">Subscribe to updates</label>
    <small class="form-text">We'll send you a weekly digest of what's new.</small>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="form-field">
  <input type="radio" id="fieldRadioDesc" class="radio" name="fieldRadioDesc" checked />
  <div class="form-field-content">
    <label for="fieldRadioDesc">Standard shipping</label>
    <small class="form-text">Arrives in three to five working days.</small>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Cards

Add `.form-field-card` to each field for a card treatment that highlights the selected option. The label's hit area covers the whole card, so the option is selected by clicking anywhere on it. Wrap the set in a `.form-group` to carry its own label and keep the spacing tight.

```html
<div class="form-group">
  <label class="form-label">Select a plan</label>
  <div class="vstack gap-1">
    <div class="form-field form-field-card">
      <input type="radio" id="fieldRadioCard1" class="radio" name="fieldRadioCard" checked />
      <div class="form-field-content">
        <label for="fieldRadioCard1">Basic</label>
        <small class="form-text">$9/month — for individuals.</small>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="form-field form-field-card">
      <input type="radio" id="fieldRadioCard2" class="radio" name="fieldRadioCard" />
      <div class="form-field-content">
        <label for="fieldRadioCard2">Pro</label>
        <small class="form-text">$29/month — for teams.</small>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Groups

`.form-group` lays out a set of related fields the way `.form-field` lays out one: a grid with the same gap, and a label or `<legend>` pinned to the start. Reach for it when several fields share a heading — the card example above uses it.

```html
<fieldset class="form-group">
  <legend class="form-label">Notifications</legend>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input type="checkbox" id="groupCheck1" class="check" checked />
    <label for="groupCheck1">Email</label>
  </div>
  <div class="form-field">
    <input type="checkbox" id="groupCheck2" class="check" />
    <label for="groupCheck2">Push</label>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

```scss
$form-field-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-form-field-column-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-field-tokens
);
```

`.form-field-card` and `.form-group` carry their own sets:

```scss
$form-field-card-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-y: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-padding-x: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-form-field-card-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-form-field-card-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-form-field-card-checked-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $form-field-card-tokens
);
```

```scss
$form-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-group-gap: .5rem,
  ),
  $form-group-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Floating Labels

> Create beautifully simple form labels that float over your input fields.

## Example

Wrap a `<label>` and an `<input class="form-control" />` in `.form-floating` to enable floating labels with CoreUI for Bootstrap's textual form fields. A `placeholder` is required on each `<input />` as our method of CSS-only floating labels uses the `:placeholder-shown` pseudo-element. The placeholder stays hidden while the label rests in the field, and shows under the floated label once the field has focus.

Write the `<label>` first, so a screen reader announces it before the field's value. The v5 order — control first, label after — keeps working: every state is matched in both directions, forward with `:has()` and backward with the sibling combinator.

```html
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingInput">Email address</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control" id="floatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com">
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingPassword">Password</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="floatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••">
</div>
```

When there's a `value` already defined, `<label>`s will automatically adjust to their floated position.

```html
<form class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingInputValue">Input with value</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control" id="floatingInputValue" placeholder="name@example.com" value="test@example.com">
</form>
```

Form validation styles also work as expected.

```html
<form class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingInputInvalid">Invalid input</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control is-invalid" id="floatingInputInvalid" placeholder="name@example.com" value="test@example.com">
</form>
```

## Textareas

By default, `<textarea>`s with `.form-control` will be the same height as `<input />`s.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingTextarea">Comments</label>
  <textarea class="form-control" placeholder="Leave a comment here" id="floatingTextarea"></textarea>
</div>
```

To set a custom height on your `<textarea>`, do not use the `rows` attribute. Instead, set an explicit `height` (either inline or via custom CSS).

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingTextarea2">Comments</label>
  <textarea class="form-control" placeholder="Leave a comment here" id="floatingTextarea2" style="height: 100px"></textarea>
</div>
```

## Selects

Other than `.form-control`, floating labels are only available on `.form-control`s. They work in the same way, but unlike `<input />`s, they'll always show the `<label>` in its floated state. **Selects with `size` and `multiple` are not supported.**

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingSelect">Works with selects</label>
  <select class="form-control" id="floatingSelect" aria-label="Floating label select example">
    <option selected>Open this select menu</option>
    <option value="1">One</option>
    <option value="2">Two</option>
    <option value="3">Three</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

## Date and time

Date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs also always show the `<label>` in its floated state. These controls do not support placeholders the way textual inputs do, so a `placeholder` attribute is not required (and is ignored by most browsers on these types). For a field that formats its value by locale, use the [Date Picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/date-picker/#floating-labels) or the [Time Picker](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/time-picker/#floating-labels) with the `floatingLabel` option.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingDate">Date</label>
  <input type="date" class="form-control" id="floatingDate">
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingTime">Time</label>
  <input type="time" class="form-control" id="floatingTime">
</div>
```

## Disabled

Add the `disabled` boolean attribute on an input, a textarea or a select to give it a grayed out appearance, remove pointer events, and prevent focusing.

```html
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingInputDisabled">Email address</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control" id="floatingInputDisabled" placeholder="name@example.com" disabled>
</div>
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingTextareaDisabled">Comments</label>
  <textarea class="form-control" placeholder="Leave a comment here" id="floatingTextareaDisabled" disabled></textarea>
</div>
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingTextarea2Disabled">Comments</label>
  <textarea class="form-control" placeholder="Leave a comment here" id="floatingTextarea2Disabled" style="height: 100px" disabled>Disabled textarea with some text inside</textarea>
</div>
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingSelectDisabled">Works with selects</label>
  <select class="form-control" id="floatingSelectDisabled" aria-label="Floating label disabled select example" disabled>
    <option selected>Open this select menu</option>
    <option value="1">One</option>
    <option value="2">Two</option>
    <option value="3">Three</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

## Readonly plaintext

Floating labels also support `.form-control-plaintext`, which can be helpful for toggling from an editable `<input />` to a plaintext value without affecting the page layout.

```html
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingEmptyPlaintextInput">Empty input</label>
  <input type="email" readonly class="form-control-plaintext" id="floatingEmptyPlaintextInput" placeholder="name@example.com">
</div>
<div class="form-floating mb-4">
  <label for="floatingPlaintextInput">Input with value</label>
  <input type="email" readonly class="form-control-plaintext" id="floatingPlaintextInput" placeholder="name@example.com" value="name@example.com">
</div>
```

## Input groups

Floating labels also support `.input-group` — put the `.form-floating` next to the other addons:

```html
<div class="input-group mb-4">
  <span class="input-group-text">@</span>
  <div class="form-floating">
    <label for="floatingInputGroup1">Username</label>
    <input type="text" class="form-control" id="floatingInputGroup1" placeholder="mdo">
  </div>
</div>
```

When using `.input-group` and `.form-floating` along with form validation, wrap the group in a [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) and place the feedback outside the `.input-group`, so it renders under the whole group rather than inside the frame:

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <div class="input-group">
    <span class="input-group-text">@</span>
    <div class="form-floating is-invalid">
      <label for="floatingInputGroup2">Username</label>
      <input type="text" class="form-control is-invalid" id="floatingInputGroup2" placeholder="mdo" required>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="invalid-feedback">
    Please choose a username.
  </div>
</div>
```

## Always floating

Add `.form-floating-always` to keep the label floated and show the placeholder. Use it on the `.form-floating` itself, or on any ancestor to cover every floating field inside.

```html
<div class="form-floating form-floating-always">
  <label for="alwaysFloatingInput">Email address</label>
  <input type="email" class="form-control" id="alwaysFloatingInput" placeholder="name@example.com">
</div>
<div class="form-floating form-floating-always">
  <label for="alwaysFloatingPassword">Password</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="alwaysFloatingPassword" placeholder="••••••••">
</div>
```

The date and time pickers build their `.form-floating` from the `floatingLabel` option, so put the class on the component element.

```html
<div class="form-floating-always" data-coreui-locale="en-US" data-coreui-floating-label="Delivery date" data-coreui-date-picker></div>
```

By default, placeholders stay transparent until the control is focused. With `.form-floating-always`, the placeholder stays visible in both states, so keep it short on a textarea, where the floated label covers its first line.

## Layout

When working with the CoreUI for Bootstrap grid system, be sure to place form elements within column classes.

```html
<div class="row g-3">
  <div class="col-md">
    <div class="form-floating">
      <label for="floatingInputGrid">Email address</label>
      <input type="email" class="form-control" id="floatingInputGrid" placeholder="name@example.com" value="mdo@example.com">
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-md">
    <div class="form-floating">
      <label for="floatingSelectGrid">Works with selects</label>
      <select class="form-control" id="floatingSelectGrid">
        <option selected>Open this select menu</option>
        <option value="1">One</option>
        <option value="2">Two</option>
        <option value="3">Three</option>
      </select>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

`.form-floating` carries the tokens, so a single field can be retuned without recompiling. Anything nested inside it follows them, including the date and time inputs, which drive their own float on `:focus-within` instead of `:placeholder-shown`.

```scss
$form-floating-tokens: () !default;
$form-floating-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-floating-height: calc(3.5rem + var(--cui-btn-input-border-width) * 2),
    --cui-form-floating-line-height: 1.25,
    --cui-form-floating-padding-x: var(--cui-btn-input-padding-x),
    --cui-form-floating-padding-y: 1rem,
    --cui-form-floating-input-padding-t: 1.625rem,
    --cui-form-floating-input-padding-b: .625rem,
    --cui-form-floating-label-height: 1.5em,
    --cui-form-floating-label-opacity: .65,
    --cui-form-floating-label-transform: scale(.85) translateY(-.5rem) translateX(.15rem),
    --cui-form-floating-label-disabled-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    // The label is a sibling of the control, so it cannot inherit its background.
    --cui-form-floating-label-bg: var(--cui-btn-input-bg),
    --cui-form-floating-label-disabled-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-form-floating-label-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-border-radius),
    --cui-form-floating-transition-property: #{"opacity, transform"},
    --cui-form-floating-transition-duration: .1s,
    --cui-form-floating-transition-timing: ease-in-out,
  ),
  $form-floating-tokens
);
```
