## Custom dropdown header

_Added in 5.26.0._

Use the `headerTemplate` option to fully customize the dropdown header — the area above the options list — including rendering several action buttons. It replaces the built-in select all button and renders independently of `selectAll`. The template function receives a `state` object (`{ selected, total, filtered, filteredSelected }`) and an `actions` object (`selectAll`, `selectFiltered`, `deselectFiltered`, `deselectAll`) whose functions change the selection for the user, so a call drops a given [validation state](#validation) like a pick in the list. Return an `HTMLElement` and wire your own listeners to the `actions`, or return an HTML string for simple custom content. A string goes through the sanitizer, which drops interactive elements such as `<button>`, and nothing wires the `actions` to it, so controls belong on the `HTMLElement` path. The header re-renders on every selection change and search filter, so labels and `disabled` states stay up to date.

```html
<select id="myMultiSelectHeader" data-coreui-multi-select></select>
```

We use the following JavaScript to set up our multi-select:

```js
const myMultiSelectHeader = document.getElementById('myMultiSelectHeader')

new coreui.MultiSelect(myMultiSelectHeader, {
  multiple: true,
  options: [
    { value: 'angular', text: 'Angular' },
    { value: 'bootstrap', text: 'Bootstrap' },
    { value: 'react', text: 'React.js' },
    { value: 'vue', text: 'Vue.js' },
    { value: 'django', text: 'Django' },
    { value: 'laravel', text: 'Laravel' },
    { value: 'node', text: 'Node.js' }
  ],
  placeholder: 'Select frameworks',
  search: true,
  selectionType: 'chips',
  headerTemplate(state, actions) {
    const wrapper = document.createElement('div')
    wrapper.className = 'd-flex flex-wrap gap-3'

    const selectAll = document.createElement('button')
    selectAll.type = 'button'
    selectAll.className = 'btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm'
    selectAll.textContent = `Select all (${state.total})`
    selectAll.disabled = state.selected >= state.total
    selectAll.addEventListener('click', () => actions.selectAll())

    const selectFiltered = document.createElement('button')
    selectFiltered.type = 'button'
    selectFiltered.className = 'btn-solid theme-secondary btn-sm'
    selectFiltered.textContent = `Select filtered (${state.filtered})`
    selectFiltered.disabled = state.filtered === state.filteredSelected
    selectFiltered.addEventListener('click', () => actions.selectFiltered())

    const deselectFiltered = document.createElement('button')
    deselectFiltered.type = 'button'
    deselectFiltered.className = 'btn-outline theme-secondary btn-sm'
    deselectFiltered.textContent = `Deselect filtered (${state.filteredSelected})`
    deselectFiltered.disabled = state.filteredSelected === 0
    deselectFiltered.addEventListener('click', () => actions.deselectFiltered())

    const deselectAll = document.createElement('button')
    deselectAll.type = 'button'
    deselectAll.className = 'btn-outline theme-danger btn-sm'
    deselectAll.textContent = `Deselect all (${state.selected})`
    deselectAll.disabled = state.selected === 0
    deselectAll.addEventListener('click', () => actions.deselectAll())

    wrapper.append(selectAll, selectFiltered, deselectFiltered, deselectAll)
    return wrapper
  }
})
```

## Selectable groups

_Added in 5.26.0._

Enable `optionsGroupsSelectable` to turn each group label into its own tri-state button (`aria-pressed` `false` / `mixed` / `true`) that toggles the group's visible options. Because the indicator is rendered with CSS, it supports a third, `indeterminate` state — shown when only some of a group's options are selected — without any real `<input />` element. The same tri-state logic drives the header [select all](#select-all) button. Group labels join the arrow-key order, and the indicator on options, groups and select all follows the one `indicator` option; the whole feature requires `multiple`.

```html
<select id="myMultiSelectIndeterminate" data-coreui-multi-select></select>
```

We use the following JavaScript to set up our multi-select:

```js
const myMultiSelectIndeterminate = document.getElementById('myMultiSelectIndeterminate')

new coreui.MultiSelect(myMultiSelectIndeterminate, {
  multiple: true,
  optionsGroupsSelectable: true,
  options: [
    {
      label: 'Frontend',
      options: [
        { value: 'angular', text: 'Angular' },
        { value: 'react', text: 'React.js' },
        { value: 'vue', text: 'Vue.js' }
      ]
    },
    {
      label: 'Backend',
      options: [
        { value: 'django', text: 'Django' },
        { value: 'laravel', text: 'Laravel' },
        { value: 'node', text: 'Node.js' }
      ]
    }
  ],
  placeholder: 'Select frameworks',
  search: true,
  selectionType: 'counter'
})
```

## Floating labels

Multi Select supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/). Wrap the component in `.form-floating` and put a `<label>` beside it. It has no input to report emptiness, so the label floats on focus and on the first selection, and the component's `placeholder` is hidden while the label rests inside the field.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingMultiSelect">Frameworks</label>
  <select id="floatingMultiSelect" data-coreui-multi-select multiple>
    <option value="0">Angular</option>
    <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
    <option value="2">React.js</option>
    <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the wrapper, or to any ancestor, to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Sizing

The frame carries the size. Add `.form-control-sm` or `.form-control-lg` to the `<select>` — the component copies the element's classes onto the `.form-control-group` it builds, so the field matches our similarly sized text inputs. The whole selection follows: the chips, the counter text and the cleaner and toggle icons all scale with the frame.

```html
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <select id="multiple-select-counter-lg" class="form-control-lg mb-4" data-coreui-multi-select data-coreui-selection-type="counter" data-coreui-search="true">
      <option value="0">Angular</option>
      <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
      <option value="2">React.js</option>
      <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
      <optgroup label="backend">
        <option value="4">Django</option>
        <option value="5">Laravel</option>
        <option value="6">Node.js</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
    <select id="multiple-select-counter-sm" class="form-control-sm" data-coreui-multi-select data-coreui-selection-type="counter" data-coreui-search="true">
      <option value="0">Angular</option>
      <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
      <option value="2">React.js</option>
      <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
      <optgroup label="backend">
        <option value="4">Django</option>
        <option value="5">Laravel</option>
        <option value="6">Node.js</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
  </div>
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <select id="multiple-select-chips-lg" class="form-control-lg mb-4" data-coreui-multi-select data-coreui-selection-type="chips" data-coreui-search="true">
      <option value="0">Angular</option>
      <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
      <option value="2">React.js</option>
      <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
      <optgroup label="backend">
        <option value="4">Django</option>
        <option value="5">Laravel</option>
        <option value="6">Node.js</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
    <select id="multiple-select-chips-sm" class="form-control-sm" data-coreui-multi-select data-coreui-selection-type="chips" data-coreui-search="true">
      <option value="0">Angular</option>
      <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
      <option value="2">React.js</option>
      <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
      <optgroup label="backend">
        <option value="4">Django</option>
        <option value="5">Laravel</option>
        <option value="6">Node.js</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add the `data-coreui-multi-select` attribute to a `select` element.

```html
<select id="ms1" name="stack" multiple data-coreui-multi-select data-coreui-search="true">
  <option value="0">Angular</option>
  <option value="1">Bootstrap</option>
  <option value="2">React.js</option>
  <option value="3">Vue.js</option>
  <optgroup label="backend">
    <option value="4">Django</option>
    <option value="5">Laravel</option>
    <option value="6">Node.js</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>
```

### Via JavaScript

Call the multi select via JavaScript:

```html
<select data-coreui-multi-select></select>
```

```js
const mulitSelectElementList = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-coreui-multi-select]'))
const mulitSelectList = mulitSelectElementList.map(mulitSelectEl => {
  return new coreui.MultiSelect(mulitSelectEl, {
    // options
  })
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-animation="{value}"`. Remember to convert the case of the option name from "_camelCase_" to "_kebab-case_" when using data attributes. For instance, you should write `data-coreui-custom-class="beautifier"` rather than `data-coreui-customClass="beautifier"`.

Starting with CoreUI 4.2.6, all components support an **experimental** reserved data attribute named `data-coreui-config`, which can contain simple component configurations as a JSON string. If an element has attributes `data-coreui-config='{"delay":50, "title":689}'` and `data-coreui-title="Custom Title"`, then the final value for `title` will be `Custom Title`, as the standard data attributes will take precedence over values specified in `data-coreui-config`. Moreover, existing data attributes can also hold JSON values like `data-coreui-delay='{"show":50, "hide":250}'`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `DefaultAllowlist` | Object containing allowed tags and attributes for HTML sanitization when using custom templates. |
| `ariaChipRemoveLabel` | string \| function | `'Remove'` | Names a chip's remove button with the selected option's text: a string has `{label}` replaced by it, or gets it appended when there is no `{label}` ("Remove Angular"); a function receives the text and returns the whole name. |
| `ariaCleanerLabel`| string | `Clear all selections` | A string that provides an accessible label for the cleaner button. This label is read by screen readers to describe the action associated with the button. |
| `ariaPickerLabel` | string | `'Toggle options list'` | Accessible label of the picker button. |
| `ariaRemovedAnnouncement` | string \| function | `'removed'` | Announced after a value is removed through its chip, <kbd>Backspace</kbd> or the cleaner. A string follows the removed labels (`Angular removed`); a function receives them and returns the whole message. A pick in the list is not announced, since the option says it is selected. |
| `ariaSearchLabel`| string | `Search` | Accessible label for the search input (when `search` is enabled). |
| `ariaTagDeleteLabel` | string \| null | `null` | Deprecated, use `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. While it is set, it takes precedence over `ariaChipRemoveLabel`. |
| `cleaner`| boolean | `true` | Enables selection cleaner element. |
| `clearSearchOnSelect`| boolean | `false` | Clear current search on selecting an item. |
| `container` | string, element, false | `false` | Appends the dropdown to a specific element. Example: `container: 'body'`. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `deselectAllLabel` | string | `'Deselect all'` | Sets the select all button label shown once everything is selected. See `selectAllLabel`. |
| `deselectFilteredLabel` | string | `'Deselect filtered'` | Label shown instead of `deselectAllLabel` when `selectAllMode: 'filtered'` and a search filter narrows the list. See `selectFilteredLabel`. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Toggle the disabled state for the component. |
| `globalSearch` | boolean | `true` | Routes typing to the search box from anywhere in the component, so a keystroke never depends on where the focus sits. Set to `false` to keep it local: the search box then filters only while it has the focus, and typing over the options list jumps to the first option that starts with what was typed, except with `search: 'external'`, where the list holds only the last results. Needs `search`. |
| `headerTemplate` | function, null | `null` | Custom template function for rendering the dropdown header (the area above the options list). Replaces the built-in select all button and renders independently of `selectAll`. Receives a `state` object (`{ selected, total, filtered, filteredSelected }`), where `selected` counts every selected value, disabled ones and ones the current options lack included, and the other three count options in the list, and an `actions` object (`{ selectAll, deselectAll, selectFiltered, deselectFiltered }`) whose functions act for the user and drop a given validation state. Return an `HTMLElement` (wire your own listeners using `actions`, supports multiple controls) or an HTML string (sanitized, no actions wired). Re-renders on every selection change and search filter. |
| `hideSelectAllOnSearchNoResults` | boolean | `true` | Hides the dropdown header with the built-in select all button when a search filter leaves no matching options. Set to `false` to keep the select all button visible even when there are no results. |
| `id` | string, null | `null` | Id of the native select and the base of the ids the component builds (`-listbox`, `-label`, `search-`). Without it the select keeps its own `id`, or gets a generated one. |
| `indicator` | string | `'checkbox'` | Sets the marker used by the options, the selectable group labels and the select all button: `'checkbox'` or `'none'`. |
| `invalid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'invalid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `loadingLabel` | string | `'Loading…'` | Text of the row below the options while the list loads, announced to screen readers when the open panel starts waiting or opens on a wait. |
| `multiple` | boolean | `true` | It specifies that multiple options can be selected at once. |
| `name` | string, null | `null` | Name of the native select the selection is submitted under. A `name` written on the `<select>` itself is honoured too, and this option wins over it. With neither the selection is not submitted with the form. |
| `options` | boolean, array | `false` | List of option elements. A group with `disabled: true` disables every option in it. A selected disabled option stays selected and, like in a native select, is not sent with the form. |
| `optionsGroupsSelectable` | boolean | `false` | When enabled (with `multiple`), each option group label becomes a tri-state button: clicking it toggles the group's visible options, and it reflects `none` / `all` / `indeterminate` based on the group's selected options. |
| `optionsGroupsTemplate` | function, null | `null` | Custom template function for rendering option group labels. Receives the group object as parameter. |
| `optionsMaxHeight` | number, string | `'auto'` | Sets `max-height` of options list.	 |
| `optionsTemplate` | function, null | `null` | Custom template function for rendering individual options. Receives the option object as parameter. |
| `pickerIcon` | string, boolean | `true` | The button that toggles the options list: `true` for the built-in icon, an inline SVG string for your own (sanitized), `false` for no button. Clicking the control only opens the list, so without the button a pointer closes it by clicking away. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Select...'` | Specifies a short hint that is visible in the input. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Makes the input field required for form validation. |
| `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` | boolean | `false` | Empties the selection when `setOptions()` brings options with different values, then takes the options marked `selected`. For options that depend on another field. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Enables HTML sanitization for custom templates to prevent XSS attacks. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function, null | `null` | Custom sanitization function. If provided, it will be used instead of the built-in sanitizer. |
| `search` | boolean, string | `false` | Renders a search box in the control. `true` filters the options as the user types; `'external'` filters nothing and fires `search.coreui.multi-select`, which you answer with `setOptions()`. Any other string throws a `TypeError`. The box takes the focus when the panel opens, and typing anywhere in the component reaches it unless `globalSearch` is off. |
| `searchNoResultsLabel` | string | `'No results found'` | Sets the label for no results when filtering.	|
| `selectAll` | boolean | `true` | Enables select all button.|
| `selectAllLabel` | string | `'Select all'` | Sets the select all button label shown until everything is selected. The button is a toggle: it shows `selectAllLabel` (and selects all) until everything is selected, then shows `deselectAllLabel` (and deselects all). |
| `selectAllMode` | string | `'all'` | Scope of the built-in select all button: `'all'` toggles every option (ignoring the search filter), `'filtered'` toggles only the search-filtered options. With no active filter both behave the same. |
| `selectedLabel` | string, function | `` (count) => `${count} item(s) selected` `` | The counter selection label. A function `(count, total) => string`, or a string in which `{count}` and `{total}` are replaced; `total` is the number of options in the list, disabled ones and the ones inside a group included, so a disabled option shows that not everything is selected, plus any selected value the current options lack, so it never falls below `count`, unless the `total` option gives a number of its own. |
| `selectFilteredLabel` | string | `'Select filtered'` | Label shown instead of `selectAllLabel` when `selectAllMode: 'filtered'` and a search filter narrows the list, so the button reads as acting on the filtered options rather than the whole list. |
| `selectionLimit` | number, null | `null` | Sets the maximum number of selectable options. The select all button stays enabled and selects up to the limit (firing the `selectionLimit` event), then toggles to deselect all once the limit is reached. |
| `selectionType` | string | `'chips'` | Sets the selection style: `'chips'`, `'counter'` or `'text'`. `'chips'` renders the selection as [Chip](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/chip/) components. `'tags'` is a deprecated name for `'chips'`. |
| `total` | number, null | `null` | The `{total}` of `selectedLabel`. Leave it `null` to count the options in the list; with `search: 'external'` give the number of records your data source holds, which the component cannot see. |
| `valid` | boolean | `false` | Deprecated alias of `validationState: 'valid'`, ignored once `validationState` is set. |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The validation state the control shows: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` also blocks the submit. The next change of the selection by the user clears it, see [Validation](#validation). |
| `value` | string, number, array, null | `null` | Sets the initially selected values for the multi-select component; a string may list several values separated by commas. Given values win over options marked `selected`, in the markup or in `options`, and apply when the component starts or when `setValue()` gives them; `[]` selects nothing, and a value the options lack waits for them: options that `setOptions()` brings later for the first time are selected when the last given value lists them. Options shown before keep their state. A single select whose selection is empty holds its `value=""` placeholder option, or no option. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `deselectAll` | Deselects every selected option that is not disabled, including selected values the current options lack. Pass an array of options to deselect only those. |
| `deselectFiltered` | Deselect only the currently filtered (search-matched) options. |
| `dispose` | Destroys an element's multi select, removes the wrapper and panel it built, and gives the native select back the options it had before the component started, when the component replaced them. The native select stays hidden with the attributes the component wrote; a new instance writes them again from its options. (Removes stored data on the DOM element) |
| `getInstance` | Static method which allows you to get the multi select instance associated with a DOM element. |
| `getValue` | Returns the array with selected elements. |
| `hide` | Hides the multi select's options. |
| `selectAll` | Select all options. |
| `selectFiltered` | Select only the currently filtered (search-matched) options. |
| `setLoading` | Marks the list busy while you wait for options, for example with `search: 'external'`: a row with `loadingLabel` shows below the options and is announced, and the options it shows can still be picked. |
| `setOptions` | Replaces the options without rebuilding the control: the selection, an open panel and the search box keep their state, and the focus stays where it was unless the element holding it goes. A selected option the new list lacks stays selected and is still sent with the form unless it is disabled; `selected` flags in the new options are ignored unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` empties the selection first. |
| `disable()` | Disables the select. |
| `enable()` | Enables the select. |
| `setTotal(total)` | Sets the number of all results an external search has, for the counter. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the select a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setValue(value)` | Selects the options with the given values without firing a change event. |
| `show` | Shows the multi select's options. |

### Events

Multi Select component exposes a few events for hooking into multi select functionality.

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.multi-select` | Fires, with the native `input` and `change` of the select, once for every change of the selection the user or the component makes: a pick, `selectAll()`, `deselectAll()`, `setOptions()` emptying the selection for `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange`, and a native reset of the form that brings the initial selection back. It fires after the native select holds the new value; `event.value` is the selection. An action that selects or deselects several options sends one event, and an action that changes nothing sends none. A selection you give sends nothing: the start, `setValue()`, and a given `value` that options from `setOptions()` bring later, unless `resetSelectionOnOptionsChange` puts it in place of the selection. |
| `hidden.coreui.multi-select` | Fired when the multi select options have finished being hidden from the user and CSS transitions have completed. |
| `hide.coreui.multi-select` | Fires immediately when the hide instance method has been called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the menu open. |
| `search.coreui.multi-select` | Fires when the text of the search box changes, a paste included, and when `search()` gets a different text; `event.query` is the text. A key that leaves the text alone and opening or closing the panel over an empty box send nothing; closing the panel clears a filled box, which reports an empty `query`. With `search: 'external'` nothing is filtered, so answer with `setOptions()`. |
| `selectionLimit.coreui.multi-select` | Fires when selecting an option is blocked because the selection limit has been reached. |
| `show.coreui.multi-select` | Fires immediately when the show instance method is called. Call `event.preventDefault()` to keep the menu closed. |
| `shown.coreui.multi-select` | Fired when the multi select options have been made visible to the user and CSS transitions have completed. |

```js
const myMutliSelect = document.getElementById('myMutliSelect')
myMutliSelect.addEventListener('change.coreui.multi-select', event => {
  // Get the list of selected options.
  const selected = event.value
})
```

## Accessibility

The control takes its name from the select's `aria-labelledby`, then its `aria-label`, then a `<label>` pointing at the select. A `<label>` that wraps the select is left out, because its text would take in the control's own content and selection, so point the label at the select's `id` instead. The search box keeps a name of its own, `ariaSearchLabel`. When `required` is set, the control that takes the focus, the search box when `search` is on, carries `aria-required`; an `aria-required` on the select does not mark it. The native select itself is hidden from assistive technology.

The options panel is a dialog named like the control. Opening it moves the focus inside — onto the search box when `search` is on, otherwise onto the option the list points at, which is the selection the user left or the first option. The options are focusable one at a time: the arrows move the focus itself rather than a highlight read through `aria-activedescendant`. <kbd>Tab</kbd> cycles through what the panel offers and the search box in the control, and reaches nothing outside them until the panel closes, which <kbd>Escape</kbd> does, returning the focus to the control.

The select stays in the page as an invisible overlay for form validation and is hidden from screen readers, so the control speaks for it. The `aria-describedby` the select has when the component starts goes on the control, the search box when `search` is on, and while the state is invalid the control carries `aria-invalid` and is described by the message that follows it as well. Focus that reaches the select, from validation or from its label, goes on to the control. A change of selection fires `input` and `change` on the select, as a native list does, so a script that clears a field's error on input sees it.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between the search box, the select all button and the options list; the focus stays in the open panel |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd>/<kbd>Space</kbd> | Open the panel from the control, or select the focused option; <kbd>Enter</kbd> in the search box takes the option the list points at |
| <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd>/<kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Move through the options (and the selectable group labels), or enter the list from the search box |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Arrow Up</kbd>/<kbd>Arrow Down</kbd> | Extend the selection while moving (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> | Focus the first/last option (not while typing in the search box), or the first/last chip from a chip |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select every option the list shows, from the options list (multiple selection) |
| <kbd>Escape</kbd> | Close the panel and return the focus to the control |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd>/<kbd>Delete</kbd> | In the empty search box, focus the last chip; on a chip, remove it and move the focus to the next chip, else the previous one, else the search box, or the field when there is none. Entering the chips closes an open panel. A single select and the `counter` and `text` selections remove the last selected item at once |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd>/<kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | From the start of the search box, focus the last chip; between the chips, move the focus; past the last chip, return to the search box (mirrored in right-to-left) |

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The field is a [`.form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/#css-variables), so its frame, the cleaner and the toggle read the `--cui-control-*` and `--cui-control-group-*` tokens. The plugin renders that frame as a `.multi-select` element around your `<select>`: set the tokens with a rule on `.multi-select`, because a `style` attribute on the `<select>` does not reach the frame. The selected chips add two of their own:

```scss
$multi-select-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-multi-select-selection-chips-padding-y: .25rem,
  ),
  $multi-select-tokens
);
```

The options panel is the shared combobox surface, which only sizes itself:

```scss
$combobox-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-combobox-popup-min-width: 100%,
  ),
  $combobox-tokens
);
```

Its surface, border, shadow, stacking and fade come from the `.popup` tokens it shares with the pickers. `.popup` declares them itself, so set them on `.combobox-popup` or on `.popup`; a value set on an ancestor or on `:root` does not reach it.

```scss
$popup-tokens: () !default;
$popup-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-popup-zindex: var(--cui-z-dropdown),
    --cui-popup-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-popup-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-popup-border-color: var(--cui-border-color),
    --cui-popup-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-popup-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-popup-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-popup-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
  ),
  $popup-tokens
);
```

Everything inside it — options, section labels, checkbox indicators and the select all button — is a [List box](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/) and takes its `--cui-list-box-*` variables. `.list-box` declares them itself, so a value set on `.combobox-popup` or on `:root` does not reach it: set them with a rule on `.combobox-popup .list-box`, which covers the panels of Combobox, Autocomplete and Multi Select alike.


---

# Bootstrap 6 Number Input

> Add accessible increment and decrement buttons to a Bootstrap number field, with min, max and step handled by the browser.

# Number Input

A number field with a stepper you can actually hit. The browser's own spinner is
tiny, appears only on hover in some engines and does not exist at all on iOS, so
the component replaces it with two buttons sized like every other adornment in a
[`form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/).

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

Add `data-coreui-number-input` to an `<input type="number">`. The
component wraps it in a [`form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/) and
adds the buttons — you write neither the frame, the buttons nor their icons.

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" data-coreui-number-input>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="numberInputField" class="form-label">Quantity</label>
  <input type="number" class="form-control" id="numberInputField" value="3" data-coreui-number-input>
  <div class="form-text">Up to ten items per order.</div>
</div>
```

## Min, max and step

`min`, `max` and `step` are the native attributes — the component does not
reimplement them, it calls the browser's own stepping. **A button that cannot
move the value any further is disabled**, so the bound is visible rather than
just unresponsive. When a script changes these attributes later, the buttons
follow as described under [Disabled and read-only](#disabled-and-read-only).

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control" value="10" min="0" max="10" aria-label="Quantity" data-coreui-number-input>
```

A fractional `step` works the same way:

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control" value="2" step="0.5" aria-label="Amount" data-coreui-number-input>
```

When the field is empty, a button steps from zero, and the result stays within
`min` and `max` and on the `step` grid.

## Sizing

Write `.form-control-sm` or `.form-control-lg` on the input as you would on any
other control, and the buttons follow.

Sizing belongs to the frame rather than to the control inside it, so the
component moves the class onto the group it builds — and with it **every other
class you wrote except `.form-control` itself**. Spacing, width and the rest
describe the field as a whole, and the field is now the frame; leaving `mb-4`
on the input would put the margin inside the border.

State classes stay where you wrote them: `.is-valid`, `.is-invalid` and
anything else starting with `is-` or `was-`, plus `js-` hooks your own code
selects by. The frame picks the validation state up from the input, so
`document.querySelector('.form-control.is-invalid')` still finds the control
and a validator that toggles the class keeps working.

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control form-control-sm mb-4" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" data-coreui-number-input>
<input type="number" class="form-control form-control-lg" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" data-coreui-number-input>
```

## Disabled and read-only

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" disabled data-coreui-number-input>
```

```html
<input type="number" class="form-control" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" readonly data-coreui-number-input>
```

Both buttons are disabled while the field is `disabled` or `readonly`. When a
script changes either attribute, or `min`, `max` or `step`, later, the buttons
catch up as soon as the pointer moves over or presses the field, the field takes
focus or the user edits it. A press never steps a field it should not step, and
a touch on a button that still looks disabled brings it up to date first.

## Inside your own group

An input that is already in a `.form-control-group` is left where you put it, so
a number field can share a frame with anything else the group holds:

```html
<div class="form-control-group">
  <span class="form-control-icon">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512" fill="currentColor"><path d="M464 240H272V48h-32v192H48v32h192v192h32V272h192z"/></svg>
  </span>
  <input type="number" class="form-control" value="3" aria-label="Quantity" data-coreui-number-input>
</div>
```

## Floating labels

The number input supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/). Wrap the control in `.form-floating` and put a `<label>` beside it — the stepper buttons ride along with the field.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingNumberInput">Quantity</label>
  <input class="form-control" type="number" placeholder=" " id="floatingNumberInput" value="42" data-coreui-number-input>
</div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the wrapper, or to any ancestor, to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating).

## Accessibility

The buttons carry labels (`Increase` / `Decrease` by default, both
configurable) but are **kept out of the tab order**: a number field already
steps with <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd>, so putting them in would add two tab
stops per field for something the keyboard already reaches. A mouse press on a
button, enabled or not, puts the focus in the field rather than on the button,
so typing and the arrow keys act on the field you just stepped. Give the input an `aria-label` or a `<label>` as you would any other
field.

## Usage

Holding a button repeats after a short delay, and releasing it does not add a
step. Set `repeat: false` to require a click per step.

```js
const numberInput = new coreui.NumberInput('#myNumberInput', {
  repeat: false
})

numberInput.increment()
numberInput.decrement()
```

### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `SVGAllowlist` | Allowlist the icons are sanitized against. |
| `ariaDecrementLabel` | string | `'Decrease'` | Accessible label for the decrement button. |
| `ariaIncrementLabel` | string | `'Increase'` | Accessible label for the increment button. |
| `decrementIcon` | string | minus | Icon markup for the decrement button. |
| `incrementIcon` | string | plus | Icon markup for the increment button. |
| `repeat` | boolean | `true` | Repeat the step while a button is held. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize the icon markup. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function \| null | `null` | Your own sanitizer. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `decrement()` | Steps the value down by `step` (or by one, on a field without a numeric `step`), exactly as the decrement button does. |
| `dispose()` | Destroys the component instance, removes the increment/decrement buttons it created, and releases the field. |
| `getInstance(element)` | Static method that returns the instance associated with a DOM element, or `null`. |
| `getOrCreateInstance(element, config)` | Static method that returns the instance associated with a DOM element, creating it when there is none. |
| `increment()` | Steps the value up by `step` (or by one, on a field without a numeric `step`), exactly as the increment button does. |

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.number-input` | Fires after the value changes through a button, carrying the new `value`. |

The element also fires the native `input` and `change` events, so anything
already listening to the field keeps working.

> **Decimal separators.** `` accepts the dot as the decimal
> separator regardless of locale, and a value the browser rejects is reported as
> an empty string — the field cannot tell you what was typed. If you need
> locale-aware separators, currency or grouping, that is a formatted-input
> problem rather than a stepper one, and `type="number"` is the wrong base for
> it.

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The frame, the buttons and their sizing are the group's, and read the shared
`--cui-control-*` properties. Set them on the `.form-control-group` around the
input, the one you wrote or the one the plugin adds when there is none; a
`style` attribute on the `<input>` does not reach the frame:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

The group takes its own icon and action sizes per size class, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-control-group-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (icon-size: .875rem, action-size: 1.25rem),
    "lg": (icon-size: 1.25rem, action-size: 1.75rem),
  ),
  $form-control-group-sizes
);
```

## Validation

The code is validated as one value, kept in an input laid invisibly over the group. With `data-coreui-required="true"` an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit, and an incomplete code blocks it even when the field is not required; the browser, or the [form plugin](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/validation/#usage) in a form with `novalidate`, puts focus on the first empty slot, the browser with its own message over the group. The state shows on the group as `.is-{state}`, which colours every slot and shows the `.invalid-feedback` that follows the group, and while it is `'invalid'` every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by that message. Every change of the code sends `input` and `change` from the input that holds the value.

```html
<form class="row g-4" data-coreui-validate novalidate>
  <div class="col-12">
    <span class="form-label" id="otpValidationLabel">Verification code</span>
    <div class="form-otp" data-coreui-otp aria-labelledby="otpValidationLabel" data-coreui-name="code" data-coreui-required="true">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
      <input class="form-otp-control">
    </div>
    <div class="invalid-feedback">Enter the six digits we sent you.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="col-12">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Verify</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

The state comes from four places, in this order:

- The `validationState` option: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state you added to `$form-validation-states`.
- An `.is-invalid` or `.is-valid` class written on the `.form-otp` element or on a slot in the markup, for example by a server that has already checked the code. It is read once, when the component starts, and moves to the group, since the code is one value.
- A validation that reports the code invalid: a submit, `checkValidity()` or `reportValidity()`, which the form plugin and the [stepper](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/stepper/) call as well. From then on the group shows it invalid whenever the code is invalid, until a native reset of the form.
- In a form with `data-coreui-validate`, the `:user-invalid` state of the input that holds the value, and with `data-coreui-validate="valid"` also its `:user-valid` state.

A state you give, with the option or with the class, is a verdict on the code it was given for, so the next change of the code the user makes drops it: typing or deleting a character, a paste or an autofill. A keystroke that leaves the code as it was keeps it. One action drops the state once, at its first change, so a state you give from a `change.coreui.otp-input`, `input` or `change` listener while the action runs stays. A change your own code makes with `clear()`, `reset()` or `setValue()` keeps it. To set it again, call `setValidationState()`: it also replaces a class written in the markup, so `setValidationState(null)` withdraws that class. The component does not read `aria-invalid` on the group or a slot, and a state class written after it started only paints the group: the slots get no `aria-invalid` and the submit is not blocked, so change the state after start with `setValidationState()`. While the given state is `'invalid'`, the code blocks the submit with the text of the linked message, or `Invalid value.` when there is none; a disabled code does not block. A message placed where the stylesheet does not show it for the group can be named in `data-coreui-invalid-feedback` on the `.form-otp` element. A native reset of the form puts back the code the field started with and drops a state given before it; a state you give from a `reset` listener on the form, or right after `form.reset()`, stays.

```html
<span class="form-label" id="otpServerLabel">Verification code</span>
<div class="form-otp is-invalid" data-coreui-otp aria-labelledby="otpServerLabel" data-coreui-name="code" data-coreui-value="482910">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
</div>
<div class="invalid-feedback">This code has expired. Request a new one.</div>
```

## Accessibility

The one-time password input component is designed with accessibility in mind and follows WCAG guidelines for form inputs.

- **ARIA Labels**: Each input field automatically receives descriptive `aria-label` attributes
- **Label click**: clicking a label that names the field, through `aria-labelledby` or a `<label for>` pointing at the element, moves focus to the first empty slot, as clicking the label of an input focuses it.
- **Role Attribute**: The container has `role="group"` to indicate related form controls
- **Required**: with `data-coreui-required="true"`, every slot carries `aria-required="true"`, since the value input that holds `required` is hidden from assistive technologies
- **Keyboard Navigation**: Full keyboard support with arrow keys, tab, and backspace
- **Screen Reader Support**: Clear announcements when values change; while the state is `'invalid'`, every slot carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message after the group
- **Description**: an `aria-describedby` on the group moves to the first slot, and to every slot while the state is `'invalid'`, after the ids each slot already has; the group gets it back on dispose
- **Focus Management**: Automatic focus handling for seamless navigation
- **Autofill**: only the first field advertises `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so SMS autofill and password managers target a single field; a code delivered that way is spread across the slots automatically, exactly like a paste

### Customizing accessibility

You can customize the aria-label generation function to provide more specific descriptions:

```javascript
const otp = new coreui.OTPInput(element, {
  ariaLabel: (index, total) => `Enter digit ${index + 1} of your ${total}-digit verification code`
})
```

### Keyboard support

The one-time password input component provides comprehensive keyboard navigation support:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Arrow Right</kbd> | Move focus to next input field |
| <kbd>Arrow Left</kbd> | Move focus to previous input field |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Delete current character and move to previous field (if empty) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to next focusable element (respects linear mode) |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move to previous focusable element |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> | Paste clipboard content and auto-fill fields |

## Usage

### Via data attributes

The simplest way to use the one-time password input is through data attributes. Add `data-coreui-otp` to a container with `.form-otp` class containing `.form-otp-control` inputs.

```html
<div class="form-otp" data-coreui-otp data-coreui-name="code">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
  <input class="form-otp-control">
</div>
```

### Via JavaScript

Create one-time password inputs programmatically with JavaScript:

```javascript
const otpElement = document.querySelector('.form-otp')
const otp = new coreui.OTPInput(otpElement, {
  name: 'code',
  type: 'number',
  autoSubmit: true,
  linear: true,
  masked: false
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript. For data attributes, append the option name to `data-coreui-`, as in `data-coreui-type="number"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | function | `(index, total) => Digit ${index + 1} of ${total}` | Function to generate aria-label for each input field. Receives current index (0-based) and total number of inputs |
| `autoSubmit` | boolean | `false` | Automatically submit the form when all OTP fields are filled |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Disable all OTP input fields |
| `id` | string, null | `null` | ID attribute for the value input |
| `linear` | boolean | `true` | Enforce sequential input (users must fill fields in order) |
| `masked` | boolean | `false` | Show input as password (masked characters) |
| `name` | string, null | `null` | Name of the value input the code is submitted under. Without it the code is not submitted with the form. |
| `placeholder` | string, null | `null` | Placeholder text for input fields. Single character applies to all fields, longer strings apply character-by-character |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Makes the code required: an empty or incomplete code blocks the submit. |
| `type` | string | `'number'` | Input validation type: 'number' for digits only, or any other string for free text |
| `validationState` | string, null | `null` | The state the code shows: `'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state of `$form-validation-states`. `'invalid'` blocks the submit. The user's next change of the code drops it. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `value` | string, number, null | `null` | Value the slots start with. Characters the `type` does not accept are dropped, the same way typing and pasting drop them. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clear` | Clear all OTP input fields |
| `reset` | Puts back the code the input started with, its `value` or the code in the markup, as a native form reset does. |
| `disable()` | Disables the field. |
| `enable()` | Enables the field. |
| `setValidationState(state)` | Gives the field a validation state (`'valid'`, `'invalid'` or a state added to `$form-validation-states`), or drops it with `null`. The value stays. See [Validation](#validation). |
| `setValue(value)` | Sets the code. The slots show that value, cleared where it does not reach, and characters the `type` does not accept are dropped; the slots keep their attributes and the focus, and it fires no event. The slots are read when the field starts: to add or remove one, dispose the instance and create a new one. |

```javascript
const otp = coreui.OTPInput.getInstance(document.querySelector('.form-otp'))
otp.clear() // Clear all fields
otp.reset() // Reset to initial value
otp.setValue('123456') // Set the code
```

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.otp-input` | Fired when the code changes: typing, a paste, `clear()`, `reset()` or a native form reset, together with the native `input` and `change` of the hidden field. A call that leaves the code as it was, and `setValue()`, do not fire it. |
| `complete.coreui.otp-input` | Fired when all OTP fields are filled |

```javascript
document.addEventListener('change.coreui.otp-input', event => {
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('OTP value changed:', event.value)
})

document.addEventListener('complete.coreui.otp-input', event => {
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('OTP completed:', event.value)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Each cell is an input, so it carries the shared `--cui-control-*` tokens on `.form-otp-control` itself. Override them on a single OTP input to restyle just that one; to restyle every text control at once, set the `--cui-btn-input-*` frame on `:root` instead.

```scss
$form-otp-control-tokens: () !default;
$form-otp-control-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-padding-x: 0,
    --cui-form-otp-control-width: 2rem,
  ),
  $form-otp-control-tokens
);
```

```scss
$form-otp-tokens: () !default;
$form-otp-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-form-otp-gap: .125rem,
  ),
  $form-otp-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each size is one entry, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$form-otp-sizes: defaults(
  (
    "sm": (
      width:         1.5rem,
      padding-y:     var(--cui-btn-input-sm-padding-y),
      padding-x:     0,
      font-size:     var(--cui-btn-input-sm-font-size),
      border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    ),
    "lg": (
      width:         2.5rem,
      padding-y:     var(--cui-btn-input-lg-padding-y),
      padding-x:     0,
      font-size:     var(--cui-btn-input-lg-font-size),
      border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-lg-border-radius),
    ),
  ),
  $form-otp-sizes
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Password Input

> Enhance your password input fields in Bootstrap with custom styles, sizing options, toggle visibility button, and more.

## Example

Add `data-coreui-password-input` to a password field. The component
wraps it in a [`form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/) and adds the
toggle — you write neither the frame, the button nor its icon.

```html
<div class="mb-4">
  <label for="examplePasswordInput1" class="form-label">Password</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="examplePasswordInput1" placeholder="Enter your password" data-coreui-password-input>
</div>
<div class="mb-4">
  <label for="examplePasswordInput2" class="form-label">Password with value</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="examplePasswordInput2" placeholder="Enter your password" value="Top secret" data-coreui-password-input>
</div>
```

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="passwordInputField" class="form-label">Password</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="passwordInputField" placeholder="Enter your password" data-coreui-password-input>
  <div class="form-text">At least 12 characters.</div>
</div>
```

## Sizing variants

Bootstrap Password Input supports different sizes using Bootstrap's sizing utilities like `.form-control-lg` and `.form-control-sm`.

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control form-control-lg" placeholder="Large password input" data-coreui-password-input>
<input type="password" class="form-control" placeholder="Default password input" data-coreui-password-input>
<input type="password" class="form-control form-control-sm" placeholder="Small password input" data-coreui-password-input>
```

## Disabled

To make a Bootstrap Password Input non-interactive, add the `disabled` attribute to the `<input />`. The visibility toggle is disabled with it and leaves the tab order, so it can't change what a disabled field shows: a password revealed before stays visible, and can be hidden once the field is enabled again. A field you disable after init takes the toggle with it the first time the toggle is pressed or `toggle()` is called, which then changes nothing; a field you enable gives it back once the field takes focus. Inside a `<fieldset disabled>` the browser disables the toggle with the field.

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control" placeholder="Disabled password input" disabled data-coreui-password-input>
<input type="password" class="form-control" placeholder="Disabled and readonly input" disabled readonly data-coreui-password-input>
```

## Readonly state

Use the `readonly` attribute to make the input non-editable but still selectable. This is useful for displaying values without allowing user changes.

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control" placeholder="Readonly password input" value="Readonly input here..." readonly data-coreui-password-input>
```

## Floating labels

The password input supports [floating labels](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/). Wrap the control in `.form-floating` and put a `<label>` beside it — the toggle button rides along with the field, and the placeholder stays hidden until the label floats.

```html
<div class="form-floating">
  <label for="floatingPasswordInput">Password</label>
  <input class="form-control" type="password" placeholder=" " id="floatingPasswordInput" data-coreui-password-input>
</div>
```

Add `.form-floating-always` to the wrapper, or to any ancestor, to keep the label [always floating](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/floating-labels/#always-floating) with the placeholder showing.

## Usage

Add `data-coreui-password-input` to the field. The plugin initializes
on load, builds the frame and the toggle, and flips the input's type when the
button is pressed.

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control" placeholder="Enter your password" data-coreui-password-input>
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-aria-toggle-label="{value}"`. Remember to convert the case of the option name from "_camelCase_" to "_kebab-case_" when using data attributes.

Please note that for security reasons, the `sanitize`, `sanitizeFn`, and `allowList` options cannot be supplied via data attributes.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `SVGAllowlist` | Allowlist the icons are sanitized against. |
| `ariaToggleLabel` | string | `'Toggle password visibility'` | Accessible name of the show and hide button. The button carries no text, so this is the only name it has. |
| `hideIcon` | string | SVG | Icon markup shown while the password is visible, which is the button that hides it again. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize the icon markup. |
| `sanitizeFn` | function \| null | `null` | Your own sanitizer, used instead of the built-in one. |
| `showIcon` | string | SVG | Icon markup shown while the password is hidden. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose()` | Destroys the component instance, removes the toggle button and releases the field, putting back the `type` from the markup. |
| `getInstance(element)` | Static method that returns the instance associated with a DOM element, or `null`. |
| `getOrCreateInstance(element, config)` | Static method that returns the instance associated with a DOM element, creating it when there is none. |
| `toggle()` | Flips the field between `password` and `text`, exactly as the button does; on a disabled field it changes nothing and disables the button. |

```js
const passwordInput = coreui.PasswordInput.getOrCreateInstance(document.querySelector('[data-coreui-password-input]'))

passwordInput.toggle()
```

## Customizing

A password field is an `<input>` and a toggle button inside a
[`form-control-group`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/form-control-group/). Almost everything you would
want to change belongs to the group; what this component owns is the icon the
button shows.

### Icons

The plugin renders the icon and swaps it when the password becomes visible, as
inline SVG on `currentColor` — so it follows the button through hover, focus and
disabled without a colour of its own. Pass your own artwork to replace it:

```js
new coreui.PasswordInput('#myPasswordInput', {
  ariaToggleLabel: 'Show or hide the password',
  showIcon: '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">…</svg>',
  hideIcon: '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="currentColor">…</svg>'
})
```

Both are sanitized before they reach the DOM. To pass markup the default
allowlist rejects, extend `allowList`, supply your own `sanitizeFn`, or turn
`sanitize` off for content you control.

An input already inside a `.form-control-group` is left where you put it, so a
password field can share a frame with other adornments; only a frame the
component built is removed on `dispose()`. Classes you write on the input other
than `.form-control` move onto that frame, because they describe the field and
the field is the frame — except state classes (`is-*`, `was-*`) and `js-*`
hooks, which stay on the input so validators and your own selectors keep
finding it; the frame reads the state from the input.

### CSS variables

The frame — padding, colours, border and the size of the toggle button,
including the icon inside it — is the group's, and it reads the shared
`--cui-control-*` properties. Set them on `.form-control-group` to restyle one
field, since a `style` attribute on the `<input>` does not reach the frame; the
group declares them itself, so a value on `:root` stops there — to
restyle every field at once, change the shared
[`--cui-btn-input-*` frame](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/overview/#css-variables). The focus ring is
the library's own, coloured by `--cui-focus-ring-color` or the theme:

```scss
$form-control-group-tokens: () !default;
$form-control-group-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-control-group-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-control-group-icon-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-text-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-size: 1.5rem,
    --cui-control-group-action-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-control-group-action-bg: transparent,
    --cui-control-group-action-hover-bg: var(--cui-bg-1),
    --cui-control-group-action-border-radius: var(--cui-btn-input-sm-border-radius),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-property: #{var(--cui-btn-input-action-transition-property), transform},
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-duration: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-duration),
    --cui-control-group-action-transition-timing: var(--cui-btn-input-transition-timing),
    --cui-control-group-disabled-opacity: var(--cui-btn-input-disabled-opacity),
  ),
  $form-control-group-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Password Strength

> Show how strong a password is as it is typed — a segmented meter, a label, and a pluggable scorer that can be asynchronous so a real strength estimator or a breach check can drive it.

## Example

_Added in 6.0.0._

Point the component at a password field and it renders the meter, the label and
the feedback itself. You write one empty element.

```html
<label for="strengthDemo" class="form-label">Password</label>
<input type="password" class="form-control mb-3" id="strengthDemo" data-coreui-password-input placeholder="Type a password…">
<div data-coreui-password-strength data-coreui-input="#strengthDemo"></div>
```

## How it works

- **The field stays yours.** The meter never wraps, moves or re-types the input.
  It listens for `input` and `change` and renders next to it, which is what lets
  it sit alongside [Password Input](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/password-input/) — that component owns
  the field's frame and visibility toggle, and the two do not compete.
- **It does not care whether the password is visible.** Revealing the value
  switches the field's `type`, and the meter keeps scoring across the toggle in
  either direction — including when it is created while the password is already
  showing.
- **The meter is built for you.** It creates the segments, the label, and the
  places a scorer's warning and suggestions go. Segments are one fewer than
  there are levels, so the top level fills the bar.
- **The score is a number from 0 to 4.** Level `0` is the worst. That is the
  same scale [zxcvbn](#zxcvbn) returns, so a real estimator drops in without a
  conversion step.
- **The meter is hidden from assistive technology** (`aria-hidden`) because it
  only restates the label. The label and its feedback sit in a polite live
  region, so a screen reader hears the verdict once, not twice.

## What the built-in scorer is worth

> **The built-in scorer is a UX hint, not a security control.** It counts length
> and character classes — lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols. That measures
> *composition*, not how guessable a password actually is. `P@ssw0rd1` clears
> every rule it checks and is among the first passwords any attacker tries.
> 
> [NIST SP 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) recommends
> **against** composition rules of exactly this kind, and **for** checking the
> password against lists of known-breached secrets. Do that on the server, where
> it cannot be skipped. Treat this meter as encouragement while typing, and never
> as the thing that decides whether a password is allowed.

The default scorer stays small and rule-based on purpose: a real estimator ships
a dictionary far larger than this entire library. Plug one in with `scorer`.

## Custom scorer

`scorer` replaces the built-in scoring completely. It receives the password and
the [user inputs](#user-inputs), and returns either a bare number or an object:

```js
type StrengthResult = number | { score: number, warning?: string, suggestions?: string[] }
```

Return a number when that is all you have — the simple case stays simple:

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control mb-3" id="scorerDemo" data-coreui-password-input placeholder="Length alone decides…">
<div id="scorerMeter"></div>
```

Return an object to say *why*. The `warning` and `suggestions` are rendered
below the label, and both are inserted as text — markup in them is never parsed.

```js
new coreui.PasswordStrength('#meter', {
  input: '#password',
  scorer(password) {
    if (/^[a-z]+$/.test(password)) {
      return {
        score: 1,
        warning: 'Letters only is easy to guess.',
        suggestions: ['Add a digit or a symbol.', 'Use several unrelated words.']
      }
    }

    return { score: 3 }
  }
})
```

A score outside the range of `levels` is clamped, and a scorer that throws
clears the meter rather than leaving a stale verdict on screen.

### Asynchronous scorers

`scorer` may return a promise. This is what makes a serious estimator possible:
zxcvbn loads its language packs asynchronously, and a breach check is a network
call. Both are impossible against a synchronous contract.

Three things the component handles so you do not have to:

- **Debounce.** Input is coalesced (`debounce`, 200 ms by default) so typing a
  password does not fire a request per keystroke.
- **Out-of-order results.** Every evaluation takes a sequence token. If a slow
  answer for an old password arrives after a newer one has already resolved, it
  is discarded. Without this, pausing mid-word and typing on can leave the meter
  showing the verdict for a prefix.
- **A pending state.** While a promise is outstanding the root gets
  `.password-strength-busy` and the label shows `busyLabel`. A synchronous
  scorer never gets this state, so it cannot flicker.

A rejected promise clears the meter, for the same reason a throw does.

> **A scorer that calls the network sends the password off the page.** Anything
> you `fetch` from inside `scorer` receives the secret the user is in the middle
> of typing — before they have submitted anything, and on every debounce tick.
> 
> If you check against a breach corpus, use a protocol built for it: the
> [Pwned Passwords range API](https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3#PwnedPasswords)
> takes the first five characters of the password's SHA-1 hash and returns every
> matching suffix, so the password itself never leaves the browser. Sending the
> raw password to a third party is a credential disclosure, whatever the endpoint
> promises.

### zxcvbn

[zxcvbn](https://github.com/dropbox/zxcvbn) and its maintained successor
[zxcvbn-ts](https://github.com/zxcvbn-ts/zxcvbn) estimate how many guesses a
password would survive, using dictionaries of common passwords, names, words and
keyboard patterns. That is a different question from "does it have a capital
letter", and a much more useful one.

We do not ship an adapter — the shapes already line up. zxcvbn returns
`{ score, feedback: { warning, suggestions } }`, and `score` is 0–4 on the same
scale this component uses:

```js
import { zxcvbn, zxcvbnOptions } from '@zxcvbn-ts/core'
import * as common from '@zxcvbn-ts/language-common'
import * as en from '@zxcvbn-ts/language-en'

zxcvbnOptions.setOptions({
  dictionary: { ...common.dictionary, ...en.dictionary },
  graphs: common.adjacencyGraphs,
  translations: en.translations
})

new coreui.PasswordStrength('#meter', {
  input: '#password',
  userInputs: () => [
    document.getElementById('email').value,
    document.getElementById('username').value
  ],
  scorer(password, userInputs) {
    const { score, feedback } = zxcvbn(password, userInputs)

    return { score, warning: feedback.warning, suggestions: feedback.suggestions }
  }
})
```

The language packs are large. Load them on demand and let the promise support do
the waiting — the meter shows its pending state until the pack has arrived:

```js
let zxcvbnReady = null

const loadZxcvbn = () => {
  zxcvbnReady ||= Promise.all([
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/core'),
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/language-common'),
    import('@zxcvbn-ts/language-en')
  ]).then(([core, common, en]) => {
    core.zxcvbnOptions.setOptions({
      dictionary: { ...common.dictionary, ...en.dictionary },
      graphs: common.adjacencyGraphs,
      translations: en.translations
    })

    return core.zxcvbn
  })

  return zxcvbnReady
}

new coreui.PasswordStrength('#meter', {
  input: '#password',
  async scorer(password, userInputs) {
    const zxcvbn = await loadZxcvbn()
    const { score, feedback } = zxcvbn(password, userInputs)

    return { score, warning: feedback.warning, suggestions: feedback.suggestions }
  }
})
```

Both run entirely in the browser, so neither sends the password anywhere.

## User inputs

A password containing the user's own email, username or site name is weak no
matter how it is composed, and no amount of character-class counting notices
that. `userInputs` is the list to penalize against.

Pass a function when the values live in fields the user is still filling in — it
is called on every evaluation, so it always sees current values. Pass an array
when they are fixed.

```html
<input type="text" class="form-control mb-3" id="userEmail" value="ada@example.com">
<input type="password" class="form-control mb-3" id="userPassword" data-coreui-password-input placeholder="Try using the email above…">
<div id="userInputsMeter"></div>
```

The built-in scorer returns `0` when the password contains any of these values
(three characters or more, case-insensitive). A custom scorer receives the same
list as its second argument and decides for itself — zxcvbn takes it directly.

## With form field

Wrap the control in [`.form-field`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/forms/field/) to lay it out with its label and description, and to get validation feedback in the right place. The meter is a child of the field like any other, so it picks up the same gap.

```html
<div class="form-field">
  <label for="strengthField" class="form-label">Password</label>
  <input type="password" class="form-control" id="strengthField" data-coreui-password-input placeholder="Type a password…">
  <div data-coreui-password-strength data-coreui-input="#strengthField"></div>
  <div class="form-text">At least 12 characters.</div>
</div>
```

## Without JavaScript

The meter is driven entirely by two hooks, so a server that already knows the
score can render the result without loading the plugin: `data-coreui-strength`
on the wrapper picks the colour, and `.active` on a segment fills it.

The score runs `0`–`4` and there is one segment fewer than there are levels —
four segments for the five default labels.

```html
<div class="password-strength" data-coreui-strength="2">
  <div class="password-strength-meter" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="password-strength-segment active"></span>
    <span class="password-strength-segment active"></span>
    <span class="password-strength-segment"></span>
    <span class="password-strength-segment"></span>
  </div>
  <div class="password-strength-feedback" role="status">
    <span class="password-strength-text">Fair</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

This is the same markup the plugin builds, so a field can start server-rendered
and keep working once the script initializes it.

## Accessibility

- The segmented bar is `aria-hidden`, because it carries no information the
  label does not.
- The label, warning and suggestions share one `role="status"` region with
  `aria-live="polite"`, so the verdict is announced without interrupting, and as
  a single message rather than three.
- Debouncing keeps that region from being updated on every keystroke, which is
  what makes a live region usable here at all.
- The strength label is never the only signal — it is text, not colour alone.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-password-strength` to an empty element and point it at
a field with `data-coreui-input`. Without `data-coreui-input`, the component uses
the first `input[type="password"]` inside its parent, or the first input marked
`data-coreui-password-input` — the second is what keeps the pairing
working while the password is revealed and the field's `type` is `text`.

```html
<input type="password" class="form-control" id="password" data-coreui-password-input>
<div data-coreui-password-strength data-coreui-input="#password"></div>
```

### Via JavaScript

```js
const meter = new coreui.PasswordStrength('#meter', {
  input: '#password'
})
```

### Options

Options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript. For data attributes, append the option name to `data-coreui-`, as in `data-coreui-debounce="500"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `busyLabel` | string | `'Checking…'` | Label shown while an asynchronous scorer is pending. |
| `debounce` | number | `200` | Milliseconds to wait after typing stops before scoring. `0` scores on every input event. |
| `input` | string, element, null | `null` | Selector or element of the password field. When `null`, the first `input[type="password"]` or `input[data-coreui-password-input]` in the parent is used. |
| `levels` | array | `['Very weak', 'Weak', 'Fair', 'Good', 'Strong']` | Labels by score. The meter renders one segment fewer than there are levels, and a score above the last label is clamped to it. |
| `minLength` | number | `8` | Length the built-in scorer treats as the first threshold. Ignored when `scorer` is set. |
| `scorer` | function, null | `null` | `(password, userInputs) => StrengthResult \| Promise<StrengthResult>`. Replaces the built-in scoring. |
| `thresholds` | array | `[2, 4, 6]` | Point boundaries the built-in scorer maps to scores 1–4. A boundary you leave out, or set to something that is not a number, keeps its default, so a partial array has to ascend past the defaults it keeps. Ignored when `scorer` is set. |
| `userInputs` | array, function | `[]` | Values to penalize a password for containing, or a function returning them. |
| `weights` | object | see below | Points the built-in scorer awards per rule. Ignored when `scorer` is set. |

Each key in `weights` is one rule the built-in scorer checks, and its value is what a pass is worth. Set a rule to `0` to stop it counting — useful when a policy does not ask for that class of character and a meter demanding it would only mislead. Raise a value to make one rule outweigh the others.

| Rule | Passes when the password |
| --- | --- |
| `minLength` | reaches `minLength` characters |
| `extraLength` | reaches `minLength` + 4 |
| `longPassword` | reaches 16 |
| `lowercase` / `uppercase` / `numbers` | contains one |
| `special` | contains a symbol |
| `multipleSpecial` | contains two or more symbols |

Every rule defaults to `1`, so out of the box the score is a count of rules passed, measured against `thresholds`. A rule you leave out of `weights`, or set to something that is not a number, keeps its default, so the object above is a set of overrides rather than a replacement.

```js
// Do not ask for an uppercase letter, and reward real length instead
new coreui.PasswordStrength(element, {
  weights: { uppercase: 0, longPassword: 3 }
})
```

Three of the eight rules measure length and two measure symbols, so a short password dense with symbols can outscore a long passphrase. That is the composition problem the callout above describes; `scorer` is the way out of it, not these numbers.

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Destroys the instance and removes the meter and the feedback it created. |
| `evaluate` | Scores the current value immediately, skipping the debounce. |
| `getInstance` | Static method to get the instance associated with a DOM element. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | Static method to get the instance associated with a DOM element, or create a new one if it was not initialized. |
| `getScore` | Returns the current score, or `null` when there is none. |

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.password-strength` | Fires when the score changes — not on every keystroke. |

The event carries `score`, `level` (the label for that score), and `password`,
which is `'***'` for any non-empty value. The real password is never put on an
event, because a listener anywhere on the page could read it.

```js
const meter = document.getElementById('meter')

meter.addEventListener('change.coreui.password-strength', event => {
  console.log(event.score, event.level)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The component reads these from `.password-strength`. The level colour is one
token, reassigned per score, so restyling the scale is five declarations:

```scss
$password-strength-tokens: () !default;
$password-strength-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-password-strength-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-password-strength-meter-gap: .25rem,
    --cui-password-strength-segment-height: .25rem,
    --cui-password-strength-segment-bg: var(--cui-bg-2),
    --cui-password-strength-segment-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-pill),
    --cui-password-strength-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-password-strength-text-font-weight: 600,
    --cui-password-strength-warning-color: var(--cui-fg-2),
    --cui-password-strength-suggestions-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-password-strength-busy-opacity: .65,
    --cui-password-strength-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
  ),
  $password-strength-tokens
);
```

Colour by score:

```scss
// stylelint-disable-next-line scss/dollar-variable-default
$password-strength-levels: defaults(
  (
    "0": var(--cui-danger-base),
    "1": var(--cui-danger-base),
    "2": var(--cui-warning-base),
    "3": var(--cui-info-base),
    "4": var(--cui-success-base),
  ),
  $password-strength-levels
);
```
