# Bootstrap 6 Context Menu

> The Context Menu component opens a menu at the pointer on right-click, long-press or the keyboard's Menu key - built on the Menu engine with the same items, submenus, keyboard navigation and dismissal.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

Context menus replace the browser's native menu on an element with a [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/). Add `data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"` to any element and place a `.menu` next to it: a right-click (or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> / the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key when the element has focus) opens it at the pointer, and every menu feature - items, icons, dividers, headers, submenus and the keyboard navigation - works unchanged.

```html
<div class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu">
  Right-click anywhere in this area
</div>
<div class="menu">
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-icon fg-3" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
      <path fill-rule="evenodd" d="M4 2a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v8a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H6a2 2 0 0 1-2-2zm2-1a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v8a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h8a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V2a1 1 0 0 0-1-1zM2 5a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v8a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h8a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-1h1v1a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H2a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V6a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h1v1z"/>
    </svg>
    Copy
  </button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-icon fg-3" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
      <path d="M3.5 3.5c-.614-.884-.074-1.962.858-2.5L8 7.226 11.642 1c.932.538 1.472 1.616.858 2.5L8.81 8.61l1.556 2.661a2.5 2.5 0 1 1-.794.637L8 9.73l-1.572 2.177a2.5 2.5 0 1 1-.794-.637L7.19 8.61zm2.5 10a1.5 1.5 0 1 0-3 0 1.5 1.5 0 0 0 3 0m7 0a1.5 1.5 0 1 0-3 0 1.5 1.5 0 0 0 3 0"/>
    </svg>
    Cut
  </button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Paste</button>
  <hr class="menu-divider">
  <button class="menu-item theme-danger" type="button">
    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
      <path d="M6.5 1h3a.5.5 0 0 1 .5.5v1H6v-1a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5M11 2.5v-1A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 9.5 0h-3A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5 1.5v1H1.5a.5.5 0 0 0 0 1h.538l.853 10.66A2 2 0 0 0 4.885 16h6.23a2 2 0 0 0 1.994-1.84l.853-10.66h.538a.5.5 0 0 0 0-1zm1.958 1-.846 10.58a1 1 0 0 1-.997.92h-6.23a1 1 0 0 1-.997-.92L3.042 3.5zm-7.487 1a.5.5 0 0 1 .528.47l.5 8.5a.5.5 0 0 1-.998.06L5 5.03a.5.5 0 0 1 .47-.53Zm5.058 0a.5.5 0 0 1 .47.53l-.5 8.5a.5.5 0 1 1-.998-.06l.5-8.5a.5.5 0 0 1 .528-.47M8 4.5a.5.5 0 0 1 .5.5v8.5a.5.5 0 0 1-1 0V5a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5"/>
    </svg>
    Delete
  </button>
</div>
```

Context menus are built on a third party library, [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/), which keeps the menu inside the viewport: it flips above the pointer near the bottom edge and shifts sideways near the right one. Use `coreui.bundle.min.js` / `coreui.bundle.js` which includes Floating UI, or include Floating UI separately via an [import map](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#using-coreui-for-bootstrap-as-a-module).

## Examples

### Submenus

Submenus work as in [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/#submenus): wrap a `.menu-item` trigger and a nested `.menu` in a `.submenu`.

```html
<div class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu">
  Right-click to see the submenus
</div>
<div class="menu">
  <div class="submenu">
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">New</button>
    <div class="menu">
      <button class="menu-item" type="button">Folder</button>
      <button class="menu-item" type="button">Text document</button>
      <button class="menu-item" type="button">Spreadsheet</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="submenu">
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">Sort by</button>
    <div class="menu">
      <button class="menu-item selected" type="button">Name <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-check" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M13.485 1.431a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 2.121 2.121l-8.5 8.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-2.121 0l-4-4a1.5 1.5 0 1 1 2.121-2.121L6.5 9.324l6.985-6.893z"/></svg></button>
      <button class="menu-item" type="button">Date modified <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-check" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M13.485 1.431a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 2.121 2.121l-8.5 8.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-2.121 0l-4-4a1.5 1.5 0 1 1 2.121-2.121L6.5 9.324l6.985-6.893z"/></svg></button>
      <button class="menu-item" type="button">Size <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" fill="currentColor" class="menu-item-check" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M13.485 1.431a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 2.121 2.121l-8.5 8.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-2.121 0l-4-4a1.5 1.5 0 1 1 2.121-2.121L6.5 9.324l6.985-6.893z"/></svg></button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <hr class="menu-divider">
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Refresh</button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Properties</button>
</div>
```

### One menu for many rows

A context menu belongs to the element that carries `data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"`, and it opens for right-clicks anywhere inside that element. Put the attribute on the container - a table, a list, a file grid - rather than on every row, and read `contextmenuEvent.target` in the `show.coreui.context-menu` event to learn which row was clicked. One menu, one instance, no matter how many rows.

```html
<table class="table table-hover" id="contextMenuTable" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">Name</th>
      <th scope="col">Modified</th>
      <th scope="col">Size</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr data-name="Quarterly report.pdf">
      <td>Quarterly report.pdf</td>
      <td>2 hours ago</td>
      <td>1.2 MB</td>
    </tr>
    <tr data-name="Logo.svg">
      <td>Logo.svg</td>
      <td>Yesterday</td>
      <td>24 KB</td>
    </tr>
    <tr data-name="Notes.txt">
      <td>Notes.txt</td>
      <td>3 days ago</td>
      <td>2 KB</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<div class="menu" id="contextMenuTableMenu">
  <h6 class="menu-header">File</h6>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Open</button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Rename</button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Download</button>
  <hr class="menu-divider">
  <button class="menu-item theme-danger" type="button">Delete</button>
</div>
```

```js
const table = document.getElementById('contextMenuTable')
const header = document.querySelector('#contextMenuTableMenu .menu-header')

table.addEventListener('show.coreui.context-menu', event => {
  const row = event.contextmenuEvent?.target.closest('tbody tr')
  if (!row) {
    event.preventDefault()
    return
  }

  header.textContent = row.dataset.name
})
```

Preventing the `show` event keeps the browser's own menu away too - the right-click on the header row above opens nothing.

### Menu elsewhere in the DOM

By default the plugin looks for the `.menu` next to the trigger. Point `data-coreui-target` at it when the menu lives elsewhere, for example one menu shared by several independent areas.

```html
<div class="border rounded-3 p-5 flex-fill text-center fg-2" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu" data-coreui-target="#sharedContextMenu">
  Area one
</div>
<div class="border rounded-3 p-5 flex-fill text-center fg-2" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu" data-coreui-target="#sharedContextMenu">
  Area two
</div>
<div class="menu" id="sharedContextMenu">
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Action</button>
  <button class="menu-item" type="button">Another action</button>
</div>
```

### Container

The menu is positioned with `position: fixed` at the pointer, so it escapes ancestors with `overflow: hidden` on its own. A `transform`, `filter` or `contain` on an ancestor turns that ancestor into the containing block for fixed elements and the menu drifts; append it to the body with `data-coreui-container="body"` in that case. The menu returns to its original place when hidden.

```html
<div class="border rounded-3 p-6 text-center fg-2 overflow-hidden" style="transform: translateZ(0)" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="context-menu" data-coreui-container="body">
  Right-click inside a transformed, clipping container
  <div class="menu">
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">Still in the viewport</button>
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">Another action</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

Pointing devices are not the only way in: with focus on the trigger, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> and the <kbd>Menu</kbd> key open the menu anchored to the element instead of the pointer. <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> is the Windows convention the [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) adopt for opening a context menu from the keyboard; the plugin handles the keys itself, so they work on macOS too, where no system shortcut exists and browsers never turn them into a `contextmenu` event. On Apple keyboards the function keys default to their media actions, so the shortcut is <kbd>Fn</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> unless the system is set to use them as standard function keys. Give a non-interactive trigger `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can reach it, and describe the gesture somewhere nearby - nothing in the markup announces that an element has a context menu.

Focus moves into the menu when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes. Like [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/#accessibility), the plugin adds no `role="menu"`/`menuitem` attributes on its own; add them yourself when the menu is a true application menu.

### Keyboard navigation

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>, <kbd>Menu</kbd> | Open the context menu anchored to the focused trigger (<kbd>Fn</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> on Apple keyboards) |
| `↓` / `↑` | Navigate to next/previous menu item |
| `→` | Enter submenu (or `←` in RTL) |
| `←` | Exit submenu and return to parent (or `→` in RTL) |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Activate focused item or open submenu |
| `Esc` | Close the menu and return focus to the trigger |
| `Home` / `End` | Jump to first/last menu item |
| `Tab` | Move focus and close the menu |

## Usage

The plugin listens on the document: a `contextmenu` event (a right-click, or a long-press on touch devices that dispatch it) or a <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd> / <kbd>Menu</kbd> keydown inside an element with `data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"` opens its `.menu` and suppresses the browser menu. A right-click inside the open menu keeps it open; one elsewhere closes it, and so does a left-click anywhere outside the menu (the trigger area included), <kbd>Esc</kbd> or tabbing out. While the menu is open the page does not scroll - wheel, touch and the scroll keys are held, as with the native menu - but a `.menu-scrollable` still scrolls inside.

> iOS Safari does not dispatch `contextmenu` for a long-press. Call `show()` yourself from a `touchstart`/`pointerdown` timer when the gesture matters on iOS.

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"` to the element that should own the menu and place the `.menu` right after it (or point at it with `data-coreui-target`).

| Attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"` | Initializes the context menu on the element and wires the `contextmenu` listener. |
| `data-coreui-target` | Selector of the `.menu` to open when it isn't a sibling of the trigger. |

```html
<div data-coreui-toggle="context-menu">
  Right-click here
</div>
<div class="menu">
  ...
</div>
```

### Via JavaScript

Call the context menus via JavaScript:

```js
const contextMenuElementList = document.querySelectorAll('[data-coreui-toggle="context-menu"]')
const contextMenuList = [...contextMenuElementList].map(element => new coreui.ContextMenu(element))
```

To open the menu at a point, pass viewport coordinates to `show()`; without a point the menu anchors to the trigger element:

```js
const contextMenu = coreui.ContextMenu.getOrCreateInstance('#myArea')

contextMenu.show({ x: 240, y: 120 })
contextMenu.show()
contextMenu.hide()
```

### Options

The context menu accepts every [Menu option](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/#options). Two defaults differ.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoClose` | boolean, string | `true` | Configure the auto close behavior of the menu: <ul class="my-3"><li>`true` - the menu will be closed by clicking outside or inside the menu. A click on the trigger area counts as outside.</li><li>`false` - the menu will be closed by manually calling `hide` or `toggle` method. (Also will not be closed by pressing <kbd>Esc</kbd> key)</li><li>`'inside'` - the menu will be closed (only) by clicking inside the menu.</li> <li>`'outside'` - the menu will be closed (only) by clicking outside the menu.</li></ul> A right-click elsewhere closes the menu under the same rules as a left-click outside. |
| `boundary` | string, element | `'clippingParents'` | Overflow constraint boundary of the menu (applies only to the shift middleware). By default it's `clippingParents` and can accept an HTMLElement reference (via JavaScript only). For more information refer to Floating UI's [shift docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/shift). |
| `container` | string, element, boolean | `false` | Appends the menu to a specific element when shown. Use `'body'` or `true` to append to the document body, which helps escape ancestors that act as a containing block for fixed elements. The menu is moved back to its original position when hidden. Inside a modal dialog it goes into the dialog instead, because the rest of the page is inert. |
| `display` | string | `'dynamic'` | By default, we use Floating UI for dynamic positioning. Disable this with `static`. |
| `floatingConfig` | null, object, function | `null` | To change the default Floating UI config, see [Floating UI's configuration](https://floating-ui.com/docs/computePosition). When a function is used to create the Floating UI configuration, it's called with an object that contains the default Floating UI configuration. It helps you use and merge the default with your own configuration. The function must return a configuration object for Floating UI. |
| `menu` | null, element | `null` | The `.menu` to open (JavaScript only). By default the plugin takes the element `data-coreui-target` points at, or a `.menu` next to the trigger. |
| `offset` | array, string, function | `[0, 2]` | Offset of the menu relative to the pointer. You can pass a string in data attributes with comma separated values like: `data-coreui-offset="10,20"`. When a function is used to determine the offset, it is called with an object containing the placement, the reference, and floating rects as its first argument. The triggering element DOM node is passed as the second argument. The function must return an array with two numbers: [skidding, distance]. For more information refer to Floating UI's [offset docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/offset). |
| `placement` | string | `'bottom-start'` | Placement of the menu relative to the pointer. Physical placements: `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'left'`, `'right'`. Logical placements (RTL-aware): `'start'`, `'end'`. All support alignment modifiers: `-start`, `-end`. Supports responsive prefixes like `'bottom-start md:end'`. |
| `reference` | string, element, object | `'pointer'` | What the menu is positioned against. `'pointer'` opens it at the right-click point (falling back to the trigger for keyboard invocation); `'toggle'` and `'parent'` anchor it to the trigger element or its parent regardless of the pointer; an HTMLElement or an object providing `getBoundingClientRect` anchors it elsewhere. For more information refer to Floating UI's [virtual elements docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/virtual-elements). |
| `strategy` | string | `'fixed'` | Positioning strategy for the menu. `'fixed'` places it in viewport coordinates, which is what the pointer position is; use `'absolute'` only when anchoring to an element inside a scrolling container. For more information refer to Floating UI's [strategy docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/computePosition#strategy). |
| `submenuDelay` | number | `100` | Delay in milliseconds before closing a submenu when the mouse leaves. Provides a grace period for diagonal mouse movement toward the submenu. |
| `submenuTrigger` | string | `'both'` | How submenus are triggered. Use `'click'` for click only, `'hover'` for hover only, or `'both'` for both click and hover activation. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Destroys an element's context menu. (Removes stored data on the DOM element) |
| `getInstance` | Static method which allows you to get the context menu instance associated to a DOM element, you can use it like this: `coreui.ContextMenu.getInstance(element)`. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | Static method which returns a context menu instance associated to a DOM element or create a new one in case it wasn't initialized. You can use it like this: `coreui.ContextMenu.getOrCreateInstance(element)`. |
| `hide` | Hides the menu and returns focus to the trigger when the menu had it. |
| `show` | Shows the menu. Accepts an optional `{ x, y }` point in viewport coordinates; without it the menu anchors to the trigger element. |
| `toggle` | Toggles the menu. Accepts the same optional point as `show`. |
| `update` | Updates the position of the menu. |

### Events

All context menu events are fired at the trigger element and then bubbled up. `show.coreui.context-menu` and `shown.coreui.context-menu` carry a `contextmenuEvent` property when the menu was opened by the data API - the native `contextmenu` event, whose `target` is the element under the pointer. `hide.coreui.context-menu` and `hidden.coreui.context-menu` carry a `clickEvent` property when a click closed the menu.

| Event type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden.coreui.context-menu` | Fired when the menu has finished being hidden from the user and CSS transitions have completed. |
| `hide.coreui.context-menu` | Fires immediately when the `hide` instance method has been called. |
| `show.coreui.context-menu` | Fires immediately when the `show` instance method is called. Calling `preventDefault()` keeps the menu closed and still suppresses the browser's own menu. |
| `shown.coreui.context-menu` | Fired when the menu has been made visible to the user and CSS transitions have completed. |

```js
const myArea = document.getElementById('myArea')
myArea.addEventListener('show.coreui.context-menu', event => {
  // event.contextmenuEvent.target is the element that was right-clicked
})
```

## Customizing

The menu a context menu opens is a regular `.menu`, so it is styled by the [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/#customizing) tokens.

---

# Bootstrap Dialog

> Bootstrap Dialog component built on the native <dialog> element — top layer rendering, blurred native backdrop, focus trapping, and accessible semantics out of the box.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

The Dialog component renders popups on the browser's native `<dialog>` element, providing built-in accessibility, focus management, and backdrop handling without the complexity of custom implementations. It follows the design Bootstrap 6 introduces under the same name — a centered floating panel over a blurred backdrop.

Dialog shares its base behavior with [Modal](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/modal/). Modal keeps the classic modal look and the v5 vocabulary; Dialog carries the new Bootstrap 6 look and the `dialog-*` classes. Pick one — they are independent components.

Key features of the native dialog:

- **Modal or non-modal** via `showModal()` / `show()` — `modal: true` (default) promotes the dialog to the browser's top layer with a backdrop and focus trapping; `modal: false` renders it non-modally, leaving the page interactive.
- **Built-in backdrop** using the `::backdrop` pseudo-element, with a blur effect; set `backdrop: "static"` to lock clicks outside, or `backdrop: false` to visually suppress it.
- **Escape key handling** closes the dialog by default; set `keyboard: false` to disable.
- **Accessibility** — focus is trapped inside modal dialogs and returned to the trigger on close, with native `<dialog>` ARIA semantics: no `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-hidden`, or `tabindex` attributes in the markup.
- **Animated open and close** — the exit transition (including the `::backdrop` fade) plays in every browser, because the plugin keeps the dialog in the top layer until the transition ends.

## Example

Toggle a dialog by clicking the button below.

<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialog" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogLabel">Dialog title</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>This is a native dialog element. It uses the browser's built-in modal behavior for accessibility and focus management.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog">Close</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Save changes</button>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" data-coreui-toggle="dialog" data-coreui-target="#exampleDialog">
  Open dialog
</button>

<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialog" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogLabel">Dialog title</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>This is a native dialog element.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog">Close</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Save changes</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Slide animations

Dialogs fade in and out by default. Add `.dialog-slide-down` to slide in from above, or `.dialog-slide-up` to slide in from below — the exit reverses the entry.

<dialog class="dialog dialog-slide-down" id="exampleDialogSlideDown" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogSlideDownLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogSlideDownLabel">Slide down</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>This dialog slides in from above.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

<dialog class="dialog dialog-slide-up" id="exampleDialogSlideUp" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogSlideUpLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogSlideUpLabel">Slide up</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>This dialog slides in from below.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog dialog-slide-down">...</dialog>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-slide-up">...</dialog>
```

To disable animation entirely, add `.dialog-instant`.

## Static backdrop

When backdrop is set to `static`, the dialog will not close when clicking outside of it — it plays a scale "bounce" instead.

<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialogStatic" data-coreui-backdrop="static" data-coreui-keyboard="false" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogStaticLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogStaticLabel">Dialog title</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>I will not close if you click outside of me. Don't even try to press escape key.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog">Close</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Understood</button>
  </div>
</dialog>

## Backdrop

The backdrop reads three tokens from `:root` — `--cui-backdrop-color`, `--cui-backdrop-opacity` and `--cui-backdrop-blur` — and every overlay component paints it the same way. A dialog defaults to a dark scrim; the drawer defaults to a translucent tint of the page. Pick the other look with a [backdrop preset](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/helpers/backdrop/) on the element: `.backdrop-translucent` here, `.backdrop-scrim` on a drawer, `.backdrop-none` on either.

<dialog class="dialog backdrop-translucent" id="exampleDialogTranslucent" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogTranslucentLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogTranslucentLabel">Translucent backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>The page behind stays readable through a light tint instead of a dark scrim.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog backdrop-translucent" id="exampleDialogTranslucent" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogTranslucentLabel">
  …
</dialog>
```

## Scrolling long content

Add `.dialog-scrollable` — the header and footer stay fixed while the dialog body scrolls.

<dialog class="dialog dialog-scrollable" id="exampleDialogScrollable" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogScrollableLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogScrollableLabel">Dialog title</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>This is some placeholder content to show the scrolling behavior for dialogs. We use repeated line breaks to demonstrate how content can exceed minimum inner height, thereby showing inner scrolling.</p>
    <br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br /><br />
    <p>This content should appear at the bottom after you scroll.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog">Close</button>
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary">Save changes</button>

```html
<dialog class="dialog dialog-scrollable">
  ...

```

## Toggle between dialogs

When a trigger sits inside an open dialog, the component swaps to the target dialog seamlessly — the backdrop stays up without flashing. The swap fires `show.coreui.dialog` on the target and `hide.coreui.dialog` on the open dialog before it changes either one; when a handler cancels either event, or one of the two dialogs is still opening or closing, the open dialog stays as it is.

```html
<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialogToggle" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogToggleLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogToggleLabel">Dialog 1</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    Show a second dialog and hide this one with the button below.
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button class="btn-solid theme-primary" data-coreui-target="#exampleDialogToggle2" data-coreui-toggle="dialog">Open second dialog</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialogToggle2" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogToggleLabel2">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogToggleLabel2">Dialog 2</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    Hide this dialog and show the first with the button below.
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button class="btn-solid theme-primary" data-coreui-target="#exampleDialogToggle" data-coreui-toggle="dialog">Back to first</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary" data-coreui-target="#exampleDialogToggle" data-coreui-toggle="dialog">Open first dialog</button>
```

## Non-modal dialogs

Set the `modal` option to `false` to show the dialog without the top layer — no backdrop, no focus trap, and the rest of the page stays interactive.

<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleDialogNonModal" data-coreui-modal="false" aria-labelledby="exampleDialogNonModalLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleDialogNonModalLabel">Non-modal dialog</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>The rest of the page stays interactive while this dialog is open.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog" id="myDialog" data-coreui-modal="false">
  ...
</dialog>
```

## Optional sizes

Dialogs have three optional sizes, available via modifier classes placed on the `<dialog class="dialog">`.

| Size | Class | Dialog max-width
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small | `.dialog-sm` | `280px` |
| Default | <span class="fg-2">None</span> | `500px` |
| Large | `.dialog-lg` | `800px` |
| Extra large | `.dialog-xl` | `1140px` |

```html
<dialog class="dialog dialog-xl">...</dialog>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-lg">...</dialog>
<dialog class="dialog dialog-sm">...</dialog>
```

## Fullscreen dialog

Pop up a dialog that covers the user viewport, via modifier classes placed on the `<dialog class="dialog">`.

| Class | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| `.dialog-fullscreen` | Always |
| `.dialog-fullscreen-sm-down` | `576px` |
| `.dialog-fullscreen-md-down` | `768px` |
| `.dialog-fullscreen-lg-down` | `1024px` |
| `.dialog-fullscreen-xl-down` | `1280px` |
| `.dialog-fullscreen-2xl-down` | `1536px` |

```html
<dialog class="dialog dialog-fullscreen-sm-down">
  ...
</dialog>
```

## Dark variant

Put `data-coreui-theme="dark"` on the `<dialog>` and it flips the tokens its own surface reads, so the dialog and everything in it — including the close button — turns dark on a light page.

<dialog class="dialog" id="darkDialog" data-coreui-theme="dark" aria-labelledby="darkDialogLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="darkDialogLabel">Dark dialog</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>The surface, the text and the dividers all read the flipped tokens.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-footer">
    <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog">Close</button>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html

  ...
</dialog>
```

## Accessibility

Be sure to add `aria-labelledby="..."`, referencing the dialog title, to the `<dialog>`. Additionally, you may give a description of your dialog with `aria-describedby`. The native `<dialog>` element already provides the dialog role, `aria-modal` semantics, focus trapping, and background inertness — don't add `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-hidden`, or `tabindex` yourself.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Set `data-coreui-toggle="dialog"` on a controller element, like a button, along with a `data-coreui-target="#foo"` or `href="#foo"` to target a specific dialog to toggle. Dismiss from within with `data-coreui-dismiss="dialog"`.

### Via JavaScript

```js
const myDialog = new coreui.Dialog(document.getElementById('myDialog'), options)
// or
const myDialogAlternative = new coreui.Dialog('#myDialog', options)
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-backdrop="static"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backdrop` | boolean, `'static'` | `true` | Shows the native `::backdrop` behind the dialog. Alternatively, specify `static` for a backdrop which doesn't close the dialog when clicked, or `false` to visually suppress it. |
| `keyboard` | boolean | `true` | Closes the dialog when escape key is pressed. |
| `modal` | boolean | `true` | Opens the dialog in the browser's top layer with a backdrop and focus trapping. Set to `false` for a non-modal dialog that leaves the rest of the page interactive. |

### Methods

> #### Promises and transitions
> 
> **Methods that show or hide a component return a promise.** The promise resolves when the transition ends, so `await` continues at the same moment a `shown.coreui.*` or `hidden.coreui.*` listener runs. The methods still return immediately and never block the caller. A call on a component that is already transitioning does nothing and resolves right away.
> 
> [Refer to our JavaScript documentation for further details](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#promises-and-transitions).

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Destroys an element's dialog. (Removes stored data on the DOM element) |
| `getInstance` | *Static* method which allows you to get the dialog instance associated with a DOM element. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | *Static* method which allows you to get the dialog instance associated with a DOM element, or create a new one in case it wasn't initialized. |
| `handleUpdate` | Provided for API consistency with Modal — the native `<dialog>` needs no manual adjustments. |
| `hide` | Manually hides a dialog. **Returns a promise that resolves after the dialog is hidden** (i.e. after the `hidden.coreui.dialog` event occurs). |
| `show` | Manually opens a dialog. **Returns a promise that resolves after the dialog is shown** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.dialog` event occurs). Also, you can pass a DOM element as an argument that can be received in the dialog events (as the `relatedTarget` property). |
| `toggle` | Manually toggles a dialog. **Returns a promise that resolves after the dialog is shown or hidden** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.dialog` or `hidden.coreui.dialog` event occurs). |

### Events

All dialog events are fired at the dialog itself (i.e. at the `<dialog class="dialog">`).

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `cancel.coreui.dialog` | This event is fired when the dialog is dismissed with the escape key, right before hiding starts. |
| `hidden.coreui.dialog` | This event is fired when the dialog has finished being hidden from the user (will wait for CSS transitions to complete). |
| `hide.coreui.dialog` | This event is fired immediately when the `hide` instance method has been called. |
| `hidePrevented.coreui.dialog` | This event is fired when the dialog is shown, its backdrop is `static` and a click outside of the dialog is performed. The event is also fired when the escape key is pressed and the `keyboard` option is set to `false`. |
| `show.coreui.dialog` | This event fires immediately when the `show` instance method is called. If caused by a click, the clicked element is available as the `relatedTarget` property of the event. |
| `shown.coreui.dialog` | This event is fired when the dialog has been made visible to the user (will wait for CSS transitions to complete). If caused by a click, the clicked element is available as the `relatedTarget` property of the event. |

```js
const myDialogEl = document.getElementById('myDialog')
myDialogEl.addEventListener('hidden.coreui.dialog', event => {
  // do something...
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Dialogs use local CSS variables on `.dialog` for enhanced real-time customization.

```scss
$dialog-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-dialog-zindex: var(--cui-z-dialog),
    --cui-dialog-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-width: 500px,
    --cui-dialog-margin: 1.75rem,
    --cui-dialog-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-dialog-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-dialog-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-dialog-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
    --cui-dialog-transition-property: #{"opacity, transform, visibility"},
    --cui-dialog-transition-duration: .3s,
    --cui-dialog-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
    --cui-dialog-backdrop-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-backdrop-color) var(--cui-backdrop-opacity), transparent),
    --cui-dialog-backdrop-blur: var(--cui-backdrop-blur),
    --cui-dialog-header-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-header-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-header-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-header-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-title-line-height: var(--cui-body-line-height),
    --cui-dialog-footer-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-footer-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-dialog-footer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-dialog-footer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-dialog-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-dialog-slide-distance: 3rem,
    --cui-dialog-scale-transform: scale(1.02),
  ),
  $dialog-tokens
);
```

### Sass maps

Each entry is one `.dialog-{size}` class and the width it sets, and the map merges with your overrides — add a key to define a size, or set one to `null` to drop it:

```scss
$dialog-sizes: () !default;
$dialog-sizes: defaults(
  (
    sm: 280px,
    lg: 800px,
    xl: 1140px,
  ),
  $dialog-sizes
);
```

# Bootstrap Drawer

> Bootstrap Drawer component built on the native <dialog> element — a floating, inset side panel with a blurred native backdrop, focus trapping, and responsive variants.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

The Drawer component slides a floating, rounded panel in from any edge of the viewport — for navigation, shopping carts, filters, and settings. It renders on the browser's native `<dialog>` element, so the top layer, `::backdrop`, focus trapping, and dialog semantics come from the browser. It follows the design Bootstrap 6 introduces under the same name — an inset panel over a blurred, translucent backdrop.

Drawer shares its base behavior with [Offcanvas](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/offcanvas/). Offcanvas keeps the classic edge-anchored look and the v5 vocabulary; Drawer carries the new Bootstrap 6 look and the `drawer-*` classes. Pick one — they are independent components.

## Example

Toggle a drawer by clicking the button below.

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" id="exampleDrawer" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerLabel">Drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    The drawer content goes here. You can place nearly any Bootstrap component or custom element here.
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#exampleDrawer">
  Open drawer
</button>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" id="exampleDrawer" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerLabel">Drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Placement

Drawers can slide in from any edge of the viewport — apply one of the placement classes:

- `.drawer-start` — left side of the viewport
- `.drawer-end` — right side of the viewport
- `.drawer-top` — top of the viewport
- `.drawer-bottom` — bottom of the viewport
- `.drawer-fullscreen` — covers the viewport (minus the inset)

<dialog class="drawer drawer-end" id="exampleDrawerEnd" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerEndLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerEndLabel">Right drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-top" id="exampleDrawerTop" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerTopLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerTopLabel">Top drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-bottom" id="exampleDrawerBottom" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerBottomLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerBottomLabel">Bottom drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-fullscreen" id="exampleDrawerFullscreen" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerFullscreenLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerFullscreenLabel">Fullscreen drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

## Variants

### Translucent

Add `.drawer-translucent` for a frosted-glass panel that blurs the content behind it.

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start drawer-translucent" id="exampleDrawerTranslucent" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerTranslucentLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerTranslucentLabel">Translucent drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

### Sheet

Combine `.drawer-bottom` with `.drawer-sheet` for a flush-to-edge bottom sheet with no inset and squared bottom corners. On large viewports the sheet is centered with a maximum width (`--cui-drawer-sheet-width`).

<dialog class="drawer drawer-bottom drawer-sheet" id="exampleDrawerSheet" aria-labelledby="exampleDrawerSheetLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleDrawerSheetLabel">Bottom sheet</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    ...
  </div>
</dialog>

### Fit content

Add `.drawer-fit-content` to a `.drawer-start`/`.drawer-end` drawer to keep the panel only as tall as its content.

### Footer

Add a `.drawer-footer` below the `.drawer-body` for the panel's actions. It is a flex row that wraps and keeps its children spaced and vertically centered, so a row of buttons needs no utilities.

### Backdrop presets

The backdrop reads `--cui-backdrop-color`, `--cui-backdrop-opacity` and `--cui-backdrop-blur`; a drawer defaults to a translucent tint of the page. For the dialog's dark scrim add `.backdrop-scrim`; the [presets](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/helpers/backdrop/) work on every overlay component.

```html
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#drawerScrim">
  Toggle drawer with a dark backdrop
</button>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start backdrop-scrim" id="drawerScrim" aria-labelledby="drawerScrimLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="drawerScrimLabel">Dark backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    The scrim the dialog uses, on a drawer.
  </div>
</dialog>
```

### No backdrop

Add `.drawer-no-backdrop` to hide the backdrop while keeping the drawer modal — the panel still takes the top layer and traps focus, but nothing dims the page behind it.

### Instant

Add `.drawer-instant` to a drawer that should appear and disappear at once, with no slide and no backdrop fade. It is the same opt-out that [`.alert-instant`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/alert/#dismissing) provides, and it applies to both directions.

### Dark

Put `data-coreui-theme="dark"` on the drawer and it flips the tokens its own surface reads, so the panel and everything in it — including the close button — turns dark on a light page.

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" data-coreui-theme="dark" id="drawerDark" aria-labelledby="drawerDarkLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="drawerDarkLabel">Dark drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    <p>The surface, the text and the dividers all read the flipped tokens.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" data-coreui-theme="dark">
  ...
</dialog>
```

## Body scrolling

The page scroll is blocked while a drawer is open. Set `scroll: true` to open the drawer non-modally instead — the page stays interactive and scrollable. A visible backdrop requires the top layer, so `backdrop: true` (the default) takes precedence over `scroll: true` for the page-interactivity part.

```html
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#drawerScrolling">Enable body scrolling</button>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" data-coreui-scroll="true" data-coreui-backdrop="false" id="drawerScrolling" aria-labelledby="drawerScrollingLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="drawerScrollingLabel">Drawer with body scrolling</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    <p>Scroll further down the page to see this option in action.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Static backdrop

When the backdrop is set to `static`, the drawer will remain open when clicking outside of it.

```html
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#drawerStatic">
  Toggle static drawer
</button>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start" data-coreui-backdrop="static" id="drawerStatic" aria-labelledby="drawerStaticLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="drawerStaticLabel">Drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    <div>
      I won’t close if you click outside of me.
    </div>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Responsive

Responsive drawer classes hide content in a drawer below a specified breakpoint and render it inline above it. For example, `.drawer-lg` acts as a drawer below the `lg` breakpoint and displays the content inline above it.

```html
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary d-lg-none" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#drawerResponsive" aria-controls="drawerResponsive">Toggle drawer</button>

<div class="alert theme-info d-none d-lg-block">Resize your browser to show the responsive drawer toggle.</div>

<dialog class="drawer-lg drawer-end" id="drawerResponsive" aria-labelledby="drawerResponsiveLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="drawerResponsiveLabel">Responsive drawer</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" data-coreui-target="#drawerResponsive" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    <p class="mb-0">This is content within a <code>.drawer-lg</code>.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

Responsive drawer classes are available for each breakpoint.

- `.drawer`
- `.drawer-sm`
- `.drawer-md`
- `.drawer-lg`
- `.drawer-xl`
- `.drawer-2xl`

## Accessibility

Since the drawer is conceptually a modal dialog, be sure to add `aria-labelledby="..."` — referencing the drawer title — to `.drawer`. The native `<dialog>` element already provides the dialog role and focus management — don't add `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-hidden`, or `tabindex` yourself.

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Include `data-coreui-toggle="drawer"` along with a `data-coreui-target` or `href` in the element to automatically control a drawer. Dismiss from within with `data-coreui-dismiss="drawer"`. To have a drawer open by default, add the `open` attribute.

### Via JavaScript

```js
const drawerElementList = document.querySelectorAll('.drawer')
const drawerList = [...drawerElementList].map(drawerEl => new coreui.Drawer(drawerEl))
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-backdrop="static"`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backdrop` | boolean or the string `static` | `true` | Shows the native `::backdrop` while the drawer is open. Alternatively, specify `static` for a backdrop that doesn't close the drawer when clicked, or `false` to visually suppress it. |
| `keyboard` | boolean | `true` | Closes the drawer when the escape key is pressed. |
| `scroll` | boolean | `false` | Allows body scrolling while the drawer is open — the drawer then opens non-modally, keeping the rest of the page interactive.

### Methods

> #### Promises and transitions
> 
> **Methods that show or hide a component return a promise.** The promise resolves when the transition ends, so `await` continues at the same moment a `shown.coreui.*` or `hidden.coreui.*` listener runs. The methods still return immediately and never block the caller. A call on a component that is already transitioning does nothing and resolves right away.
> 
> [Refer to our JavaScript documentation for further details](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#promises-and-transitions).

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Destroys an element's drawer. (Removes stored data on the DOM element) |
| `getInstance` | *Static* method that allows you to obtain the drawer instance associated with a DOM element |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | *Static* method that enables you to retrieve the drawer instance linked to a DOM element, or create a new one if it hasn't been initialized |
| `hide` | Hides a drawer. **Returns a promise that resolves after the drawer is hidden** (i.e. after the `hidden.coreui.drawer` event occurs).|
| `show` | Displays a drawer. **Returns a promise that resolves after the drawer is shown** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.drawer` event occurs).|
| `toggle` | Switches a drawer between shown and hidden. **Returns a promise that resolves after the drawer is shown or hidden** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.drawer` or `hidden.coreui.drawer` event occurs).

### Events

| Event type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden.coreui.drawer` | This event is fired when a drawer is hidden from the user (it will wait for CSS transitions to complete). |
| `hide.coreui.drawer` | This event is fired immediately after the `hide` method has been called. |
| `hidePrevented.coreui.drawer` | This event is triggered when the drawer is shown, its backdrop is `static`, and a click outside of the drawer occurs. The event is also triggered when the escape key is pressed and the `keyboard` option is set to `false`. |
| `show.coreui.drawer` | This event fires immediately when the `show` instance method is invoked. |
| `shown.coreui.drawer` | This event is fired when a drawer becomes visible to the user (it will wait for CSS transitions to complete).

```js
const myDrawer = document.getElementById('myDrawer')
myDrawer.addEventListener('hidden.coreui.drawer', event => {
  // do something...
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Drawers use local CSS variables on `.drawer` for enhanced real-time customization.

```scss
$drawer-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-drawer-inset: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-zindex: var(--cui-z-drawer),
    --cui-drawer-width: 400px,
    --cui-drawer-height: 30vh,
    --cui-drawer-sheet-width: 760px,
    --cui-drawer-padding-x: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-padding-y: var(--cui-spacer),
    --cui-drawer-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-drawer-bg: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-drawer-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-drawer-border-color: var(--cui-border-color-translucent),
    --cui-drawer-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-drawer-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
    --cui-drawer-transition-property: #{"transform, visibility"},
    --cui-drawer-transition-duration: .3s,
    --cui-drawer-transition-timing: var(--cui-transition-timing-overlay),
    --cui-drawer-title-line-height: var(--cui-body-line-height),
    --cui-drawer-body-gap: var(--cui-drawer-padding-y),
    --cui-drawer-footer-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-bg-body),
    --cui-backdrop-opacity: 25%,
    --cui-drawer-backdrop-bg: color-mix(in oklch, var(--cui-backdrop-color) var(--cui-backdrop-opacity), transparent),
    --cui-drawer-backdrop-blur: var(--cui-backdrop-blur),
    --cui-drawer-scale-transform: scale(1.02),
  ),
  $drawer-tokens
);
```


---

# Bootstrap 6 Dropdown

> Bootstrap dropdown component allows you to toggle contextual overlays for displaying lists, links, and more html elements.

## Overview

> **Built on Menu — and heading for retirement.** Since v6 the Dropdown plugin is a compatibility layer over the new [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/) component — same engine, keyboard handling and dismissal, with the v5 markup, classes and `*.coreui.dropdown` events preserved. Existing dropdown markup keeps working unchanged throughout v6, but **Dropdown may be removed in v7** — we recommend using Menu for new work and migrating when convenient.

Dropdowns are toggleable, contextual overlays for displaying lists of links and more. They're made interactive with the included Bootstrap dropdown JavaScript plugin. They're toggled by clicking, not by hovering.

Dropdowns are built on a third party library, [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/), which provides dynamic positioning and viewport detection. Be sure to include [floating-ui.core.umd.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@floating-ui/core@1.8.0/dist/floating-ui.core.umd.min.js) and [floating-ui.dom.umd.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@floating-ui/dom@1.8.0/dist/floating-ui.dom.umd.min.js) (in this order) before CoreUI's JavaScript or use `coreui.bundle.min.js` / `coreui.bundle.js` which contains Floating UI. Floating UI isn't used to position dropdowns in navbars though as dynamic positioning isn't required.

## Accessibility

The [<abbr title="Web Accessibility Initiative">WAI</abbr> <abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr>](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/) standard defines an actual [`role="menu"` widget](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#menu), but this is specific to application-like menus which trigger actions or functions. <abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr> menus can only contain menu items, checkbox menu items, radio button menu items, radio button groups, and sub-menus.

CoreUI for Bootstrap's dropdowns, on the other hand, are designed to be generic and applicable to a variety of situations and markup structures. For instance, it is possible to create dropdowns that contain additional inputs and form controls, such as search fields or login forms. For this reason, Bootstrap does not expect (nor automatically add) any of the `role` and `aria-` attributes required for true <abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr> menus. Authors will have to include these more specific attributes themselves.

However, Bootstrap does add built-in support for most standard keyboard menu interactions, such as the ability to move through individual `.dropdown-item` elements using the cursor keys and close the menu with the <kbd>ESC</kbd> key.

## Examples

Bind the dropdown's toggle and the dropdown menu inside `.dropdown`, or different element that declares `position: relative;`. Dropdowns can be triggered from `<a>` or `<button>` elements to better fit your possible requirements.

### Single button

Each single `.btn` can be changed into a dropdown toggle with small changes. Here's how you can put them to work with either `<button>` elements:

```html
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropdown button
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

And with `<a>` elements:

```html
<div class="dropdown">
  <a class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" href="#" role="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropdown link
  </a>

  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

The best part is you can do this with any button variant, too:

```html
<!-- Example single danger button -->
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-danger dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Action
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
    <li><hr class="dropdown-divider"></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Separated link</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Split button

Similarly, create split button dropdowns with virtually the same markup as single button dropdowns, but with the addition of `.dropdown-toggle-split` for proper spacing around the dropdown caret.

We use this extra class to reduce the horizontal `padding` on either side of the caret by 25% and remove the `margin-left` that's attached for normal button dropdowns. Those additional changes hold the caret centered in the split button and implement a more properly sized hit area next to the main button.

```html
<!-- Example split danger button -->
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-danger">Action</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-danger dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropdown</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
    <li><hr class="dropdown-divider"></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Separated link</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

## Sizing

Button dropdowns work with buttons of all sizes, including default and split dropdown buttons.

```html
<!-- Large button groups (default and split) -->
<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-lg dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Large button
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    ...
  </ul>
</div>
<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-lg" type="button">
    Large split button
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-lg dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropdown</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    ...
  </ul>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-sm dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Small button
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    ...
  </ul>
</div>
<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-sm" type="button">
    Small split button
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-sm dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropdown</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    ...
  </ul>
</div>
```

## Dark dropdowns

Opt into darker dropdowns to match a dark navbar or custom style by adding `.dropdown-menu-dark` onto an existing `.dropdown-menu`. No changes are required to the dropdown items.

```html
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropdown button
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-dark">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item active" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
    <li><hr class="dropdown-divider"></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Separated link</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

And putting it to use in a navbar:

```html
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-lg bg-3" data-coreui-theme="dark">
  <div class="container-fluid">
    <a class="navbar-brand" href="#">Navbar</a>
    <button class="navbar-toggler" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="collapse" data-coreui-target="#navbarNavDarkDropdown" aria-controls="navbarNavDarkDropdown" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Toggle navigation">
      <span class="navbar-toggler-icon"></span>
    </button>
    <div class="collapse navbar-collapse" id="navbarNavDarkDropdown">
      <ul class="navbar-nav">
        <li class="nav-item dropdown">
          <button class="btn-solid theme-inverse dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
            Dropdown
          </button>
          <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-dark">
            <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
            <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
            <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
          </ul>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</nav>
```

## Directions

> #### RTL
> 
> Directions are mirrored when using CoreUI in RTL, meaning `.dropstart` will appear on the right side.

### Centered

Make the dropdown menu centered below the toggle with `.dropdown-center` on the parent element.

```html
<div class="dropdown-center">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Centered dropdown
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action two</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action three</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Dropup

Trigger dropdown menus above elements by adding `.dropup` to the parent element.

```html
<!-- Default dropup button -->
<div class="btn-group dropup">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropup
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- Split dropup button -->
<div class="btn-group dropup">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary">
    Split dropup
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropdown</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Dropup centered

Make the dropup menu centered above the toggle with `.dropup-center` on the parent element.

```html
<div class="dropup-center dropup">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Centered dropup
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action two</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action three</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Dropend

Trigger dropdown menus at the right of the elements by adding `.dropend` to the parent element.

```html
<!-- Default dropend button -->
<div class="btn-group dropend">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropend
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- Split dropend button -->
<div class="btn-group dropend">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary">
    Split dropend
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropend</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Dropstart

Trigger dropdown menus at the left of the elements by adding `.dropstart` to the parent element.

```html
<!-- Default dropstart button -->
<div class="btn-group dropstart">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropstart
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
</div>

<!-- Split dropstart button -->
<div class="btn-group dropstart">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle dropdown-toggle-split" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="visually-hidden">Toggle Dropstart</span>
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <!-- Dropdown menu links -->
  </ul>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary">
    Split dropstart
  </button>
</div>
```

### Placement option

_Added in 6.0.0._

The direction classes above pick one of six fixed positions. `data-coreui-placement` on the toggle takes the same values the [Menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/#placement) takes — physical (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`), logical (`start`, `end`, which mirror in RTL) and every `-start`/`-end` alignment — and it wins over the wrapper classes when both are present. Breakpoint prefixes make it responsive: `bottom-start md:top-end` reads as bottom-start below `md` and top-end from `md` up.

```html
<div class="dropdown">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" data-coreui-placement="top-end" aria-expanded="false">
    Top end
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
<div class="dropdown">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" data-coreui-placement="bottom-start md:end-start" aria-expanded="false">
    Bottom start, end from md
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

Inside a `.navbar`, or with `display: 'static'`, the plugin writes the resolved placement onto the menu and the stylesheet positions it from that, so the option works there too — every placement except the centered ones.

## Menu items

You can use `<a>` or `<button>` elements as dropdown items.

```html
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Dropdown
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Another action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Something else here</button></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

You can also create non-interactive dropdown items with `.dropdown-item-text`. Feel free to style further with custom CSS or text utilities.

```html
<ul class="dropdown-menu">
  <li><span class="dropdown-item-text">Dropdown item text</span></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Action</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another action</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Something else here</a></li>
</ul>
```

### Active

Add `.active` to items in the dropdown to **style them as active**. To convey the active state to assistive technologies, use the `aria-current` attribute — using the `page` value for the current page, or `true` for the current item in a set.

```html
<ul class="dropdown-menu">
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Regular link</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item active" href="#" aria-current="true">Active link</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another link</a></li>
</ul>
```

### Disabled

Add `.disabled` to items in the dropdown to **style them as disabled**.

```html
<ul class="dropdown-menu">
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Regular link</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item disabled" aria-disabled="true">Disabled link</a></li>
  <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Another link</a></li>
</ul>
```

## Menu alignment

By default, a dropdown menu is automatically positioned 100% from the top and along the left side of its parent. Add `.dropdown-menu-end` to a `.dropdown-menu` to right align the dropdown menu.

> **Heads up!** Dropdowns are positioned thanks to Floating UI except when they are contained in a navbar.

```html
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">
    Right-aligned menu example
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-end">
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Another action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Something else here</button></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### Responsive alignment

Alignment that changes with the viewport is a responsive [placement](#placement-option): `data-coreui-placement="bottom-start lg:bottom-end"` aligns the menu left and switches to right from `lg` up. It works with dynamic positioning and, because the plugin writes the resolved placement onto the menu, with `data-coreui-display="static"` and inside a navbar too.

```html
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" data-coreui-display="static" data-coreui-placement="bottom-start lg:bottom-end" aria-expanded="false">
    Left-aligned but right aligned when large screen
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Another action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Something else here</button></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="btn-group">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary dropdown-toggle" data-coreui-toggle="dropdown" data-coreui-display="static" data-coreui-placement="bottom-end lg:bottom-start" aria-expanded="false">
    Right-aligned but left aligned when large screen
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Another action</button></li>
    <li><button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Something else here</button></li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

The v5 classes `.dropdown-menu{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}{-start|-end}` ship in [`coreui-legacy.css`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/install/#v5-compatibility-css) for markup that still uses them.
