```html
  </div>
  <div class="toast-body">The TLS certificate expires in 7 days.</div>
</div>
```

Theme classes also apply from an ancestor, so a themed container passes its colors to every toast inside it.

### Custom content

Customize your toasts by removing sub-components, adjusting them with [utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/api/), or adding your own markup. In this example, we've made a simpler toast by removing the default `.toast-header`, incorporating a custom hide icon from [CoreUI Icons](https://coreui.io/icons/), and using [flexbox utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/flex/) to modify the layout.

```html
<div class="toast align-items-center show" role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">
  <div class="d-flex">
    <div class="toast-body">
    Hello, world! This is a toast message.
   </div>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close me-3 m-auto" data-coreui-dismiss="toast" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

Alternatively, you can also add additional controls and components to toasts.

```html
<div class="toast show" role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">
  <div class="toast-body">
    Hello, world! This is a toast message.
    <div class="mt-3 pt-3 border-top">
      <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary btn-sm">Take action</button>
      <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary btn-sm" data-coreui-dismiss="toast">Close</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Color schemes

Building on the previous example, you can design various toast color schemes using our [color](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/colors/) and [background](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/background/) utilities. We added `.text-bg-primary` to the `.toast`; the close button takes the colour it inherits, so it stays legible on its own. To achieve a clean edge, we remove the default border with `.border-0`.

```html
<div class="toast align-items-center text-bg-primary border-0 show" role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">

</div>
```

### Instant

By default, toasts fade in and out. To disable the animation, add `.toast-instant` to the toast. The `show` and `hide` methods then finish immediately, so `shown.coreui.toast` and `hidden.coreui.toast` fire right away.

```html
<div class="toast toast-instant show" role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">
  <div class="toast-header">
    <svg class="docs-placeholder-img rounded me-3" width="20" height="20" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Placeholder" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Placeholder</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em"></text></svg>
    <strong class="me-auto">CoreUI for Bootstrap</strong>
    <small>11 mins ago</small>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="toast" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="toast-body">
    This toast appears and disappears instantly.
  </div>
</div>
```

## Placement

_Added in 6.0.0._

Nine `.toast-container-{block}-{inline}` classes pin the container to the viewport: `block` is `top`, `middle` or `bottom`, `inline` is `start`, `center` or `end`. They set `position: fixed` and read the distance from the edge from `--cui-toast-container-inset` (`--cui-spacer-5` by default). Inside a positioned box — like the example below — add `.position-absolute` to pin the container to that box instead of the viewport.

```html
<form>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <label for="selectToastPlacement">Toast placement</label>
    <select class="form-control mt-3" id="selectToastPlacement">
      <option value="" selected>Select a position...</option>
      <option value="toast-container-top-start">Top start</option>
      <option value="toast-container-top-center">Top center</option>
      <option value="toast-container-top-end">Top end</option>
      <option value="toast-container-middle-start">Middle start</option>
      <option value="toast-container-middle-center">Middle center</option>
      <option value="toast-container-middle-end">Middle end</option>
      <option value="toast-container-bottom-start">Bottom start</option>
      <option value="toast-container-bottom-center">Bottom center</option>
      <option value="toast-container-bottom-end">Bottom end</option>
    </select>
  </div>
</form>
<div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" class="bg-black position-relative docs-example-toasts">
  <div class="toast-container position-absolute" id="toastPlacement">
    <div class="toast show">
      <div class="toast-header">
        <svg class="docs-placeholder-img rounded me-3" width="20" height="20" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Placeholder" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Placeholder</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em"></text></svg>
        <strong class="me-auto">CoreUI for Bootstrap</strong>
        <small>11 mins ago</small>
      </div>
      <div class="toast-body">
        Hello, world! This is a toast message.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

For systems that generate more notifications, consider using a wrapping element to allow them to stack easily.


## Toaster

Toasts you create at runtime — from a form submission, a request that settled, a background job — come from the [Toaster](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/toaster/): a store keyed by id with `add()`, `update()`, `close()` and `promise()`, its own placed container, announcements through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages), a visible-toasts limit and screen-reader priority. The markup and classes on this page are what it renders.

## Accessibility

Toasts are meant to be brief interruptions for your visitors or users. To assist those using screen readers and similar assistive technologies, you should wrap your toasts in an [`aria-live` region](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/ARIA_Live_Regions). Changes to live regions, such as injecting or updating a toast component, are automatically announced by screen readers without moving the user's focus or interrupting the user. Additionally, include `aria-atomic="true"` to ensure the entire toast is announced as a single, unfragmented unit, rather than just announcing what changed—this prevents issues if only part of the toast is updated or if the same toast appears again later. If the information is critical to the process, such as a list of form errors, use the [alert component](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/alert/) instead of a toast.

Note that the live region must exist in the markup *before* the toast is generated or updated. If you generate both dynamically and inject them simultaneously, assistive technologies generally will not announce them.

You should also adjust the `role` and `aria-live` level based on the content. For important messages like errors, use `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"`; otherwise, use `role="status" aria-live="polite"`.

As the content changes, remember to update the [`delay` timeout](#options) so users have enough time to read the toast.

```html
<div class="toast" role="alert" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" data-coreui-delay="10000">
  <div role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">...</div>
</div>
```

When using `autohide: false`, you need to add a close button to let users dismiss the toast.

```html
<div role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true" class="toast show" data-coreui-autohide="false">
  <div class="toast-header">
    <svg class="docs-placeholder-img rounded me-3" width="20" height="20" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Placeholder" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Placeholder</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em"></text></svg>
    <strong class="me-auto">CoreUI for Bootstrap</strong>
    <small>11 mins ago</small>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="toast" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="toast-body">
    Hello, world! This is a toast message.
  </div>
</div>
```

While technically it's possible to add focusable or actionable controls, such as additional buttons or links, to your toast, you should avoid doing this with autohiding toasts. Even if you set a long [`delay` timeout](#options), keyboard and assistive technology users might find it hard to reach the toast in time to act because toasts don't receive focus when they appear. If you absolutely need to have additional controls, we recommend using a toast with `autohide: false`.

## Usage

Initialize toasts using JavaScript:

```js
const toastElList = document.querySelectorAll('.toast')
const toastList = [...toastElList].map(toastEl => new coreui.Toast(toastEl, option))
```

### Triggers

Dismissal can be achieved with the `data` attribute on a button **within the toast** as demonstrated below:

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="toast" aria-label="Close"></button>
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-autohide="{value}"`. Remember to convert the case of the option name from "_camelCase_" to "_kebab-case_" when using data attributes. For instance, you should write `data-coreui-custom-class="beautifier"` rather than `data-coreui-customClass="beautifier"`.

Starting with CoreUI 4.2.6, all components support an **experimental** reserved data attribute named `data-coreui-config`, which can contain simple component configurations as a JSON string. If an element has attributes `data-coreui-config='{"delay":50, "title":689}'` and `data-coreui-title="Custom Title"`, then the final value for `title` will be `Custom Title`, as the standard data attributes will take precedence over values specified in `data-coreui-config`. Moreover, existing data attributes can also hold JSON values like `data-coreui-delay='{"show":50, "hide":250}'`.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autohide` | boolean | `true` | Hides the Bootstrap toast automatically |
| `delay` | number | `5000` | Sets delay before hiding the toast (ms) |

### Methods

> #### Promises and transitions
> 
> **Methods that show or hide a component return a promise.** The promise resolves when the transition ends, so `await` continues at the same moment a `shown.coreui.*` or `hidden.coreui.*` listener runs. The methods still return immediately and never block the caller. A call on a component that is already transitioning does nothing and resolves right away.
> 
> [Refer to our JavaScript documentation for further details](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#promises-and-transitions).

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Hides an element's toast. Your Bootstrap toast will stay in the DOM but won't be visible anymore. |
| `getInstance` | *Static* method that allows you to get the toast instance associated with a DOM element. For example: `const myToastEl = document.getElementById('myToastEl')` and `const myToast = coreui.Toast.getInstance(myToastEl)`. Returns a Bootstrap toast instance.
| `getOrCreateInstance` | *Static* method that gets the toast instance associated with a DOM element or creates a new one if it wasn't initialized. For example: `const myToastEl = document.getElementById('myToastEl')` and `const myToast = coreui.Toast.getOrCreateInstance(myToastEl)`. Returns a Bootstrap toast instance.
| `hide` | Hides an element's toast. **Returns a promise that resolves after the toast is hidden** (i.e., after the `hidden.coreui.toast` event occurs). You need to manually call this method if you set `autohide` to `false`. |
| `isShown` | Returns a boolean indicating the toast's visibility state. |
| `show` | Reveals an element's toast. **Returns a promise that resolves after the toast is shown** (i.e., after the `shown.coreui.toast` event occurs). You need to call this method manually; otherwise, your toast won't appear. |

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden.coreui.toast` | This event occurs when the toast has finished hiding from the user. |
| `hide.coreui.toast` | This event is triggered immediately when the `hide` instance method is called. |
| `show.coreui.toast` | This event triggers immediately when the `show` instance method is called. |
| `shown.coreui.toast` | This event occurs when the toast has become visible to the user. |

```js
const myToastEl = document.getElementById('myToast')
myToastEl.addEventListener('hidden.coreui.toast', () => {
  // do something...
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Toasts use local CSS variables on `.toast` for enhanced real-time customization.

```scss
$toast-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-toast-zindex: var(--cui-z-toast),
    --cui-toast-padding-x: .75rem,
    --cui-toast-padding-y: .5rem,
    --cui-toast-spacing: #{$container-padding-x},
    --cui-toast-max-width: #{350px},
    --cui-toast-color: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-toast-bg: #{$toast-background-color},
    --cui-toast-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-toast-border-color: #{$toast-border-color},
    --cui-toast-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-7),
    --cui-toast-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow),
    --cui-toast-header-color: var(--cui-fg-3),
    --cui-toast-header-bg: #{$toast-background-color},
    --cui-toast-header-border-color: #{$toast-border-color},
    --cui-toast-font-size: .875rem,
    --cui-toast-slide: .5rem,
    --cui-toast-transition-property: #{"opacity, translate, display"},
    --cui-toast-transition-duration: #{.3s},
    --cui-toast-transition-timing: #{ease-out},
  ),
  $toast-tokens
);
```

The container declares its own two, on `.toast-container`:

```scss
--cui-toast-zindex: var(--cui-z-toast);
--cui-toast-container-inset: #{var(--cui-spacer-5)};
--cui-toast-inline-sign: 1;
--cui-toast-max-width: #{350px};
--cui-toast-spacing: #{$container-padding-x};
--cui-toast-transition-duration: #{.3s};
--cui-toast-transition-timing: #{ease-out};
```

### Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$toast-background-color:            var(--cui-bg-body) !default;
$toast-border-color:                var(--cui-border-color-translucent) !default;
```

# Bootstrap 6 Toaster

> Create toast notifications from JavaScript with the CoreUI Toaster: a store keyed by id with add, update, close and promise, a placed container, a visible-toasts limit and screen-reader priority.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

The `Toaster` plugin creates [toasts](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/toasts/) from options, so nothing has to be in the markup up front. It keeps a store of the toasts it shows, keyed by id, and one instance serves the whole page: `add()` returns the id, `update()` rewrites a toast in place, `close()` hides one or all of them, and `promise()` follows an asynchronous operation through its loading, success and error states.

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement: 'top-end', limit: 3 })
const id = toaster.add({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are live.', theme: 'success' })
toaster.update(id, { description: 'Done' })
toaster.close(id)
```

Without an element the toaster creates its own `.toast-container` in `<body>`, placed by the `placement` option; pass an existing container instead to keep control over where the toasts land. The container is a `region` landmark named `Notifications`, so users of assistive technology can navigate to it.

## Live example

Two toasters, each with its container in a top corner of the viewport: a list on the end side and a [stack](#stacking) on the start side. Every other example on this page passes a container that sits inside the example, so its toasts stay put.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterLiveBtn">Add a toast</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" id="toasterLiveStackBtn">Add to the stack</button>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement: 'top-end' })
const stacked = new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement: 'top-start', stack: true, limit: 6 })

document.getElementById('toasterLiveBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({ title: 'CoreUI for Bootstrap', description: 'Hello, world! This is a toast message.' })
})

document.getElementById('toasterLiveStackBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  stacked.add({ title: 'CoreUI for Bootstrap', description: 'Hello, world! This one joins a stack.' })
})
```

## Title, description and theme

A toast is a plain options object. `title` renders the header with a close button, `description` the body; a toast without a title puts the close button in the body. `theme` adds the `theme-{color}` class, `priority: 'high'` has screen readers announce it right away, `timeout` overrides the toaster's default (`0` keeps the toast until it is closed) and `dismissible: false` drops the close button.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-3 flex-wrap mb-4">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterTitleBtn">Title and description</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" id="toasterDescriptionBtn">Description only</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-danger" id="toasterThemeBtn">Themed, high priority</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" id="toasterStickyBtn">Not dismissible</button>
</div>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterContent"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterContent', { timeout: 0 })

document.getElementById('toasterTitleBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are live.' })
})

document.getElementById('toasterDescriptionBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({ description: 'Copied to the clipboard' })
})

document.getElementById('toasterThemeBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({
    title: 'Payment failed', description: 'The card was declined.', theme: 'danger', priority: 'high'
  })
})

document.getElementById('toasterStickyBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({
    title: 'Read me', description: 'This one stays until you close it.', dismissible: false, timeout: 0
  })
})
```

Strings are written as text. Set `html: true` on the toaster to render markup; it runs through the same sanitizer as tooltips, configurable with `allowList` and `sanitizeFn`.

## Updating a toast

Passing an `id` that already exists updates that toast instead of adding a second one, and bumps its `updateKey`, so a "Draft saved" toast clicked twice stays a single toast. `update()` does the same for a toast whose id you kept, and accepts a function of the current toast when the change depends on it: `toaster.update(id, previous => ({ description: previous.data.step + 1 }))`. A toast that is already closing is not reused: adding its `id` again removes it at once and adds a new toast, which takes the newest place in the container.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-3 flex-wrap mb-4">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterDraftBtn">Save draft</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" id="toasterUploadBtn">Upload with progress</button>
</div>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterUpdate"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterUpdate', { timeout: 0 })
let saves = 0

document.getElementById('toasterDraftBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  saves += 1
  toaster.add({ id: 'draft', title: 'Draft saved', description: `Saved ${saves} time${saves === 1 ? '' : 's'}` })
})

document.getElementById('toasterUploadBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const id = toaster.add({ title: 'Uploading…', description: '0 %' })
  let progress = 0

  const interval = setInterval(() => {
    progress += 25
    toaster.update(id, { description: `${progress} %` })

    if (progress === 100) {
      clearInterval(interval)
      toaster.update(id, { title: 'Uploaded', theme: 'success' })
    }
  }, 500)
})
```

## Promises

`promise()` adds a toast in the `loading` state and updates it when the promise settles: `success` receives the resolved value, `error` the rejection. Each state is a description string, a full options object, or a function returning either.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary mb-4" id="toasterPromiseBtn">Save</button>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterPromise"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterPromise', { timeout: 0 })

document.getElementById('toasterPromiseBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const request = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    setTimeout(() => (Math.random() > 0.3 ? resolve('3 files') : reject(new Error('Network error'))), 2000)
  })

  toaster.promise(request, {
    loading: 'Saving…',
    success: files => `Saved ${files}`,
    error: error => ({ title: 'Not saved', description: error.message, priority: 'high' })
  }).catch(() => {})
})
```

## Action

`action` renders a button in the body; its `onClick` receives the click event and the toast object, so an undo can rewrite the same toast.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary mb-4" id="toasterArchiveBtn">Archive message</button>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterAction"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterAction', { timeout: 0 })

document.getElementById('toasterArchiveBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({
    description: 'Message archived',
    action: {
      label: 'Undo',
      onClick: (event, toast) => toaster.update(toast.id, { description: 'Message restored', action: null })
    }
  })
})
```

## Limit

`limit` caps how many toasts are visible at once. The newest stay on screen; older ones sink away from the edge and fade, remain in the DOM with `inert` and `data-coreui-limited`, and rise back in as the visible ones go away. `limit: 0` shows everything.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-3 mb-4">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterLimitBtn">Add a toast</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" id="toasterLimitCloseBtn">Close all</button>
</div>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterLimit"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterLimit', { limit: 2, timeout: 0 })
let count = 0

document.getElementById('toasterLimitBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  count += 1
  toaster.add({ title: `Toast ${count}`, description: 'Only two stay visible.' })
})

document.getElementById('toasterLimitCloseBtn').addEventListener('click', () => toaster.close())
```

## Stacking

With `stack: true` the toasts sit on top of each other: the newest in front at full size, the ones behind it scaled down by `--cui-toast-stack-scale` per step and receding towards a vanishing depth. The first toast behind peeks out by `--cui-toast-stack-peek` and every further one by that strip times the scale ratio, so the corners of the stack line up like a deck of cards seen in perspective. Only the front toast's timer runs; the ones behind wait their turn and start counting when they reach the front, so the stack empties from the front. A toast that leaves from behind — closed by id, or pushed over the limit — fades where it is instead of sliding out from under the deck. Hovering or focusing the container spreads the stack into a list; leaving it folds the stack back. The stack takes the place of the flow layout; `limit` decides how many toasts it holds. Folded, the deck shows the front toast and two behind it (`--cui-toast-stack-visible`); spreading it reveals every toast within the limit.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-3 mb-4">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterStackBtn">Add a toast</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" id="toasterStackCloseBtn">Close all</button>
</div>
<div class="toast-container position-relative" id="toasterStack"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterStack', { stack: true, limit: 0, timeout: 0 })
let count = 0

document.getElementById('toasterStackBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  count += 1
  toaster.add({ title: `Toast ${count}`, description: count % 2 ? 'Hover or focus the stack to spread it out.' : 'A shorter one.' })
})

document.getElementById('toasterStackCloseBtn').addEventListener('click', () => toaster.close())
```

The toaster keeps the geometry in tokens the CSS reads: `--cui-toast-stack-index`, `--cui-toast-stack-before` (the height of the toasts in front) and `--cui-toast-height` on each toast, `--cui-toast-stack-count`, `--cui-toast-stack-front-height` and `--cui-toast-stack-heights` on the container. Style the stack by these — the `data-coreui-stack-index` and `data-coreui-stack-hidden` attributes mark a toast's place in it.

A stack works in every placement: it grows away from the edge it is pinned to, so at the bottom the newest toast is the lowest one and the stack peeks upward.

```html
<div class="d-grid gap-3" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); max-width: 30rem" id="toasterPlacementStack">
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-start">Top start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-center">Top center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-end">Top end</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-start">Middle start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-center">Middle center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-end">Middle end</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-start">Bottom start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-center">Bottom center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-end">Bottom end</button>
</div>
```

```js
const stacks = new Map()

for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('#toasterPlacementStack [data-coreui-placement]')) {
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const placement = button.dataset.coreuiPlacement

    if (!stacks.has(placement)) {
      stacks.set(placement, new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement, stack: true, limit: 0 }))
    }

    const toaster = stacks.get(placement)
    toaster.add({ title: `${placement} · ${toaster.getToasts().length + 1}`, description: 'Hover the stack to spread it.' })
  })
}
```

## Motion

A toast slides in from beyond the container's edge while it fades in — from the side in the `start` and `end` placements, from above in `top-center` and from below in `bottom-center` — and leaves the way it came, so the entry and the exit read as one gesture. `middle-center` sits in the middle of the screen with no edge to come from, so its toasts only fade. While a toast leaves, the ones behind it glide into the freed space; when a new one arrives, they make room the same way. `enter` picks another edge for the entry and `leave` for the exit — a `top-end` toaster can drop its toasts in from above and still send them out sideways — and a toast outside a placed container slides by `--cui-toast-slide` instead. `start` and `end` are logical: they follow the direction the container sits in, so under `dir="rtl"` they change sides along with the placement. All of it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement: 'top-end', enter: 'top', leave: 'end' })
```

### Instant

A toast with `instant: true` skips all of it — no slide, no fade, no glide of its neighbours, no stack transition — and so does every toast when the user prefers reduced motion: the stylesheet emits no transitions under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and the toaster skips its position animations, so toasts appear, move and vanish in place.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-3 mb-4">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary" id="toasterInstantBtn">Add an instant toast</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" id="toasterAnimatedBtn">Add an animated toast</button>
</div>
<div class="toast-container position-static" id="toasterInstant"></div>
```

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster('#toasterInstant', { timeout: 3000 })

document.getElementById('toasterInstantBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({ title: 'Instant', description: 'No slide, no fade, no glide.', instant: true })
})

document.getElementById('toasterAnimatedBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
  toaster.add({ title: 'Animated', description: 'Slides in and glides the others.' })
})
```

## Placement

`placement` pins the container the toaster creates to the viewport with one of the nine [`.toast-container-{block}-{inline}`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/toasts/#placement) classes: `top`, `middle` or `bottom` × `start`, `center` or `end`. In the `top` placements a new toast is inserted first, in the others last, so the newest always sits closest to the edge.

Each button below adds a toast through a toaster placed at that spot, so you can see where a toast enters from: from the side in the `start` and `end` columns, from above in `top-center` and from below in `bottom-center`, while `middle-center` fades in place.

```html
<div class="d-grid gap-3" style="grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); max-width: 30rem" id="toasterPlacement">
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-start">Top start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-center">Top center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="top-end">Top end</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-start">Middle start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-center">Middle center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="middle-end">Middle end</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-start">Bottom start</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-center">Bottom center</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary" data-coreui-placement="bottom-end">Bottom end</button>
</div>
```

```js
const toasters = new Map()

for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('#toasterPlacement [data-coreui-placement]')) {
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const placement = button.dataset.coreuiPlacement

    if (!toasters.has(placement)) {
      toasters.set(placement, new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement }))
    }

    toasters.get(placement).add({ title: placement, description: 'Slides in from the nearest edge.' })
  })
}
```

A container you pass in is used as is — position it yourself:

```js
const inline = new coreui.Toaster('#notifications')
```

## Accessibility

The container is a `region` landmark named by `ariaLabel` (`Notifications` by default), so screen-reader users can jump to it through landmark navigation. Every toast is read through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) when it is added or updated: its `title` and `description` go to the polite live region of the page, or to the assertive one with `priority: 'high'`, as a message of their own, so toasts raised together are each announced instead of the last one overwriting the others. The message is sent once and belongs to the page, not to the container, so it still reaches the region when the toaster is disposed right after, and while a modal dialog is open it goes to a region inside that dialog, the one the toaster sits in included. Updating or removing a toast takes its message out of the region. Only that text is announced, never the close button or the action, and the toast element itself carries no live role. A toast added while a modal dialog plays its closing transition, or from `hidden.coreui.modal`, is announced on the page half a second after the dialog has closed, once the page is back for the screen reader; [Announcing messages](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages) has the measurements. The close button is named by `ariaCloseLabel` (`Close` by default); set it once for the whole toaster in a translated interface. `normal`, the default, waits until the user is idle, unless the toast is added together with a `high` one, which takes both to the assertive region; keep `high` for the few messages that should interrupt, such as a failed save (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages).

Auto-hiding is a time limit on reading, which WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable asks you to let the user turn off, adjust or extend. Timers stop while the pointer or focus is inside the container (`pauseOnHover`), so a spread stack or a toast being read does not disappear mid-way, and the default `timeout` is the toaster's to set for the whole page. A toast with an action, or one the user must act on, should not hide on its own: give it `timeout: 0`, so keyboard and screen-reader users can reach the button. Toasts never take focus.

## Usage

Create a toaster once and keep the instance; every toast on the page goes through it.

```js
const toaster = new coreui.Toaster(null, { placement: 'bottom-end', limit: 3 })
const id = toaster.add({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your changes are live.', theme: 'success' })
```

### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | [Default value](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript#sanitizer) | Tags and attributes allowed in toast content when `html` is `true`. |
| `ariaCloseLabel` | string | `'Close'` | Accessible name of every toast's close button. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `'Notifications'` | Accessible name of the container's `region` landmark. |
| `container` | string, element | `'body'` | Where the toaster appends the container it creates. Ignored when the toaster is given an existing element. |
| `enter` | string | `'auto'` | Edge a toast slides in from: `'start'`, `'end'`, `'top'` or `'bottom'`. `'start'` and `'end'` are logical and follow the direction the container sits in. `'auto'` follows the placement — the side in the `start` and `end` columns, above in `top-center`, below in `bottom-center`, and no slide at all in `middle-center`. |
| `html` | boolean | `false` | Render `title` and `description` as HTML instead of text. |
| `leave` | string | `'auto'` | Edge a toast slides out to, taking the same values as `enter`. `'auto'` is the edge it came in from. |
| `limit` | number | `3` | How many toasts stay visible; the oldest beyond it are hidden and `inert` until a slot frees. `0` disables the limit. |
| `pauseOnHover` | boolean | `true` | Pause every toast's timer while the pointer or focus is inside the container, and resume when it leaves. Each toast still pauses on its own hover and focus. |
| `placement` | string | `'top-end'` | Corner or edge of the viewport for the container the toaster creates: `top`, `middle` or `bottom` × `start`, `center` or `end`. Toasts in the `top` placements are inserted first, in the others last, so the newest always sits closest to the edge. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Sanitize HTML content. |
| `sanitizeFn` | null, function | `null` | Your own sanitizer, used instead of the built-in one. |
| `stack` | boolean | `false` | Stack the toasts on top of each other, newest in front, and spread them out on hover or focus. |
| `timeout` | number | `5000` | Default time (ms) before a toast hides. `0` keeps toasts until they are closed. |

### Toast options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | object, null | — | `{ label, onClick(event, toast) }` renders a button in the body. |
| `class` | string | — | Extra classes on the `.toast`. |
| `data` | object | — | Anything you want to read back from the toast object later, e.g. in `update(id, previous => …)`. |
| `description` | string, element, function | — | Body of the toast. |
| `dismissible` | boolean | `true` | Render the close button. |
| `id` | string | generated | Stable id; adding with an existing id updates that toast in place, unless it is already closing, in which case a new toast replaces it. |
| `instant` | boolean | `false` | Skip the fade (`.toast-instant`). |
| `onClose` | function | — | Called when the toast starts hiding, with the toast object. |
| `onRemove` | function | — | Called after the toast left the DOM, with the toast object. |
| `priority` | string | `'normal'` | Which live region announces the toast, as in [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages): `'normal'` the polite one, `'high'` the assertive one, which also takes the normal toasts added together with it. |
| `theme` | string | — | Adds `theme-{color}`. |
| `timeout` | number | toaster's `timeout` | Time (ms) before this toast hides; `0` keeps it. |
| `title` | string, element, function | — | Header of the toast, with the close button next to it. |
| `translucent` | boolean | `false` | Adds `.toast-translucent`. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add(options)` | Renders and shows a toast. Returns its id. With an `id` that already exists it behaves like `update`, unless that toast is already closing. |
| `close(id?)` | Hides the toast, which removes it from the DOM and the store once the fade ends. Without an id, hides every toast. |
| `dispose` | Removes every toast, and the container if the toaster created it. |
| `getInstance` | *Static* method that returns the toaster bound to a container element. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | *Static* method that returns the toaster bound to a container element or creates one on it. |
| `getToasts()` | The toast objects in insertion order, each with `id`, `updateKey`, `limited`, `element` and the options it was created with. |
| `pause()` / `resume()` | Stop and restart every toast's timer; `pauseOnHover` calls these for the container. |
| `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | Adds a toast in the `loading` state and updates it when the promise settles: `success` gets the resolved value, `error` the rejection. Each state is a description string or a full options object, or a function returning either. Returns the promise. |
| `update(id, options)` | Rewrites the toast in place and increments its `updateKey`. `options` may be a function receiving the current toast object and returning the changes. |

### Events

Events fire on the container. Each toast still fires the [toast events](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/toasts/#events) on its own element.

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add.coreui.toaster` | Fired after a toast was added; `event.id` is its id. |
| `remove.coreui.toaster` | Fired after a toast left the DOM; `event.id` is its id. |

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The toaster renders regular toasts, so their tokens apply — see the [toast CSS variables](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/toasts/#css-variables). Four are its own: `--cui-toast-container-inset` on the container sets the distance from the viewport edge, `--cui-toast-translate` on the container is where a toast enters from and leaves to, overridden separately by `--cui-toast-enter-translate` and `--cui-toast-leave-translate` (the `enter` and `leave` options write those; set them yourself for any other offset), `--cui-toast-inline-sign` on the container is the `1` or `-1` those inline offsets are multiplied by, which is how `start` and `end` follow the direction, and `--cui-toast-limited-translate` on a toast sets where a toast over the limit sinks to.

```scss
--cui-toast-zindex: var(--cui-z-toast);
--cui-toast-container-inset: #{var(--cui-spacer-5)};
--cui-toast-inline-sign: 1;
--cui-toast-max-width: #{350px};
--cui-toast-spacing: #{$container-padding-x};
--cui-toast-transition-duration: #{.3s};
--cui-toast-transition-timing: #{ease-out};
```

The stack's peek, scale step and folded count are tokens on `.toast-container-stack`:

```scss
.toast-container-stack {
  --cui-toast-stack-peek: .75rem;
  --cui-toast-stack-scale: .1;
  // Every toast behind is scaled by the same ratio again and pushed towards a vanishing depth,
  // so the corners of the stack line up and each strip is the previous one times the ratio
  --cui-toast-stack-visible: 3;
  --cui-toast-stack-ratio: calc(1 - var(--cui-toast-stack-scale));
  --cui-toast-stack-depth: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-front-height) + var(--cui-toast-stack-peek) / var(--cui-toast-stack-scale));
  --cui-toast-stack-last: calc(min(var(--cui-toast-stack-count), var(--cui-toast-stack-visible)) - 1);

  width: var(--cui-toast-max-width);
  max-width: 100%;
  height: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-depth) * (1 - pow(var(--cui-toast-stack-ratio), var(--cui-toast-stack-last))) + var(--cui-toast-stack-front-height) * pow(var(--cui-toast-stack-ratio), var(--cui-toast-stack-last)));
  pointer-events: auto;
  @include transition-props(height, var(--cui-toast-transition-duration), var(--cui-toast-transition-timing));

  > .toast {
    position: absolute;
    inset-block-start: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-depth) * (1 - pow(var(--cui-toast-stack-ratio), var(--cui-toast-stack-index))));
    inset-inline: 0;
    z-index: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-count) - var(--cui-toast-stack-index));
    height: var(--cui-toast-stack-front-height);
    margin-block-end: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    transform-origin: top center;
    scale: pow(var(--cui-toast-stack-ratio), var(--cui-toast-stack-index));

    &:not(.toast-instant) {
      @include transition-props(
        #{"opacity, translate, display, inset-block-start, height, scale"},
        var(--cui-toast-transition-duration),
        var(--cui-toast-transition-timing),
        allow-discrete
      );

      > * {
        @include transition-props(opacity, var(--cui-toast-transition-duration), var(--cui-toast-transition-timing));
      }
    }
  }

  > .toast:not([data-coreui-stack-index="0"]) {
    --cui-toast-leave-translate: 0 0;
    --cui-toast-limited-translate: 0 0;

    > * {
      opacity: 0;
    }
  }

  > .toast[data-coreui-stack-hidden] {
    pointer-events: none;
    opacity: 0;
  }

  &:is(:hover, :focus-within) {
    height: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-heights) + (var(--cui-toast-stack-count) - 1) * var(--cui-toast-spacing));

    > .toast {
      inset-block-start: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-before) + var(--cui-toast-stack-index) * var(--cui-toast-spacing));
      height: var(--cui-toast-height);
      scale: 1;

      > * {
        opacity: 1;
      }
    }

    > .toast[data-coreui-stack-hidden]:not([data-coreui-limited]) {
      pointer-events: auto;
      opacity: 1;
    }
  }
}

.toast-container-bottom-start.toast-container-stack,
.toast-container-bottom-center.toast-container-stack,
.toast-container-bottom-end.toast-container-stack {
  > .toast {
    inset-block-start: auto;
    inset-block-end: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-depth) * (1 - pow(var(--cui-toast-stack-ratio), var(--cui-toast-stack-index))));
    transform-origin: bottom center;

    &:not(.toast-instant) {
      @include transition-props(
        #{"opacity, translate, display, inset-block-end, height, scale"},
        var(--cui-toast-transition-duration),
        var(--cui-toast-transition-timing),
        allow-discrete
      );
    }
  }

  &:is(:hover, :focus-within) > .toast {
    inset-block-end: calc(var(--cui-toast-stack-before) + var(--cui-toast-stack-index) * var(--cui-toast-spacing));
  }
}
```

### Sass variables

```scss
$toast-background-color:            var(--cui-bg-body) !default;
$toast-border-color:                var(--cui-border-color-translucent) !default;
```

# Bootstrap 6 Tooltip

> Use Bootstrap Tooltips to add small, informative text boxes that appear when users hover or focus on an element. This feature enhances UX by providing contextual help without cluttering your interface.

## Overview

Things to keep in mind when using the Bootstrap tooltip plugin:

- Our tooltips depend on the third-party library [Floating UI](https://floating-ui.com/) for positioning. You need to include [floating-ui.core.umd.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@floating-ui/core@1.8.0/dist/floating-ui.core.umd.min.js) and [floating-ui.dom.umd.min.js](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@floating-ui/dom@1.8.0/dist/floating-ui.dom.umd.min.js) (in this order) before `coreui.js` or use `coreui.bundle.min.js/coreui.bundle.js`, which includes Floating UI to ensure tooltips function correctly!
- Tooltips are optional for performance reasons, so you need to initialize them yourself.
- Bootstrap Tooltips with empty titles are never displayed.
- Specify `container: 'body'` to prevent rendering issues in more complex components (such as our input groups, button groups, etc.).
- Bootstrap tooltips cannot be triggered on hidden elements.
- Tooltips for elements that are `.disabled` or `disabled` need to be activated on a wrapper element.
- When triggered by hyperlinks that span multiple lines, tooltips will be centered. Use `white-space: nowrap;` on your `<a>` elements to avoid this behavior.
- Tooltips must be hidden before the related elements are removed from the DOM.
- Our Bootstrap tooltips can be triggered thanks to an element inside a shadow DOM.

Got all that? Awesome! Now, let's explore how they work through some examples.

> By default, this component utilizes the built-in content sanitizer, which removes any HTML elements that are not explicitly allowed. Refer to the [sanitizer section in our JavaScript documentation](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#sanitizer) for more details.

> This component's animation effect relies on the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. For more information, refer to the [reduced motion section of our accessibility documentation](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/reduced-motion/).

Got all that? Great, let's see how they work with some examples.

## Examples

### Enable Bootstrap tooltips

You can enable tooltips using JavaScript or data attributes. Here's how to initialize all tooltip elements on a page:

```js
const tooltipTriggerList = document.querySelectorAll('[data-coreui-toggle="tooltip"]')
const tooltipList = [...tooltipTriggerList].map(tooltipTriggerEl => new coreui.Tooltip(tooltipTriggerEl))
```

### Tooltips on links

Hover your cursor over the links below to see tooltips:

> You can choose to use either `title` or `data-coreui-title` in your HTML. If you opt for `title,` the plugin will automatically change it to `data-coreui-title` upon rendering the element.

### Custom tooltips

_Added in 4.2.0._

Feel free to personalize the look of your tooltips with [CSS variables](#css-variables)! By setting a custom class using `data-coreui-custom-class="custom-tooltip"`, you can easily define your custom style and use it to adjust a local CSS variable.

```scss
.custom-tooltip {
  --cui-tooltip-bg: var(--cui-primary);
}
```

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-outline"
        data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="top"
        data-coreui-custom-class="custom-tooltip"
        data-coreui-title="This top tooltip is themed via CSS variables.">
  Custom tooltip
</button>
```

### Theme variants

A tooltip reads the `.theme-{color}` slots, so a [theme class](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/customize/components/#theme-variants) on the tip colors its surface and picks the contrasting text. The class lands on the tip through `data-coreui-custom-class`; without one the tip keeps its default look, the page's foreground color.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-custom-class="theme-primary" data-coreui-title="Primary tooltip">Primary</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-custom-class="theme-secondary" data-coreui-title="Secondary tooltip">Secondary</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-custom-class="theme-success" data-coreui-title="Success tooltip">Success</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-custom-class="theme-danger" data-coreui-title="Danger tooltip">Danger</button>
```

### Positioning

Tooltips support four placements: `top`, `end`, `bottom` and `start`. The default is `top`. Set them with the `data-coreui-placement` attribute:

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="top" title="Tooltip on top">Tooltip on top</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="end" title="Tooltip at the end">Tooltip at the end</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="bottom" title="Tooltip on bottom">Tooltip on bottom</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="start" title="Tooltip at the start">Tooltip at the start</button>
```

`start` and `end` are logical: they follow the reading direction, so `end` is the right side in LTR and the left side in RTL. The same names place a [menu](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/menu/) and a [dropdown](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/dropdown/).

#### Deprecated physical names

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

`left` and `right` still work and behave exactly like `start` and `end` — they have always mirrored in RTL, so `right` never meant "the right side" there either. The logical names say that plainly; the physical ones are removed in v7.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="right" title="Tooltip on right">Tooltip on right</button>
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="left" title="Tooltip on left">Tooltip on left</button>
```

### Responsive placement

Change placement at different breakpoints using responsive prefixes. The syntax is `breakpoint:placement`, where breakpoint is one of `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, or `2xl`. Multiple breakpoints can be combined in a single attribute, space-separated — a bare placement with no prefix is the one below the smallest listed breakpoint.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-placement="top md:right lg:bottom" data-coreui-title="Responsive tooltip">
  Top, then right, then bottom
</button>
```

### Tooltips with HTML Content

Bootstrap Tooltips support HTML content, allowing you to insert styled elements like `<em>`, `<strong>`, or `<u>` directly inside the tooltip. This feature is useful when you want to emphasize certain words, add inline formatting, or even insert icons.

To enable this, set the `data-coreui-html="true"` attribute and include valid HTML in the title attribute. Be mindful of security when injecting dynamic content.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-outline" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" data-coreui-html="true" title="<em>Tooltip</em> <u>with</u> <b>HTML</b>">
  Tooltip with HTML
</button>
```

This will render a styled tooltip that interprets the HTML tags instead of treating them as plain text. HTML tooltips are especially handy when you need richer formatting within a compact UI hint.

### Tooltips on SVG Elements

Applying Bootstrap Tooltips to SVG elements requires a different approach, since SVGs do not support the `title` attribute in the same way HTML elements do. To show tooltips on SVG icons or shapes, you must initialize them manually using JavaScript.

It’s recommended to set the container option to `'body'` to avoid positioning issues, especially when SVGs are nested inside complex layouts.

```html
<a href="#" class="d-inline-block" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" title="Default tooltip">
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="50" height="50" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
    <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#563d7c"/>
    <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="30" fill="#007bff"/>
  </svg>
</a>
```

Using Bootstrap Tooltips with SVGs is a great way to enhance accessibility and interactivity for icon-based UIs or data visualizations without modifying the structure of your SVGs.

## Usage

The tooltip plugin creates content and markup as needed, and by default places tooltips following their trigger elements.

Trigger the tooltip via JavaScript:

```js
const exampleEl = document.getElementById('example')
const tooltip = new coreui.Tooltip(exampleEl, options)
```

> ##### Overflow `auto` and `scroll`
> 
> When a parent container has `overflow: auto` or `overflow: scroll`, such as with our `.table-responsive`, the tooltip position attempts to adjust automatically while maintaining its original placement. To fix this, set the `boundary` option to any HTMLElement to replace the default value, `'clippingParents'`, like `document.body`:
> 
> ```js
> const tooltip = new coreui.Tooltip('#example', {
> boundary: document.body // or document.querySelector('#boundary')
> })
> ```

### Markup

The markup needed for a tooltip consists solely of a `data` attribute and a `title` on the HTML element you want to display a tooltip. The markup generated for a tooltip is quite simple, although it does require a position, which is set to `top` by default in the plugin.

> ##### Making tooltips work for keyboard and assistive technology users
> 
> Only add tooltips to HTML elements that are inherently keyboard-focusable and interactive, like links or form controls. While it is possible to make arbitrary HTML elements like ``s focusable by using the `tabindex="0"` attribute, doing so may create confusing tab stops on non-interactive elements for keyboard users. Moreover, most assistive technologies typically do not announce tooltips in these cases. Additionally, avoid depending solely on `hover` to trigger your tooltips, as this approach renders them inaccessible for keyboard users.

A shown tooltip can be dismissed by pressing the <kbd>Escape</kbd> key, and a hover- or focus-triggered tooltip stays open while the pointer or focus is over the trigger or the tip itself — so users can reach interactive content inside it, such as a link. It hides when the pointer leaves both. A focus-triggered tooltip also stays open after a press inside it, for example to select its text, and hides on the next click outside or when focus moves elsewhere. Together these satisfy the [WCAG 1.4.13 "Content on Hover or Focus"](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html) success criterion (dismissable, hoverable, persistent).

```html
<!-- HTML to write -->
<a href="#" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" title="Some tooltip text!">Hover over me</a>

<!-- Generated markup by the plugin -->
<div class="tooltip bs-tooltip-auto" role="tooltip">
  <div class="tooltip-arrow"></div>
  <div class="tooltip-inner">
    Some tooltip text!
  </div>
</div>
```

### Disabled elements

Elements that have the `disabled` attribute are non-interactive, which prevents users from focusing, hovering, or clicking on them to display a tooltip (or popover). To address this, consider triggering the tooltip from a surrounding `<div>` or `<span>`, preferably making it keyboard-focusable by using `tabindex="0"`.

```html
<span class="d-inline-block" tabindex="0" data-coreui-toggle="tooltip" title="Disabled tooltip">
  <button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="button" disabled>Disabled button</button>
</span>
```

### Options

Options can be passed using data attributes or JavaScript. To do this, append an option name to `data-coreui-`, such as `data-coreui-animation="{value}"`. Remember to convert the case of the option name from "_camelCase_" to "_kebab-case_" when using data attributes. For instance, you should write `data-coreui-custom-class="beautifier"` rather than `data-coreui-customClass="beautifier"`.

Starting with CoreUI 4.2.6, all components support an **experimental** reserved data attribute named `data-coreui-config`, which can contain simple component configurations as a JSON string. If an element has attributes `data-coreui-config='{"delay":50, "title":689}'` and `data-coreui-title="Custom Title"`, then the final value for `title` will be `Custom Title`, as the standard data attributes will take precedence over values specified in `data-coreui-config`. Moreover, existing data attributes can also hold JSON values like `data-coreui-delay='{"show":50, "hide":250}'`.

> Please note that for security reasons, the `sanitize`, `sanitizeFn`, and `allowList` options cannot be supplied via data attributes.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | [Default value](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#sanitizer) | Defines the set of permitted HTML tags and attributes that can safely appear in the tooltip content when HTML rendering is enabled. This helps maintain control over the output and prevent injection of malicious code. |
| `animation` | boolean | `true` | Determines whether the tooltip should fade in and out using a CSS transition. Set to `false` for instant show/hide behavior, which may be preferable for performance-sensitive interfaces — it renders `.tooltip-instant`, the same class you can put in a custom `template`. Retime the fade with `--cui-tooltip-transition-duration` and `--cui-tooltip-transition-timing`. |
| `boundary` | string, element | `'clippingParents'` | Determines the boundary within which the tooltip must remain visible. Can be a specific element or the default `'clippingParents'`. This setting helps avoid unwanted clipping or overflow. For more information refer to Floating UI's [detectOverflow docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/detectOverflow/#boundary). |
| `container` | string, element, false | `false` | Specifies the parent container in which the tooltip should be inserted. Commonly used value is `'body'`, which helps avoid layout or overflow issues by ensuring the tooltip isn't clipped by parent elements. |
| `customClass` | string, function | `''` | Allows adding one or more custom CSS classes to the tooltip when it's rendered. Accepts a string with class names or a callback function that returns the class string. Useful for styling variants (e.g. light vs dark). |
| `delay` | number, object | `0` | Defines how long (in milliseconds) to wait before showing or hiding the tooltip. A single number applies to both actions, or you can provide an object like `{ show: 500, hide: 200 }` for separate control over each. |
| `fallbackPlacements` | string, array | `['top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left']` | Specifies alternative placements for the tooltip if the preferred one isn't feasible (e.g., due to lack of space). The tooltip will try these placements in order until one fits. For more information refer to Floating UI's [flip docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/flip/#fallbackplacements). |
| `floatingConfig` | null, object, function | `null` | Allows you to override or extend the default Floating UI configuration used by the tooltip. Can be an object or a function that receives the default config and returns a modified one, giving you full control over tooltip behavior and positioning logic. See Floating UI's [computePosition docs](https://floating-ui.com/docs/computePosition/#options).|
| `html` | boolean | `false` | Enables support for HTML content inside the tooltip. When set to `true`, the `title` attribute may include tags like `<strong>`, `<em>`, or even icons. Be cautious with untrusted content as it increases XSS risk. |
| `offset` | array, string, function | `[0, 6]` | Defines how far the tooltip should be offset from the target element. Use a string like `data-coreui-offset="10,20"` in attributes or pass a function to calculate the offset based on context. Floating UI's offset middleware is used under the hood. |
| `placement` | string, function | `'top'` | Sets the tooltip’s position relative to its target element: `'top'`, `'end'`, `'bottom'`, `'start'` or `'auto'`, plus responsive variants such as `'top md:end'`. `'left'` and `'right'` are the deprecated spellings of `'start'` and `'end'`. With `'auto'` the tooltip reorients itself. You can also pass a function for dynamic placement based on element size or context. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Controls whether HTML content in the tooltip should be sanitized before rendering. Strongly recommended to leave enabled unless you’re fully managing the content and trust its source. |
| `sanitizeFn` | null, function | `null` | You can define your own custom sanitization logic by passing a function here. Ideal if you want to use a specialized HTML sanitizer or integrate with existing security tools. If activated `'template'`, `'content'` and `'title'` options will be sanitized. |
| `selector` | string, false | `false` | Used to delegate tooltip activation to child elements within a container. This is particularly useful when you’re dynamically adding elements to the DOM that require tooltips. Note: the `title` attribute itself should not be used as a selector. |
| `template` | string | `'<div class="tooltip" role="tooltip"><div class="tooltip-arrow"></div><div class="tooltip-inner"></div></div>'` | Provides the HTML structure used to generate the tooltip. You can override it to include custom classes or elements. The `title` content is placed inside `.tooltip-inner`, and `.tooltip-arrow` is the visual pointer. |
| `title` | string, element, function | `''` | The content displayed inside the tooltip. If a value is not provided, the component will fall back to the `title` attribute on the element. You can also provide a function that returns the content dynamically.|
| `trigger` | string | `'hover focus'` | Determines which user interactions will cause the tooltip to show. Options include `click`, `hover`, `focus`, or `manual`. Multiple triggers can be combined using a space-separated string. Use `manual` for full programmatic control. |

> #### Data attributes for individual tooltips
> 
> Options for individual tooltips can alternatively be specified through the use of data attributes, as explained above.

#### Using function with `floatingConfig`

```js
const tooltip = new coreui.Tooltip(element, {
  floatingConfig(defaultConfig) {
    // const newConfig = {...}
    // use defaultConfig if needed...
    // return newConfig
  }
})
```

### Methods

> #### Promises and transitions
> 
> **Methods that show or hide a component return a promise.** The promise resolves when the transition ends, so `await` continues at the same moment a `shown.coreui.*` or `hidden.coreui.*` listener runs. The methods still return immediately and never block the caller. A call on a component that is already transitioning does nothing and resolves right away.
> 
> [Refer to our JavaScript documentation for further details](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/getting-started/javascript/#promises-and-transitions).

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `disable` | Disables the tooltip from being triggered. This includes both manual and automatic triggers until it's enabled again. |
| `dispose` | Completely removes the tooltip instance from the target element. It clears event listeners and internal data. Tooltips created using delegation (e.g., via `selector`) cannot be destroyed on individual children. |
| `enable` | Gives an element’s tooltip the ability to be shown. All tooltips are enabled by default unless manually disabled. |
| `getInstance` | *Static* method that retrieves the current tooltip instance tied to a specific element. Returns `null` if the tooltip has not been initialized. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | *Static* method that either returns the existing tooltip instance or initializes a new one if none exists. Ensures consistent behavior in dynamic interfaces. |
| `hide` | Hides the tooltip from view when triggered programmatically. Similar to `show`, this method is asynchronous and returns before the hiding animation finishes. **Returns a promise that resolves after the tooltip is hidden** (i.e. after the `hidden.coreui.tooltip` event occurs). |
| `setContent` | Dynamically changes the content of an existing tooltip without reinitializing the instance. Useful for updating text based on user action or application state. |
| `show` | Manually displays the Bootstrap tooltip linked to an element. This method is non-blocking—it returns immediately, even though the tooltip will appear shortly after. If the tooltip’s title is empty, nothing will be shown. **Returns a promise that resolves after the tooltip is shown** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.tooltip` event occurs) |
| `toggle` | Programmatically shows or hides a tooltip based on its current visibility state. Like `show` and `hide`, this method executes immediately and the visual change happens afterward. **Returns a promise that resolves after the tooltip is shown or hidden** (i.e. after the `shown.coreui.tooltip` or `hidden.coreui.tooltip` event occurs). |
| `toggleEnabled` | Switches the ability for an element’s tooltip to be shown or hidden. |
| `update` | Recalculates and repositions the tooltip, ensuring correct alignment if the DOM has changed (e.g., due to scroll, resize, or dynamic layout updates). |

```js
const tooltip = coreui.Tooltip.getInstance('#example') // Returns a Bootstrap tooltip instance

// setContent example
tooltip.setContent({ '.tooltip-inner': 'another title' })

```

> The `setContent` method accepts an `object` argument, where each property-key is a valid `string` selector within the popover template, and each related property-value can be `string` | `element` | `function` | `null`

### Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `hidden.coreui.tooltip` | Dispatched once the tooltip has been fully removed from view and CSS transitions (if any) have finished. Ideal for cleanup logic or analytics. |
| `hide.coreui.tooltip` | Emitted immediately when the `hide()` method is called. At this point, the tooltip is still visible but is beginning the process of being hidden. |
| `inserted.coreui.tooltip` | Occurs after the tooltip has been injected into the DOM but before it becomes visible. This event gives you access to the generated tooltip element for advanced DOM manipulation. |
| `show.coreui.tooltip` | Triggered right after the `show()` method is invoked. The tooltip is about to become visible, but hasn't been inserted into the DOM yet. You can use this event to perform actions before the tooltip is rendered. |
| `shown.coreui.tooltip` | Fired after the tooltip is fully visible and any CSS transitions (like fade) have completed. Useful for tracking when the user can actually see the Bootstrap tooltip. |

```js
const myTooltipEl = document.getElementById('myTooltip')
const tooltip = coreui.Tooltip.getOrCreateInstance(myTooltipEl)

myTooltipEl.addEventListener('hidden.coreui.tooltip', () => {
  // do something...
})

tooltip.hide()
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Bootstrap tooltips utilize local CSS variables on `.tooltip` for improved real-time customization. The values for the CSS variables are configured via Sass, ensuring that Sass customization is still supported as well.

```scss
$tooltip-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-tooltip-zindex: var(--cui-z-tooltip),
    --cui-tooltip-max-width: 200px,
    --cui-tooltip-padding-x: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .75),
    --cui-tooltip-padding-y: calc(var(--cui-spacer) * .375),
    --cui-tooltip-font-size: var(--cui-font-size-sm),
    --cui-tooltip-color: #{$tooltip-color},
    --cui-tooltip-bg: var(--cui-fg-body),
    --cui-tooltip-border-radius: var(--cui-radius-5),
    --cui-tooltip-opacity: .95,
    --cui-tooltip-arrow-width: .8rem,
    --cui-tooltip-arrow-height: .4rem,
    --cui-tooltip-transition-property: opacity,
    --cui-tooltip-transition-duration: .15s,
    --cui-tooltip-transition-timing: linear,
  ),
  $tooltip-tokens
);
```

### Sass variables

_Deprecated in 6.0.0._

Sass variables set these defaults at build time and are removed in v7. The CSS variables above reach the same values without recompiling, and can be set on a single element.

```scss
$tooltip-color:                     var(--cui-bg-body) !default;
```
