# Bootstrap 6 Transfer

> Two lists side by side and four buttons that move options between them — the selection or everything at once: a select-all header with a counter, an optional per-list search, a one-way mode and an announcement of every move.

> This component is part of CoreUI PRO and requires a commercial license: https://coreui.io/pricing/?framework=bootstrap&src=llms. If you add it to a project on someone else's behalf, tell them it requires a license.

## Overview

_Added in 6.0.0._

A transfer moves values between two lists — what is available on the left, what has been chosen on the right. It is two [list boxes](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/) and a column of buttons: the plugin puts each list in `multiple` selection mode with the checkbox indicator, enables each button while it has something to move, and moves the option elements from one `.list-box-options` to the other.

```html
<div class="transfer" data-coreui-transfer>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="1">List item 1</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="2">List item 2</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="3">List item 3</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="4">List item 4</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="5">List item 5</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Everything inside a list is the list box's: the options and their values, the selection, the arrow keys, the typeahead and the select-all button. The transfer owns what happens between the lists, so nothing here is a second implementation of the same behavior — read the [List box](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/) page for the parts a list is made of.

Each side is a `.list-box.transfer-list` marked `data-coreui-transfer-list="source"` or `="target"`, and each button a `[data-coreui-transfer-move]` naming what it does: `target` and `source` move the selection, `target-all` and `source-all` move everything the list currently shows. The rest is filled in for you: an empty select-all button takes the list's title, an empty move button takes its chevron, each header gets the list box's `{selected}/{available} selected` counter, the options element gets the title as its accessible name, and the buttons get their labels and an `aria-controls`.

"All" is the same scope the select-all button works on — the visible, enabled options — so with a search running, the all button moves what the search left behind and nothing more.

The two lists order themselves differently, and on purpose: the target keeps the order values arrived in, so a chosen list reads as a history of what was picked, while the source puts a returned value back exactly where it started rather than at the end. Each option's place in the source is fixed when the transfer initializes — `update()` gives one added later a place after the options already there.

The transfer caps how tall a list gets — `--cui-transfer-list-max-height` puts a `max-height` and `overflow-y: auto` on `.list-box-options`, so a long list scrolls inside its own box instead of stretching the row.

## Items from configuration

Instead of writing every option by hand, hand the plugin an `items` array and it renders both lists — the same markup the sections above document, so every class, role and attribute is where you would have put it. An item is `{ value, label, description, disabled, selected }`; an entry with its own `items` array is a section. `value` names what starts in the target list, in the order you list it, and everything else lands in the source in the order the items came in — including a value moved back later, which returns to its place among the items rather than to the end.

Labels are text: they land as `textContent`, so a label carrying markup shows up as characters. Set `html: true` to have them parsed instead — the result runs through the sanitizer first, and `sanitize`, `sanitizeFn` and `allowList` steer it the same way they do everywhere else.

Leave an empty `.list-box-options` in each list so you can name it; the plugin appends one when it is missing, but then the list has no accessible name. Options already written inside it are replaced — `items` owns both lists from the moment it is set.

```html
<div class="transfer" id="transferItems">
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox" aria-label="Team"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox" aria-label="On call"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const element = document.getElementById('transferItems')

coreui.Transfer.getOrCreateInstance(element, {
  items: [
    {
      label: 'Engineering',
      items: [
        { value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace', description: 'Analyst' },
        { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper', description: 'Compilers' },
        {
          value: 'alan', label: 'Alan Turing', description: 'Cryptanalysis', disabled: true
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      label: 'Design',
      items: [
        { value: 'ray', label: 'Ray Eames' },
        { value: 'dieter', label: 'Dieter Rams' }
      ]
    }
  ],
  sourceTitle: 'Team',
  targetTitle: 'On call',
  value: ['grace']
})
```

`setItems(items)` rebuilds both lists at any time: the values the target holds survive the rebuild as long as the new items still carry them, in the order they were chosen, and the rest go back to the source. A value that is gone drops out. `getItems()` hands back the array as it was given.

## Search

The search belongs to the list box — `search` and `searchPlaceholder` are passed to both of them, so each list gets its own field and filters itself; how it works, and how to bring your own input, is on the [List box](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/#search) page. What the transfer adds is that a filtered list still counts: the [counter](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/#counter) in the header reads only what the search left — on both sides of the slash, so a selected value it hid stops counting without being deselected — the select-all button takes only what is left on screen, and "all" moves exactly that.

```html
<div class="transfer" data-coreui-transfer data-coreui-search="true">
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="apple">Apple</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="apricot">Apricot</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="banana">Banana</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="blueberry">Blueberry</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="cherry">Cherry</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="cranberry">Cranberry</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## External search

`search: 'external'` hands the searching over to you — the [list box's external mode](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/#external-search) on both lists at once. The transfer re-emits what they report as `search.coreui.transfer`, adding the `side` that was typed in, and you answer with `setItems()` — one method for both lists, so pass the whole set you want shown and leave out what the query rules out. Values already in the target stay there as long as your set still carries them, which is why the example below keeps the chosen users in what it sends back.

`loading` covers the wait: `setLoading(true, 'source')` writes `aria-busy="true"` on that list's options element and shows a loading row with `loadingLabel` below its options until the answer arrives. The second argument is what scopes it — `setLoading(true)` and the `loading` option both cover *both* lists, so a list you never fetch for keeps its loading row until something releases it. Fetch one list, mark one list.

Rebuilding is a fresh start for the selection: after `setItems()` neither list has anything checked, and `selected` on an item applies to the first render only, so a re-fetch never brings the checkboxes back. Moving options across clears the destination's selection too — what arrives is ready to be picked, not already picked.

```html
<div class="transfer" id="transferExternalSearch">
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox" aria-label="Users"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox" aria-label="Invited"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```js
const element = document.getElementById('transferExternalSearch')
const transfer = coreui.Transfer.getOrCreateInstance(element, {
  search: 'external',
  sourceTitle: 'Users',
  targetTitle: 'Invited'
})

const invited = new Map()

const loadUsers = async (query = '') => {
  transfer.setLoading(true, 'source')

  try {
    const response = await fetch(`https://apitest.coreui.io/demos/users?first_name=${query}&limit=10`)
    const { records } = await response.json()
    const users = records.map(user => ({
      value: String(user.id),
      label: `${user.first_name} ${user.last_name}`,
      description: user.email
    }))
    const found = new Set(users.map(user => user.value))

    transfer.setItems([...users, ...[...invited.values()].filter(user => !found.has(user.value))])
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching users:', error)
    transfer.setItems([...invited.values()])
  } finally {
    transfer.setLoading(false, 'source')
  }
}

element.addEventListener('change.coreui.transfer', event => {
  const users = new Map(transfer.getItems().map(user => [user.value, user]))

  invited.clear()

  for (const value of event.value) {
    invited.set(value, users.get(value))
  }
})

let debounceTimer = null

element.addEventListener('search.coreui.transfer', event => {
  if (event.side !== 'source') {
    return
  }

  clearTimeout(debounceTimer)
  debounceTimer = setTimeout(() => loadUsers(event.query), 200)
})

loadUsers()
```

## One way

`oneWay` takes the return trip away: both buttons that move back are hidden, `moveToSource()` and `moveAllToSource()` refuse, and a value that has been chosen stays chosen.

## Disabled items

`.disabled` with `aria-disabled="true"` takes an option out of the keyboard order and out of every selection method, so it never moves. Starting checked is a selection method too: `selected: true` next to `disabled: true` is ignored, so no move button ever picks the option up. `data-coreui-disabled="true"` on the transfer does the same for all of it: both lists go quiet and both buttons are disabled.

```html
<div class="transfer" data-coreui-transfer>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="1">List item 1</div>
      <div class="list-box-option disabled" aria-disabled="true" data-coreui-value="2">List item 2 — locked</div>
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="3">List item 3</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

Each list is a listbox of its own with the title as its accessible name, and the select-all button carries the state of its list in `aria-pressed` — all of that comes from [List box](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/#accessibility), keyboard included: the arrows, <kbd>Home</kbd>, <kbd>End</kbd>, <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>Shift</kbd> ranges, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> and the typeahead all work inside the list that has the focus.

What the transfer adds is the crossing. Each move button is named — `ariaMoveToTargetLabel`, `ariaMoveToSourceLabel`, `ariaMoveAllToTargetLabel`, `ariaMoveAllToSourceLabel` (a button that already carries an `aria-label` keeps it) — points at the list it fills through `aria-controls`, and is disabled while it has nothing to move, so the keyboard never lands on a button that would do nothing. The chevrons are decorative `aria-hidden` SVGs, so the name is all a screen reader gets.

The move happens away from the focus, and the button that did it usually turns off in the process — a list with nothing selected left. Rather than dropping the focus on the document, the plugin puts it on the first option that just arrived.

Every move, either way, adds a message of its own to the live region of the page through [`announce()`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/screen-readers/#announcing-messages), the same move made twice included: `ariaMovedAnnouncement` is `'{count} moved to {title}'` by default, with `{title}` the destination's title. `{count}` and `{title}` are replaced wherever they appear, so the sentence can be reordered for a translation.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Move between the select-all button, the search field, the options and the move buttons |
| `↓` / `↑` | Move the highlight inside the focused list |
| `Space` | Toggle the highlighted option |
| `Shift` + `↓` / `↑` | Extend the selection inside the focused list |
| `Ctrl` / `Cmd` + `A` | Select every visible, enabled option of the focused list |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Move the selection when the focus is on a move button |

## Usage

### Via data attributes

Add `data-coreui-transfer` to a `.transfer` and the plugin initializes it on page load. Mark each `.list-box` with `data-coreui-transfer-list` and each button with `data-coreui-transfer-move`.

| Attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `data-coreui-transfer` | Initializes the transfer on page load. |
| `data-coreui-transfer-list` | Marks a `.list-box` as the `source` or the `target` list. |
| `data-coreui-transfer-move` | Marks a move button: `target` / `source` move the selection, `target-all` / `source-all` move every visible, enabled option. |

A move button left empty gets the chevron its direction calls for; put anything of your own in it — a label, your own icon — and that is what stays.

```html
<div class="transfer" data-coreui-transfer>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="source">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox">
      <div class="list-box-option" data-coreui-value="1">List item 1</div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="transfer-actions">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target-all"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="target"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source"></button>
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-subtle btn-sm" data-coreui-transfer-move="source-all"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="list-box transfer-list" data-coreui-transfer-list="target">
    <div class="list-box-header">
      <button type="button" class="list-box-select-all" data-coreui-select-all></button>
    </div>
    <div class="list-box-options" role="listbox"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Via JavaScript

```js
const transfer = new coreui.Transfer('#myTransfer', {
  search: true,
  sourceTitle: 'Team',
  targetTitle: 'On call'
})
```

### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowList` | object | `SVGAllowlist` | What the icon sanitizer keeps. |
| `ariaMoveAllToSourceLabel` | string | `'Move all to available'` | Accessible name of the button that moves everything back to the source list. |
| `ariaMoveAllToTargetLabel` | string | `'Move all to chosen'` | Accessible name of the button that moves everything to the target list. |
| `ariaMovedAnnouncement` | string | `'{count} moved to {title}'` | What is announced after a move. `{count}` is how many options moved, `{title}` the destination's title. |
| `ariaMoveToSourceLabel` | string | `'Move to available'` | Accessible name of the button that moves the selection back to the source list. A button with its own `aria-label` keeps it. |
| `ariaMoveToTargetLabel` | string | `'Move to chosen'` | Accessible name of the button that moves the selection to the target list. |
| `disabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns the whole transfer off: both list boxes, both move buttons and both search fields. |
| `html` | boolean | `false` | Parse the labels and descriptions of `items` as markup instead of text. Passed to both list boxes. |
| `indicator` | string | `'checkbox'` | Passed to both list boxes. `'none'` drops the checkbox in front of every option. |
| `items` | array | `[]` | The options of both lists, rendered instead of the markup: `{ value, label, description, disabled, selected }`, or `{ label, items, disabled }` for a section, where `disabled: true` keeps every item in it on its side. `value` decides which of them start in the target list, `selected` which start checked — on the first render only, and never a disabled item. |
| `loading` | boolean | `false` | Marks both lists as busy: `aria-busy="true"` on the options element and a loading row below the options, while the lists stay usable. Release it with `setLoading(false)`, or scope it per list with `setLoading(value, list)`. |
| `loadingLabel` | string | `'Loading…'` | Text of the loading row of a busy list, announced to screen readers when it starts loading. |
| `moveAllToSourceIcon` | string | double chevron SVG | Icon of the button that moves everything back. Inline SVG, put in the button only when the markup left it empty. |
| `moveAllToTargetIcon` | string | double chevron SVG | Icon of the button that moves everything across. |
| `moveToSourceIcon` | string | chevron SVG | Icon of the button that moves the selection back. |
| `moveToTargetIcon` | string | chevron SVG | Icon of the button that moves the selection across. |
| `oneWay` | boolean | `false` | Hides and disables both buttons that move back, and makes `moveToSource()` and `moveAllToSource()` no-ops. |
| `sanitize` | boolean | `true` | Run the icon strings through the sanitizer. |
| `sanitizeFn` | null, function | `null` | Your own sanitizer, used instead of the built-in one. |
| `search` | boolean, string | `false` | Passed to both list boxes: builds a search field above each list. `'external'` filters nothing — every keystroke fires `search.coreui.transfer` and you answer with `setItems()`. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | string | `'Search'` | Passed to both list boxes as the placeholder of their search field, and used as the first half of each field's accessible name so the two are told apart. |
| `selectedLabel` | string, function | `` (count, total) => `${count}/${total} selected` `` | Passed to both list boxes as their header count text. The transfer turns their [counter](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/list-box/#counter) on. |
| `sourceTitle` | string | `'Available'` | Title of the source list: its select-all label when the button is empty, and its accessible name. |
| `targetTitle` | string | `'Chosen'` | Title of the target list. |
| `typeahead` | boolean | `true` | Passed to both list boxes: move the highlight to the option matching what the user types. |
| `value` | array | `[]` | The values of `items` that start in the target list, in the order given. The rest go to the source list. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dispose` | Destroys the transfer and both list boxes, and removes the option containers it created. |
| `getInstance` | Static method which allows you to get the transfer instance associated to a DOM element, you can use it like this: `coreui.Transfer.getInstance(element)`. |
| `getItems()` | The items array both lists were built from. |
| `getOrCreateInstance` | Static method which returns a transfer instance associated to a DOM element or creates a new one in case it wasn't initialized. You can use it like this: `coreui.Transfer.getOrCreateInstance(element)`. |
| `getSelectedValues(list)` | The selected values of `'source'` or `'target'`. Throws when `list` is anything else. |
| `getSource()` | The values in the source list, in document order. |
| `getTarget()` | The values in the target list, in document order. |
| `moveAllToSource()` | The same in the other direction. Does nothing with `oneWay`. |
| `moveAllToTarget()` | Moves every visible, enabled option of the source list — the same scope the select-all button works on. |
| `moveToSource(values?)` | The same in the other direction. Does nothing with `oneWay`. |
| `moveToTarget(values?)` | Moves the source list's selection to the target list. Pass an array of values to move exactly those, selected or not. |
| `setItems(items)` | Rebuilds both lists from a new `items` array. The values the target holds keep their place as long as the new items still carry them; everything else goes to the source in the items order. Both selections come back empty. |
| `setLoading(loading, list?)` | Marks a list busy while you fetch: pass `'source'` or `'target'` for one of them, nothing for both. A list left busy keeps its loading row, so release every list you marked. |
| `update` | Re-reads the DOM: options added or removed reach both list boxes, which re-apply their search and counter, and the move buttons are re-evaluated. |

### Events

Events fire on the `.transfer` element.

| Event type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `change.coreui.transfer` | Fired after a move settled; `event.value` is the target list and `event.source` the source list. `event.target` stays the `.transfer` element. |
| `move.coreui.transfer` | Fires before options are moved; `event.direction` is `'source'` or `'target'` and `event.values` the values about to move. Cancelable — calling `preventDefault()` leaves both lists as they were. |
| `moved.coreui.transfer` | Fired after the options were moved, with the same `direction` and `values`. |
| `search.coreui.transfer` | Fired on every keystroke in a search field with `search: 'external'`; `event.side` is `'source'` or `'target'` and `event.query` what was typed. Nothing is filtered — answer with `setItems()`. |

```js
const myTransfer = document.getElementById('myTransfer')
myTransfer.addEventListener('change.coreui.transfer', event => {
  console.log(event.value)
})
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

```scss
$transfer-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-transfer-gap: 1rem,
    --cui-transfer-actions-gap: .5rem,
    --cui-transfer-icon-size: 1rem,
    --cui-transfer-list-min-height: 8rem,
    --cui-transfer-list-max-height: 16rem,
  ),
  $transfer-tokens
);
```

# CoreUI Icons

> CoreUI Icons is an open-source icon set with more than 500 icons in multiple formats SVG, PNG, and Webfonts. CoreUI Icons are beautifully crafted symbols for common actions and items. You can use them in your digital products for web or mobile app.

## Installation

### NPM

```sh
npm install @coreui/icons --save
```

### Yarn

```sh
yarn add @coreui/icons
```

Or, you can also clone or [download this repository](https://github.com/coreui/coreui-icons/archive/main.zip) as zip.

## Usage

### Basic Use

You can place CoreUI Icons just about anywhere using a CSS style prefix and the icon’s name. CoreUI Icons are designed to be used with inline elements ex. `<i>` or `<span>`.

Please use `cil-` prefix for linear icons, `cib-` prefix for brand icons, and `cif-` prefix for flag icons.

```html
<i class="cil-paperclip icon icon-xxl"></i>
<i class="cil-tag icon icon-xxl"></i>
```

### SVG Sprites

SVG sprites let you quickly use vector icons in your website. We have prepared all the icon set styles into their own SVG sprites.

Place sprite files with the rest of your static files, like images and styles, in your project. Make sure to add a proper path to the SVG sprite file, and use the fragment identifier specific to the SVG icon or symbol you want to display.

```html
<svg>
  <use xlink:href="path/to/free.svg#cil-airplane-mode"></use>
</svg>
<svg>
  <use xlink:href="path/to/brand.svg#cib-twitter"></use>
</svg>
<svg>
  <use xlink:href="path/to/flag.svg#cif-us"></use>
</svg>
```

### SVG Symbols

When you download your icon set, it comes with a symbols directory that contains SVG icon definitions. These icons can be referenced and used as inline SVGs like so:

```html
<!-- Define the symbols -->

<!-- Use the defined symbols -->
<svg>
  <use xlink:href="#cil-apple"></use>

```

It is also possible to link to an external SVG containing the definitions:

```html
<svg class="c-icon">
  <use xlink:href="path/to/free-symbol-defs.svg#cil-apple"></use>
</svg>
```

Referencing an external SVG has the advantage that your icons get cached, with one HTTP request. But the external SVG and the HTML should be served from the same domain. This approach works fine in modern browsers except for IE 9+. In order to support IE 9+, You should use `/js/svgxuse.js` or `/js/svgxuse.min.js`. This polyfill detects if the icons are loaded properly; if they aren't, it sends one HTTP request to fetch and cache symbol definitions.

## Sizing

Add `.icon-sm`, `.icon-lg`, `.icon-xl` or `.icon-xxl` to scale an icon against the base size, and `.icon-3xl` through `.icon-9xl` for whole multiples of it.

```html
<svg class="icon icon-sm"><use xlink:href="path/to/coreui-icons.svg#cil-apple"></use></svg>
<svg class="icon"><use xlink:href="path/to/coreui-icons.svg#cil-apple"></use></svg>
<svg class="icon icon-xxl"><use xlink:href="path/to/coreui-icons.svg#cil-apple"></use></svg>
```

## CoreUI Icons PRO

If our free icon set is insufficient you can buy [CoreUI Icons Pro](https://coreui.io/icons/#pricing-new) with more than 4000 icons, and more styles - Solid, Duo-Tone and Linear.

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Icons use local CSS variables on `.icon` for enhanced real-time customization. Each step is a multiple of `--cui-icon-size-base`, which is set on `:root`, so retuning the base moves every size with it.

```scss
$icon-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-icon-size: var(--cui-icon-size-base),
  ),
  $icon-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Backdrop

> Pick the layer behind a dialog or a drawer — a dark scrim, a translucent tint of the page, or nothing — from the markup.

## How it works

Every overlay that dims the page paints its native `::backdrop` from three tokens on `:root`: `--cui-backdrop-color`, `--cui-backdrop-opacity` and `--cui-backdrop-blur`. The colour and the opacity are mixed on the element, so either can be changed alone. The [dialog](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/dialog/) keeps the root defaults — a dark scrim that deepens in the dark colour scheme — and the [drawer](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/drawer/) tints the page instead.

The backdrop helpers set the colour and the opacity on the overlay element itself, so one instance can take the other look without touching `:root`:

| Class | Backdrop |
| --- | --- |
| `.backdrop-scrim` | Black at 50% (65% in the dark scheme) — the dialog's default |
| `.backdrop-translucent` | The page colour at 25% — the drawer's default |
| `.backdrop-none` | No backdrop; the overlay still takes the top layer and traps focus |

Put the class next to `.dialog` or `.drawer`. `::backdrop` inherits custom properties from the element that opened it, so nothing else is needed.

## Examples

### Translucent dialog

<dialog class="dialog backdrop-translucent" id="exampleBackdropTranslucent" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropTranslucentLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleBackdropTranslucentLabel">Translucent backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>The page behind stays readable through a light tint instead of a dark scrim.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog backdrop-translucent" id="exampleBackdropTranslucent" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropTranslucentLabel">
  …
</dialog>
```

### Dark drawer

```html
<button class="btn-solid theme-primary" type="button" data-coreui-toggle="drawer" data-coreui-target="#exampleBackdropScrim">
  Toggle drawer with a dark backdrop
</button>

<dialog class="drawer drawer-start backdrop-scrim" id="exampleBackdropScrim" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropScrimLabel">
  <div class="drawer-header">
    <h5 class="drawer-title" id="exampleBackdropScrimLabel">Dark backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="drawer" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="drawer-body">
    The scrim the dialog uses, on a drawer.
  </div>
</dialog>
```

### No backdrop

`.backdrop-none` hides the layer while the overlay keeps its modal behaviour — the top layer, the focus trap, the dismiss on <kbd>Esc</kbd>. It is the same effect the component-level `.dialog-no-backdrop` and `.drawer-no-backdrop` provide.

<dialog class="dialog backdrop-none" id="exampleBackdropNone" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropNoneLabel">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleBackdropNoneLabel">No backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>Nothing dims the page, but it is still modal.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog backdrop-none" id="exampleBackdropNone" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropNoneLabel">
  …
</dialog>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

The three tokens live on `:root`, so a change there reaches every overlay; a change on one overlay reaches only its own backdrop.

```scss
--cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-black),
--cui-backdrop-opacity: 50%,
--cui-backdrop-blur: 8px,
```

The helpers are nothing more than the first two tokens set on the element:

```scss
.backdrop-scrim {
  --cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-black);
  --cui-backdrop-opacity: 50%;
}

@if $enable-dark-mode {
  @include color-mode(dark) {
    .backdrop-scrim {
      --cui-backdrop-opacity: 65%;
    }
  }
}

.backdrop-translucent {
  --cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-bg-body);
  --cui-backdrop-opacity: 25%;
}

.backdrop-none::backdrop {
  display: none;
}
```

A look the helpers do not cover is a matter of the same tokens — a brand-coloured tint with no blur:

<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleBackdropCustom" aria-labelledby="exampleBackdropCustomLabel" style="--cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-primary-base); --cui-backdrop-opacity: 35%; --cui-backdrop-blur: 0;">
  <div class="dialog-header">
    <h5 class="dialog-title" id="exampleBackdropCustomLabel">Custom backdrop</h5>
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-coreui-dismiss="dialog" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="dialog-body">
    <p>A primary tint at 35%, no blur.</p>
  </div>
</dialog>

```html
<dialog class="dialog" id="exampleBackdropCustom" style="--cui-backdrop-color: var(--cui-primary-base); --cui-backdrop-opacity: 35%; --cui-backdrop-blur: 0;">
  …
</dialog>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Clearfix

> Quickly and easily clear floated content within a container by adding a clearfix utility.

Easily clear `float`s by adding `.clearfix` **to the parent element**. Can also be used as a mixin.

Use in HTML:

```html
<div class="clearfix">...</div>
```

The mixin source code:

```scss
@mixin clearfix() {
  &::after {
    display: block;
    clear: both;
    content: "";
  }
}
```

Use the mixin in SCSS:

```scss
.element {
  @include clearfix;
}
```

The following example shows how the clearfix can be used. Without the clearfix the wrapping div would not span around the buttons which would cause a broken layout.

```html
<div class="bg-info clearfix">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary float-start">Example Button floated left</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary float-end">Example Button floated right</button>
</div>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Color & Background

> Set a background color with contrasting foreground color.

## Overview

_Added in 4.2.6._

Color and background helpers combine the power of our [`.text-*` utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/colors/) and [`.bg-*` utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/background/) in one class. Using our Sass `color-contrast()` function, we automatically determine a contrasting `color` for a particular `background-color`.

> **Heads up!** There's currently no support for a CSS-native `color-contrast` function, so we use our own via Sass. This means that customizing our theme colors via CSS variables may cause color contrast issues with these utilities.

## With components

Use them in place of combined `.text-*` and `.bg-*` classes, like on [badges](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/badge/):

```html
<span class="badge text-bg-primary">Primary</span>
<span class="badge text-bg-info">Info</span>
```

Or on [cards](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/components/card/#background-and-color):

```html
<div class="card text-bg-primary border-primary mb-4" style="max-width: 18rem;">
  <div class="card-header">Header</div>
  <div class="card-body">
    <p class="card-text">Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's content.</p>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="card text-bg-info border-info mb-4" style="max-width: 18rem;">
  <div class="card-header">Header</div>
  <div class="card-body">
    <p class="card-text">Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's content.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Focus Ring

> Utility classes that allows you to add and modify custom focus ring styles to elements and components.

The `.focus-ring` helper replaces the browser's default focus indicator with one of our own on `:focus-visible`. It is an `outline`, sized and coloured from a series of CSS variables inherited from the `:root` level, so it can be modified for any element or component.

## Example

Tab to the link below to see the focus ring. Clicking it will not show one — the helper styles `:focus-visible`, which the browser reserves for keyboard focus.

```html
<a href="#" class="d-inline-flex focus-ring py-1 px-3 text-decoration-none border rounded-2">
  Custom focus ring
</a>
```

## Variants

Pair `.focus-ring` with a [theme color](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/customize/theme/) class to recolour the ring. The helper reads `--cui-theme-focus-ring`, which every `.theme-*` class sets, so the ring follows the element's theme rather than needing its own class.

Use this when the element already carries a theme; reach for the `.focus-ring-*` utilities below when you only want to change the ring.

## Customizing

Modify the styling of a focus ring with our CSS variables, Sass variables, utilities, or custom styles.

### CSS variables

Modify the `--cui-focus-ring-*` CSS variables as needed to change the default appearance.

```html
<a href="#" class="d-inline-flex focus-ring py-1 px-3 text-decoration-none border rounded-2" style="--cui-focus-ring-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cui-success-base) 25%, transparent)">
  Green focus ring
</a>
```

`.focus-ring` sets styles via global CSS variables that can be overridden on any parent element, as shown above. These variables are generated from their Sass variable counterparts.

```scss
--cui-focus-ring-width: .25rem,
--cui-focus-ring-opacity: .25,
--cui-focus-ring-offset: 0,
--cui-focus-ring-color: var(--cui-primary-focus-ring),
--cui-focus-ring: var(--cui-focus-ring-width) solid var(--cui-focus-ring-color),
```

The ring is an `outline`, so it is never clipped by an ancestor's `overflow` —
it stays visible inside scroll containers, where a `box-shadow` ring was cut off.
Push it away from the element with `--cui-focus-ring-offset`, which defaults to
`0`:

```html
<a href="#" class="d-inline-flex focus-ring py-1 px-3 text-decoration-none border rounded-2" style="--cui-focus-ring-offset: 4px">
  Offset focus ring
</a>
```

### Utilities API

In addition to `.focus-ring`, we have several `.focus-ring-*` utilities to modify the helper class defaults. Modify the color with any of our [theme colors](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/customize/color/#theme-colors). Note that the light and dark variants may not be visible on all background colors given current color mode support.

Focus ring utilities are declared in our utilities API in `scss/_utilities.scss`. [Learn how to use the utilities API.](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/api/#using-the-api)

```scss
"focus-ring": (
  property: (--cui-focus-ring-color: null),
  // Writes the global :root token, so it stays inheriting — see
  // generate-utility-at-properties().
  at-property: false,
  class: focus-ring,
  values: theme-color-refs("focus-ring")
),
```

# Bootstrap 6 Hover Lift

> Lift an element and add a shadow on hover or focus for a subtle sense of depth.

## How it works

Add `.hover-lift` to any element to translate it upward and deepen its `box-shadow` on `:hover` and `:focus-visible`. It is a lightweight way to signal that a card, tile or other surface is interactive.

The effect sets only `transform` and `box-shadow`, so it composes with anything — cards, buttons, list items, plain containers — and it honours [`prefers-reduced-motion`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/accessibility/reduced-motion/): a reader who asks for reduced motion still gets the raised shadow and offset, without the animation.

## Example

Hover the card below, or tab to it. It is an `<a>` rather than a `<div>` so the `:focus-visible` half of the helper is reachable from the keyboard.

```html
<a href="#" class="card hover-lift text-decoration-none" style="width: 18rem;">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Hover me</h5>
    <p class="card-text mb-0">Hover or focus this card to see it lift with a shadow.</p>
  </div>
</a>
```

Because it only touches those two properties, it works just as well on a control:

```html
<button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-primary hover-lift">Lift on hover</button>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

CoreUI for Bootstrap's hover lift uses local CSS variables on `.hover-lift` for enhanced real-time customization.

```scss
$hover-lift-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-hover-lift-transition-duration: .2s,
    --cui-hover-lift-transition-timing: ease,
    --cui-hover-lift-transform: translateY(-.25rem),
    --cui-hover-lift-box-shadow: var(--cui-box-shadow-lg),
  ),
  $hover-lift-tokens
);
```

Override them to tune the distance, the shadow or the timing — a larger rise with a snappier transition:

```html
<a href="#" class="card hover-lift text-decoration-none" style="--cui-hover-lift-transform: translateY(-.5rem); --cui-hover-lift-transition-duration: .1s; width: 18rem;">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Bigger lift</h5>
    <p class="card-text mb-0">Customized transform and duration.</p>
  </div>
</a>
```

# Icon link

> Quickly create stylized hyperlinks with CoreUI Icons or other icons.

The icon link helper component modifies our default link styles to enhance their appearance and quickly align any pairing of icon and text. Alignment is set via inline flexbox styling and a default `gap` value. We stylize the underline with a custom offset and color. Icons are automatically sized to `1em` to best match their associated text's `font-size`.

Icon links assume [CoreUI Icons](https://coreui.io/icons/) are being used, but you can use any icon or image you like.

When icons are purely decorative, they should be hidden from assistive technologies using `aria-hidden="true"`, as we've done in our examples. For icons that convey meaning, provide an appropriate text alternative by adding `role="img"` and an appropriate `aria-label="..."` to the SVGs.

## Example

Take a regular `<a>` element, add `.icon-link`, and insert an icon on either the left or right of your link text. The icon is automatically sized, placed, and colored.

```html
<a class="icon-link" href="#">
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">  
    <path d="M8.186 1.113a.5.5 0 0 0-.372 0L1.846 3.5l2.404.961L10.404 2l-2.218-.887zm3.564 1.426L5.596 5 8 5.961 14.154 3.5l-2.404-.961zm3.25 1.7-6.5 2.6v7.922l6.5-2.6V4.24zM7.5 14.762V6.838L1 4.239v7.923l6.5 2.6zM7.443.184a1.5 1.5 0 0 1 1.114 0l7.129 2.852A.5.5 0 0 1 16 3.5v8.662a1 1 0 0 1-.629.928l-7.185 2.874a.5.5 0 0 1-.372 0L.63 13.09a1 1 0 0 1-.63-.928V3.5a.5.5 0 0 1 .314-.464L7.443.184z"/>
  </svg>
  Icon link
</a>
```

```html
<a class="icon-link" href="#">
  Icon link
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">  
    <path d="M1 8a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5h11.793l-3.147-3.146a.5.5 0 0 1 .708-.708l4 4a.5.5 0 0 1 0 .708l-4 4a.5.5 0 0 1-.708-.708L13.293 8.5H1.5A.5.5 0 0 1 1 8z"/>
  </svg>
</a>
```

## Style on hover

Add `.icon-link-hover` to move the icon to the right on hover.

```html
<a class="icon-link icon-link-hover" href="#">
  Icon link
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M1 8a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5h11.793l-3.147-3.146a.5.5 0 0 1 .708-.708l4 4a.5.5 0 0 1 0 .708l-4 4a.5.5 0 0 1-.708-.708L13.293 8.5H1.5A.5.5 0 0 1 1 8z"/>
  </svg>
</a>
```

## Customizing

Modify the styling of an icon link with our link CSS variables, Sass variables, utilities, or custom styles.

### CSS variables

Modify the `--cui-link-*` and `--cui-icon-link-*` CSS variables as needed to change the default appearance.

```scss
$icon-link-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-icon-link-gap: .375rem,
    --cui-icon-link-underline-offset: .25em,
    --cui-icon-link-icon-size: 1em,
    --cui-icon-link-icon-transition: .2s ease-in-out transform,
    --cui-icon-link-icon-transform: translate3d(.25em, 0, 0),
  ),
  $icon-link-tokens
);
```

Customize the hover `transform` by overriding the `--cui-icon-link-transform` CSS variable:

```html
<a class="icon-link icon-link-hover" style="--cui-icon-link-transform: translate3d(0, -.125rem, 0);" href="#">
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M4 1.5H3a2 2 0 0 0-2 2V14a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h10a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V3.5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2h-1v1h1a1 1 0 0 1 1 1V14a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H3a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V3.5a1 1 0 0 1 1-1h1v-1z"/>
    <path d="M9.5 1a.5.5 0 0 1 .5.5v1a.5.5 0 0 1-.5.5h-3a.5.5 0 0 1-.5-.5v-1a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5h3zm-3-1A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5 1.5v1A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 6.5 4h3A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 11 2.5v-1A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 9.5 0h-3z"/>
  </svg>
  Icon link
</a>
```

Customize the color by overriding the `--cui-link-*` CSS variable:

```html
<a class="icon-link icon-link-hover" style="--cui-link-color: var(--cui-success-base);" href="#">
  Icon link
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M1 8a.5.5 0 0 1 .5-.5h11.793l-3.147-3.146a.5.5 0 0 1 .708-.708l4 4a.5.5 0 0 1 0 .708l-4 4a.5.5 0 0 1-.708-.708L13.293 8.5H1.5A.5.5 0 0 1 1 8z"/>
  </svg>
</a>
```

### Sass utilities API

Modify icon links with any of [our link utilities](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/link/) for modifying underline color and offset.

```html
<a class="icon-link icon-link-hover theme-success underline-success underline-30" href="#">
  Icon link
  <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">

  </svg>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Position

> Use these helpers for quickly configuring the position of an element.

## Fixed top

Position an element at the top of the viewport, from edge to edge. Be sure you understand the ramifications of fixed position in your project; you may need to add additional CSS.

```html
<div class="fixed-top">...</div>
```

## Fixed bottom

Position an element at the bottom of the viewport, from edge to edge. Be sure you understand the ramifications of fixed position in your project; you may need to add additional CSS.

```html
<div class="fixed-bottom">...</div>
```

## Sticky top

Position an element at the top of the viewport, from edge to edge, but only after you scroll past it.

```html
<div class="sticky-top">...</div>
```

## Responsive sticky top

Responsive variations also exist for `.sticky-top` utility.

```html
<div class="sticky-sm-top">Stick to the top on viewports sized SM (small) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-md-top">Stick to the top on viewports sized MD (medium) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-lg-top">Stick to the top on viewports sized LG (large) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-xl-top">Stick to the top on viewports sized XL (extra-large) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-2xl-top">Stick to the top on viewports sized XXL (extra-extra-large) or wider</div>
```

## Sticky bottom

Position an element at the bottom of the viewport, from edge to edge, but only after you scroll past it.

```html
<div class="sticky-bottom">...</div>
```

## Responsive sticky bottom

Responsive variations also exist for `.sticky-bottom` utility.

```html
<div class="sticky-sm-bottom">Stick to the bottom on viewports sized SM (small) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-md-bottom">Stick to the bottom on viewports sized MD (medium) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-lg-bottom">Stick to the bottom on viewports sized LG (large) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-xl-bottom">Stick to the bottom on viewports sized XL (extra-large) or wider</div>
<div class="sticky-2xl-bottom">Stick to the bottom on viewports sized XXL (extra-extra-large) or wider</div>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Stacks

> Shorthand helpers that build on top of our flexbox utilities to make component layout faster and easier than ever.

Stacks offer a shortcut for applying a number of flexbox properties to quickly and easily create layouts in CoreUI. All credit for the concept and implementation goes to the open source [Pylon project](https://almonk.github.io/pylon/).

## Vertical

Use `.vstack` to create vertical layouts. Stacked items are full-width by default. Use `.gap-*` utilities to add space between items.

```html
<div class="vstack gap-4">
  <div class="p-3">First item</div>
  <div class="p-3">Second item</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
</div>
```

## Horizontal

Use `.hstack` for horizontal layouts. Stacked items are vertically centered by default and only take up their necessary width. Use `.gap-*` utilities to add space between items.

```html
<div class="hstack gap-4">
  <div class="p-3">First item</div>
  <div class="p-3">Second item</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
</div>
```

Using horizontal margin utilities like `.ms-auto` as spacers:

```html
<div class="hstack gap-4">
  <div class="p-3">First item</div>
  <div class="p-3 ms-auto">Second item</div>
  <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
</div>
```

And with [vertical rules](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/helpers/vertical-rule/):

```html
<div class="hstack gap-4">
  <div class="p-3">First item</div>
  <div class="p-3 ms-auto">Second item</div>
  <div class="vr"></div>
  <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
</div>
```

## Responsive

`.hstack{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}` and `.vstack{-sm|-md|-lg|-xl|-2xl}` switch direction at a breakpoint — a stack that reads as a row on a wide layout and as a column on a narrow one, without writing the flex utilities twice.

The breakpoint is measured on the **container**, not the viewport, so mark an ancestor with `.stack-container` (or the [`.contains-inline`](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/utilities/container-queries/) utility) for the query to have something to read. Without it the direction never switches.

```html
<div class="stack-container">
  <div class="hstack-md vstack gap-4">
    <div class="p-3">First item</div>
    <div class="p-3">Second item</div>
    <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="stack-container">
  <div class="hstack-md vstack gap-4">
    <div class="p-3">First item</div>
    <div class="p-3">Second item</div>
    <div class="p-3">Third item</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Because the width comes from the container, the same markup can be a column in a sidebar and a row in the main content area of the same page.

## Examples

Use `.vstack` to stack buttons and other elements:

```html
<div class="vstack gap-3 col-md-5 mx-auto">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary">Save changes</button>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-secondary">Cancel</button>
</div>
```

Create an inline form with `.hstack`:

```html
<div class="hstack gap-4">
  <input class="form-control me-auto" type="text" placeholder="Add your item here..." aria-label="Add your item here...">
  <button type="button" class="btn-solid theme-secondary">Submit</button>
  <div class="vr"></div>
  <button type="button" class="btn-outline theme-danger">Reset</button>
</div>
```

## Customizing

### Sass loops

`.hstack` and `.vstack` are one rule each; the responsive variants come from a loop over `$breakpoints`, so a breakpoint you add to that map gets its own `.hstack-{breakpoint}` and `.vstack-{breakpoint}` classes. The variants measure the nearest query container, not the viewport — `.stack-container` is what gives them something to measure.

```scss
.stack-container {
  @include set-container();
}

#{$stack-selectors} {
  display: flex;
  align-self: stretch;
}

// The responsive variants read the width of the nearest query container — put
// `.stack-container` (or the `.contains-inline` utility) on an ancestor, or the
// query has nothing to measure and the direction never switches.
@each $breakpoint in map.keys($breakpoints) {
  $infix: breakpoint-infix($breakpoint, $breakpoints);

  .hstack#{$infix} {
    @include container-breakpoint-up($breakpoint) {
      flex-direction: row;
      align-items: center;
    }
  }

  .vstack#{$infix} {
    @include container-breakpoint-up($breakpoint) {
      flex: 1 1 auto;
      flex-direction: column;
      align-items: stretch;
    }
  }
}
```

# Bootstrap 6 Stretched Link

> Make any HTML element or CoreUI for Bootstrap component clickable by "stretching" a nested link via CSS.

Add `.stretched-link` to a link to make its [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block) clickable via a `::after` pseudo element. In most cases, this means that an element with `position: relative;` that contains a link with the `.stretched-link` class is clickable. Please note given [how CSS `position` works](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/visuren.html#propdef-position), `.stretched-link` cannot be mixed with most table elements.

Cards have `position: relative` by default in CoreUI, so in this case you can safely add the `.stretched-link` class to a link in the card without any other HTML changes.

Multiple links and tap targets are not recommended with stretched links. However, some `position` and `z-index` styles can help should this be required.

```html
<div class="card" style="width: 18rem;">
  <svg class="docs-placeholder-img card-img-top" width="100%" height="180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Card image cap" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Card image cap</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em">false</text></svg>
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Card with stretched link</h5>
    <p class="card-text">Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's content.</p>
    <a href="#" class="btn-solid theme-primary stretched-link">Go somewhere</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

Most custom components do not have `position: relative` by default, so we need to add the `.position-relative` here to prevent the link from stretching outside the parent element.

```html
<div class="d-flex position-relative">
  <svg class="docs-placeholder-img flex-shrink-0 me-4" width="144" height="144" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Generic placeholder image" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Generic placeholder image</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em">false</text></svg>
  <div>
    <h5 class="mt-0">Custom component with stretched link</h5>
    <p>This is some placeholder content for the custom component. It is intended to mimic what some real-world content would look like, and we're using it here to give the component a bit of body and size.</p>
    <a href="#" class="stretched-link">Go somewhere</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="row g-0 bg-4 position-relative">
  <div class="col-md-6 mb-md-0 p-md-5">
    <svg class="docs-placeholder-img w-100" width="100%" height="200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Generic placeholder image" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Generic placeholder image</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em">false</text></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="col-md-6 p-5 ps-md-0">
    <h5 class="mt-0">Columns with stretched link</h5>
    <p>Another instance of placeholder content for this other custom component. It is intended to mimic what some real-world content would look like, and we're using it here to give the component a bit of body and size.</p>
    <a href="#" class="stretched-link">Go somewhere</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Identifying the containing block

If the stretched link doesn't seem to work, the [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block#Identifying_the_containing_block) will probably be the cause. The following CSS properties will make an element the containing block:

- A `position` value other than `static`
- A `transform` or `perspective` value other than `none`
- A `will-change` value of `transform` or `perspective`
- A `filter` value other than `none` or a `will-change` value of `filter` (only works on Firefox)

```html
<div class="card" style="width: 18rem;">
  <svg class="docs-placeholder-img card-img-top" width="100%" height="180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Card image cap" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" focusable="false"><title>Card image cap</title><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#868e96"></rect><text x="50%" y="50%" fill="#dee2e6" dy=".3em">false</text></svg>
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Card with stretched links</h5>
    <p class="card-text">Some quick example text to build on the card title and make up the bulk of the card's content.</p>
    <p class="card-text">
      <a href="#" class="stretched-link fg-danger" style="position: relative;">Stretched link will not work here, because <code>position: relative</code> is added to the link</a>
    </p>
    <p class="card-text bg-4" style="transform: rotate(0);">
      This <a href="#" class="fg-warning stretched-link">stretched link</a> will only be spread over the <code>p</code>-tag, because a transform is applied to it.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Modify the `--cui-stretched-link-z-index` CSS variable to lift the generated overlay above other positioned content inside the same containing block.

```scss
$stretched-link-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-stretched-link-z-index: 1,
  ),
  $stretched-link-tokens
);
```

### Sass variables

This one picks which pseudo-element the helper stretches. It is written into the
selector itself, and a selector cannot read a custom property, so unlike the
helper's other customization it stays Sass and has no CSS variable counterpart.

```scss
$stretched-link-pseudo-element: after !default;
```

# Bootstrap 6 Text Truncation

> Truncate long strings of text with an ellipsis.

For longer content, you can add a `.text-truncate` class to truncate the text with an ellipsis. **Requires `display: inline-block` or `display: block`.**

```html
<!-- Block level -->
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-2 text-truncate">
    This text is quite long, and will be truncated once displayed.
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Inline level -->
<span class="d-inline-block text-truncate" style="max-width: 150px;">
  This text is quite long, and will be truncated once displayed.
</span>
```

# Bootstrap 6 Vertical Rule

> Use the custom vertical rule helper to create vertical dividers like the `<hr>` element.

## How it works

Vertical rules are inspired by the `<hr />` element, allowing you to create vertical dividers in common layouts. They're styled just like `<hr />` elements:

- They're `1px` wide
- They have `min-height` of `1em`
- Their color is set via `currentColor` and `opacity`

Customize them with additional styles as needed.

## Example

```html
<div class="vr"></div>
```

Vertical rules scale their height in flex layouts:

```html
<div class="d-flex" style="height: 200px;">
  <div class="vr"></div>
</div>
```

## With stacks

They can also be used in [stacks](https://coreui.io/bootstrap/docs/helpers/stacks/):

```html
<div class="hstack gap-4">
  <div class="bg-4 border">First item</div>
  <div class="bg-4 border ms-auto">Second item</div>
  <div class="vr"></div>
  <div class="bg-4 border">Third item</div>
</div>
```

## Customizing

### CSS variables

Modify the `--cui-vr-*` CSS variables on any `.vr` to change its width or color.

```scss
$vr-tokens: defaults(
  (
    --cui-vr-border-width: var(--cui-border-width),
    --cui-vr-color: var(--cui-border-color),
  ),
  $vr-tokens
);
```

# Bootstrap 6 Visually Hidden

> Use these helpers to visually hide elements but keep them accessible to assistive technologies.

Visually hide an element while still allowing it to be exposed to assistive technologies (such as screen readers) with `.visually-hidden`. Use `.visually-hidden-focusable` to visually hide an element by default, but to display it when it's focused (e.g. by a keyboard-only user). `.visually-hidden-focusable` can also be applied to a container–thanks to `:focus-within`, the container will be displayed when any child element of the container receives focus.

```html
<h2 class="visually-hidden">Title for screen readers</h2>
<a class="visually-hidden-focusable" href="#content">Skip to main content</a>
<div class="visually-hidden-focusable">A container with a <a href="#">focusable element</a>.</div>
```

Both `visually-hidden` and `visually-hidden-focusable` can also be used as mixins.

```scss
// Usage as a mixin

.visually-hidden-title {
  @include visually-hidden;
}

.skip-navigation {
  @include visually-hidden-focusable;
}
```
